recipe.description: Line list: Splatalogue (CDMS+JPL) via astroquery for the rest ranges 164.4-179.8, 251.2-268.1, 341.9-357.3 GHz, curated species + hydrogen RRLs from the Rydberg formula
Continuum survey of all 2D pbcor images: peaks >5 sigma, positions, rms (MAD)
Spectra extraction from all pbcor cubes: N, S nominal pixels, beam aperture (diameter = geometric-mean FWHM), r=2.5" and r=8" flux densities, cube-peak pixel
Systemic velocity from HCN/HCO+ first moments and half-maximum midpoints
Blind boxcar scan (300 and 100 km/s) at 5 sigma, forced photometry of all catalogue lines, overview and zoom plots; identification at |dv|<60 km/s with plausibility tiers
Moment maps (core |v|<350, blue -400..-150, red 150..400 km/s, mom1 3-sigma clipped), peak finding (>8 sigma, >=1 beam apart) to define regions

Region spectra (peak pixel within 0.6" of the nominal position, beam aperture), 1- and 2-Gaussian fits (scipy curve_fit, constant baseline, noise from line-free channels, lag-1 correlation inflation), integrated intensity |v|<350 with empirical box-sum noise, Tb (Rayleigh-Jeans)
Weak lines by matched filter with same-region HCN/HCO+ templates (limits 3 sigma); CS/H2CS/29SiO NNLS blend model; H13CN on CO wing
Wing fluxes; clean-mask coverage
Report assembly

Round 2: wing reality tests, unified line table with template-matched integrated intensities and error budgets, spatial scatter tests, region velocities, continuum catalogue/common beam/alpha, cross-OUS check

Q4: H13CN 4-3 on the CO 3-2 wing (template + wing-model profile likelihood), HCN v2=1f 3-2/4-3 limits, 0.25" profile/absorption/T_b diagnostics, RADEX regime table (thin vs thick, A, 12/13) and opacity bounds
recipe.software: python3 (numpy, scipy, astropy, pandas), RADEX LVG + LAMDA

recipe.software: python3 (numpy, scipy, astropy, pandas), RADEX LVG + LAMDA

results.quantity: S-nucleus blue wing and Sblue blob (-450..-150 km/s): reality tests (dirty-beam/sidelobe, empirical noise, independent array)
results.target: S nucleus, Sblue
results.value: REAL (high confidence for existence; flux scale: image flux with +25%/-10% systematic per Q2r2, not a lower limit). (i) Empirical noise: beam-aperture blue-wing maps vs line-free pseudo-wing maps (-900..-600 and +450..+750 km/s, 13869-27738 pixels in 12" box excluding 1.5" around N,S): Xb4d HCO+ 3-2 Sblue peak 0.245 Jy/beam km/s = 13.8 sigma_MAD (sigma 0.0177), 0 of 13869 pseudo-wing pixels exceed it (max 0.083, 99.9th pct 0.066); HCN 0.346 = 19 sigma (0 of 27738); Xb4b (0.25") 8.1 and 12.6 sigma. S nucleus blue wing 0.156 (HCO+) / 0.074 (HCN) at 8.8 sigma / 4.0 sigma (Xb4d). (ii) Sidelobe model: Sblue spectrum fitted as a*S+b*N on core channels (|v|<150): predicts blue-wing flux 0.009 (HCO+) / 0.022 (HCN) vs observed 0.182+-0.022 / 0.139+-0.021 Jy/beam km/s in Xb4d; wing/core ratio Sblue 0.22 vs S 0.035-0.055 and N <=0.01 (a dirty-beam response is channel independent so would copy the S/N profile shape); even a 10% sidelobe copy of S gives only 0.014 (HCO+). (iii) Independent array: Xb4b convolved to the Xb4d beam (flux-conserving kernel) gives at the Sblue peak 0.154 (HCO+) and 0.215 (HCN) Jy/beam km/s (Xb4d: 0.245/0.346 at its own peak, 0.181/0.142 at nominal position) and at S 0.114/0.087 (Xb4d 0.156/0.074): the same structure appears in two arrays with different dirty beams, with pseudo-wing field sigma 0.020/0.019. (iv) Red-side check: 0.25" red wing at Sblue is -0.019+-0.012 (HCO+), i.e. the negative value flagged in round 1 is 1.6 sigma, not an artefact of structure. Caveat (Xb4b HCN only): the sidelobe model (0.012) is not distinguishable from the observed 0.016+-0.010 there. Beam-area scaling: a uniform source would be 12.1x brighter (Jy/beam) in the 0.94x0.74" beam than the 0.25" beam, so the 'ten times brighter at 0.94"' is what an extended/clumpy structure predicts, not evidence for an artefact. Wings lie outside the clean mask (0-7% of wing channels) but the two independent dirty beams agree
results.uncertainty: Sblue wing 0.18+-0.02 (stat) Jy/beam km/s HCO+ 3-2 Xb4d; +-5% flux scale; uncleaned => flux-scale +25%/-10% (Q2r2: cross-imaging spread + epsilon 0.73-0.95); the earlier 'missing-flux/sidelobe <=0.01-0.02' term is superseded

results.target: Sblue
results.value: HCO+ 3-2: area 3.1 arcsec2, intensity-weighted centroid 1.8" S of the S nucleus (offset -0.27" E, -1.76" N, PA 189 deg E of N), moment-based FWHM 2.3x0.7" (beam 0.93x0.74"), major axis PA 16 deg (nearly N-S, tilted toward SSW), integrated blue-wing flux ~0.58 Jy km/s; HCN 3-2: centroid 2.0" S (-0.11,-1.98; PA 183), 1.8x0.8", PA 14 deg, ~0.75 Jy km/s. It is aligned with the literature statement that the HCN/HCO+ outflow emanates from the southern nucleus (Michiyama+2018 abstract); Michiyama+2018 (arXiv:1810.04821, ApJ 868, 95; abstract read via arXiv API) states that the HCN/HCO+ outflow lines up with a diffuse molecular outflow from the southern nucleus and that N shows no detection of it; the outflow position angle was not found in the abstract and not read from the paper, so geometric consistency with the N-S elongation is qualitative

results.value: N I=0.929+-0.054(stat)+-0.000(baseline)+-0.093(cal) [17.3 sigma]; spatial test 14.0 sigma (field MAD 0.074, 0% of 1149 field pixels >= value); S I=1.333+-0.066(stat)+-0.074(baseline)+-0.133(cal) [13.5 sigma]; spatial test 18.5 sigma (field MAD 0.077, 0% of 1149 field pixels >= value). Spw overlap check: the Xb55 spw20/22 frequency overlap (rest 166.08-166.66 GHz) does not contain CH3OH (obs 163.52-163.57 GHz is in spw22 only) so no independent-spw confirmation exists, but the overlap region itself is line-free and the two spws agree (difference mean -0.03/-0.07 mJy/beam, std 1.0/1.1 mJy vs rms 1.45/1.56 per channel at N/S, i.e. no baseline offset between basebands). Blend integral J=1-3 (HCO+ template, +-900 km/s; scripts/s18): N 0.97+-0.07 (stat), S 1.38+-0.07; the integral depends on template width/window: N 0.38-0.97, S 0.47-1.38 (HCO+ and 150/220/300 km/s Gaussian templates) => ~30% systematic (sigma/mean 30%/33%), NOT included in the statistical error. J=4,5 not detected: 3-sigma J=4 <0.19 (N), <0.26 (S), J=5 <0.17, <0.18 Jy/beam km/s. The individual J=1,2,3 amplitudes are degenerate (J=1,2 are 20 km/s apart; the unconstrained fit gives J=1<0, i.e. unphysical) and the previous Boltzmann fit (Trot=5-6 K, chi2 20-29 for 3 dof) is WITHDRAWN. Replacement: one-scale fit of LTE and RADEX (e-ch3oh.dat, LVG, dV=200, n=1e3-1e7, N=1e14-1e16, Tkin 4-150 K) amplitude patterns to the spectrum (all 5 lines, common v/shape, chi2 ~ 285-300 for ~397 channels): LTE Tex <~10-12 K (2 sigma, best 8-10 K, range over templates 6-12 K, S 6-12 K); non-LTE: n<=1e4 cm-3 excluded at any Tkin (J=4,5 would be too strong), n=1e5: Tkin 15-40 K, n>=1e6: Tkin 6-15 K. Tkin and n are degenerate; robust statement: J>=4 E-methanol lines are weak relative to J=1-3 => low excitation (Tex<~12 K) in the 9" beam, model dependent; Tkin<~40 K for all allowed densities. Competing species at 165.05: CH3OCH3 27(1,26)-27(2,25) Eu=363 K and HC5N J=62-61 Eu=250 K are implausible.
results.uncertainty: statistical+baseline; blend-integral template/window systematic ~30% (not in stat error); cal 10%; N/S blended (beam response 0.7-0.76): apertures not independent

results.quantity: SO 5_6-4_5 (251.826 GHz; the only SO line in Band 6 data)
results.target: S (Xb4f, Xb4d, Xb4b)
results.value: UNCONFIRMED and BLENDED with CH3OH (round 4). Xb4f (5.7x3.5") S: I=0.281+-0.056(stat)+-0.000(baseline)+-0.014(cal) [5.0 sigma]; spatial test 2.8 sigma (field MAD 0.108, 1.6% of 3951 field pixels >= value); N 0.022+-0.079. Also Bridge-position 3.3 sigma, E2-position 3.2 sigma in Xb4f (all within ~one 5.7" beam of S: the same emission). Xb4d (0.94x0.74") S: I=0.019+-0.017, 3sigma UL 0.050; spatial test at Xb4d spatial test 3.1 sigma (field MAD 0.021, 0.029% of 10247 field pixels >= value); Xb4b S 0.022+-0.007. If the Xb4f emission were smooth over >6", beam dilution predicts only 0.010 Jy/beam km/s at 0.94" (below the 3 sigma Xb4d limit 0.050) so the non-detection at 1" and 0.25" does NOT demonstrate an artefact, it is non-diagnostic; conversely the single-beam significance falls from 5.0 sigma (spectral) to 2.8 sigma against the spatial scatter of the field (1.6% of field pixels as high, max 0.48). Status: tentative at best; no use for shock diagnostics beyond the 3 sigma limits. Round-4 blend test (scripts/s24_so_251826.py, Xb4f, template-shift vs HCO+ 3-2): feature centred at -28+-12 km/s from HCO+ (S) and -36+-15 (Bridge) if it is SO 251.8257 (2.3-2.4 sigma); if it is the CH3OH A-type 3(3)-2(2)...6(3)-6(2) ladder (251.74-251.92, Eu 64-99 K) the offset is +47+-12 (S) at Tex 10 K weights (3.9 sigma) or +23+-12 (1.9 sigma) at 25 K weights. Predicted CH3OH ladder integral relative to the CH3OH 254.015 line (LTE, S, I254=0.59 Jy/beam km/s): 0.10 Jy/beam km/s at Tex=10 K (~35% of the observed 0.28), 0.61 at 15 K (all of it), 2.8 at 25 K (excluded by the J>=4 blend limits); with the 254/blend ratio giving Tex 8-21 K the ladder can account for 0-100% of the 251.83 GHz feature. The SO flux is therefore an upper limit (<=0.28+-0.06 Jy/beam km/s at S) and SO is not available as a shock tracer; centroid slightly favours SO over a hot (Tex>=20 K) CH3OH ladder
results.uncertainty: stat+baseline in text; baseline-systematic 0.05-0.13 Jy/beam km/s at Xb4f (spectral vs spatial field scatter); cal 5%

results.quantity: Flux-scale, primary-beam and cross-OUS uncertainty budget
results.value: Flux-scale added in quadrature to every integrated intensity in out/s12_line_table.csv (sig_cal): 5% Band 6, 10% Band 5 and 7 (ALMA nominal; assumed). Primary-beam term (12 m Gaussian model, FWHM 33/22/16.6" at B5/B6/B7, phase centre RA 156.96346 Dec -43.90461): pb(E1)=0.86/0.71/0.54, pb(E2)=0.82 (B6)/0.70 (B7), pb(W)=0.72 (B6), 0.56 (B7), pb(Sblue)=0.84 (B6): 5% added for pb<0.9, 10% for pb<0.75 (the actual array type/pb model of the pbcor images was not available; for B7 E1/E2/W the 12 m assumption could be wrong). Cross-OUS test (Xb4b convolved to the Xb4d beam vs Xb4d, same definition): continuum peak ratio N 0.93, S 0.92, E1 0.96, E2 1.02; HCO+ 3-2 core moment-0 N 1.01, S 0.94, Bridge 0.92, E1 0.94, E2 1.02; HCN 3-2 N 0.98, S 0.95, Bridge 0.91, E1 0.74, E2 1.34 => bright regions agree to 2-8% (rms ~6%, consistent with 5% x sqrt2), faint ones to 25-35% (noise). Comparisons between OUS are image-plane only: the 0.25" array resolves out extended flux (r<8" continuum totals 24/35/51 mJy for Xb4b/Xb4d/Xb4f at a common 5.84x3.52" beam), so cross-OUS line ratios must be built from matched beams AND matched uv coverage
results.uncertainty: 5-10% scale (+5-10% pb for E1/E2/W/Sblue); cross-OUS scatter 6%

results.value: Xb4d (1"), fixed window 2783+-150 km/s, annulus-MAD noise 0.039 Jy/beam km/s; ratio CH3OH(254)/HCO+(3-2) as K km/s ratio (= Jy ratio x (265.1/251.7)^2; Jy ratio in brackets): Bridge 0.042+-0.012 [0.038]; W 0.073+-0.034 [0.066] (1.9 sigma only); E2 0.056+-0.030 [0.051]; N -0.004+-0.007 (3sigma UL 0.02); S 0.003+-0.008 (3sigma UL 0.03); E1 0.005+-0.017; Sblue 0.009+-0.039. Xb4f (6x3.7"): S 0.026+-0.004 [0.023], Bridge 0.016+-0.004, N -0.002+-0.004 (3sigma UL 0.011). So in a matched 1" beam the line is detected off-nucleus (Bridge, 9.9 sigma by matched filter, 3.4 sigma in a fixed-window moment-0) and not at the nuclei, consistent with team-a (p0001: 0.051 on Bridge and W clump, <0.013 at N, <0.017 at S; our N and S limits are weaker, 0.02/0.03, but our Bridge value 0.042+-0.012 agrees within 1 sigma). The Xb4f detection at the S pixel (5.5 sigma) is the 6" beam picking up the Bridge/W material (the Xb4f peak is 2" W of S, 0.81 Jy/beam km/s) because Xb4d S is <0.12 (3 sigma); Xb4b is not informative (0.22" beam resolves it out). CH3OH off-nuclear is therefore SUPPORTED at ~3-4 sigma in Xb4d and 7 sigma in the Xb4f map peak; the W clump and E2 are 1.7-1.9 sigma only and are not claimed. This test is only possible with the Band 6 254 GHz line; the 165 GHz J=1-3 blend (9" Xb55 beam, N-S separation 5") cannot separate nuclei from the Bridge

Ext is unconstrained (errors 0.5-2.4 on f, allowed negative). R_J (Jy ratio, zone-template R_3 N 0.558, S 0.375 included): 10" J=2-1: N 0.64+-0.12, S 0.46+-0.08; 10" J=4-3: N 0.46+-0.14, S 0.35+-0.14; 6.5" J=4-3: N 0.46+-0.07, S 0.35+-0.07 (template-shape +-0.01-0.02 only). S/N R ratio: 2-1 0.71+-0.17, 3-2 0.67 (template), 4-3 0.75+-0.17 (6.5"): S is lower than N at every J, but the N-S coefficient correlation is +0.4 to +0.85 (positive here because the signed model absorbs the common level). REPLICATION IS WEAK: Xb4b (0.25") convolved to the Xb4d beam, same aperture, window -450..-150: HCN 0.259+-0.060, HCO+ 0.302+-0.054, R=0.86+-0.25 (Xb4d same window 1.46+-0.38; difference 0.6+-0.45, 1.3 sigma); HCN in Xb4b is only 53% of Xb4d (2.5 sigma: HCN wing flux partly resolved out/extended) while HCO+ is 91%. Xb4f (5.7x3.5", r=2.5", blended with S core) R=0.83+-0.25 (HCN 0.39+-0.10, HCO+ 0.47+-0.10). So R_wing>R_core is robust in Xb4d (>3 sigma), R_wing>1 is 93% in Xb4d but is not confirmed by the independent array: adopt R_wing = 1.0-1.5 (best 1.2+-0.4 combining Xb4d and Xb4b-smoothed) i.e. HCN/HCO+ ~2 times the S-core 0.38-0.55 but not clearly >1. p0001's 1.8 'peak-pixel' bias: injection into real noise patches gives no bias (peak-pixel R median 1.40 for true 1.40, 1.39 for 1.39, 1.00 for 1.00; scatter 16-84% +-0.25-0.4), so the claim that the peak-pixel recipe is biased high is dropped; p0001's 1.8 differs from our aperture value mostly by window/aperture. Neighbouring lines: window of HCN 3-2 (263.55-263.78 GHz observed): HDO 2(2,0)-3(1,3) (Eup 157 K, logA -4.8), CH3OH 2(-2)-2(0)E2 (33 K, logA -8.9, negligible), c-C3H/l-C3H, CH3CHO (E>400 K); HCO+ window (265.21-265.43): 13CH3CN 15(7)-14(7) (453 K), SO2 28(4,24)-28(3,25) (416 K), CH3CHO (109-464 K): no strong candidate, but an HDO/c-C3H contribution to the HCN wing cannot be excluded without a second HCN-line check (spectra: out/s38_spectra.png/txt). Consequences (tentative): RADEX LVG (n 1e5-1e7, Tk 20-200 K, thin and tau~1): R_K(3-2) per unit abundance ratio A=N(HCN)/N(HCO+) is 0.08-0.15 (n=1e5), 0.15-0.45 (1e6), 0.46-1.0 (1e7); the core R_K=0.55 needs A=1.5-2.3 at n=1e6 (Tk 50-100 K) or 0.6-0.8 at n=1e7; the wing R_K=1.42 needs A=3.8-6 (n=1e6) or 1.4-2.1 (n=1e7, Tk>=50 K). Excitation and abundance are degenerate with 3-2 only. An abundance enhancement would be consistent with shock/high-T neutral-neutral HCN production (Nishimura+2024 outflow HCN/HCO+ enhancement) and contrasts with the absence of an enhancement at the AGN nucleus (Harada+2018). results.value: H13CN is NOT detected separably. Template = HCN 4-3 profile of the same aperture (integrated I(HCN)=10.9 N, 4.9 S, 6.6 Bridge Jy/beam km/s), amplitude alpha=I(H13CN)/I(HCN), CO wing fitted simultaneously (exp-linear, exp-quad, exp-cubic, power-law, Gaussian-at-CO; sky windows 341.80-342.20, 341.85-342.12, 341.80-342.28; template width x1 and x0.7; peak pixel and aperture); fits with chi2_red>1.3 (CO-core-contaminated windows) are rejected. 3-sigma profile-likelihood upper limits: N alpha<0.075-0.12 => HCN/H13CN(4-3) > 8.3 (conservative; 8-13 over models); S alpha<0.135-0.25 => > 4 (4-7); Bridge alpha<0.065-0.22 => > 4.5 (5-15). results.quantity: Optical-depth bounds from the H13CN limit: beam-averaged tau(HCN 4-3), allowed fraction of HCN 4-3 flux from an optically thick compact N core, and thin-LTE column limits
results.target: N nucleus, Xb47 beam aperture
results.value: (i) Beam-averaged: HCN/H13CN > L (same Tex/filling; ratio=(1-e^-tau)/(1-e^-tau/X)): L=8.3 => tau(HCN 4-3) < 3.8 (X=30), 6.4 (X=50), 12.8 (X=100); L=9.5 => 3.2/5.5/11.1; at S L=4 => tau < 8.6/14.4/28.8. (ii) THICK-CORE BAND (replaces the single 'marginal tension with f=0.36'): two-component model, core fraction of the HCN 3-2 flux of the 4.3x2.8" Xb47 beam aperture f3 = 0.34 (Xb4d total r<1.7" 17.0 Jy km/s) - 0.36 (Xb4b) for r<0.5" (core 5.8 Jy km/s; 0.46 of the Xb4f r<2.5" flux), scanned over f3=0.15-0.50. The 4-3 core fraction is f4=f3*L_c/L_tot with L=Tb(4-3)/Tb(3-2) (K km/s) measured at the common 6.5" beam (N, HCN: L_tot=0.50+-0.08 incl. 15% scale; HCO+ 0.64) and L_c from RADEX (thick 1.0, mid 0.9, thin 0.57): f4=0.40 (f3=0.20), 0.73 (f3=0.36), 1.0 (f3=0.50) for a thick core. The H13CN limit f4/r_c+(1-f4)/X <= 1/L (L=8.3-9.5) then bounds the core opacity: tau_core(HCN 4-3) < 7-14 (f3=0.2), 4-8 (f3=0.36), 3-6 (f3=0.5) for X=30-50 (thick core, L=9.5; X=100: 11-28); over the whole band (f3 0.15-0.5, L_tot +-15%, X 30-100, L 8.3-9.5, three L_c types) tau_max ranges 3-137 (median 10-19): a tau>=10 core is allowed in 52-79% of scenarios (X=30: 22%, X=50: 63%, X=100: 100%). So the thick-core reading is neither excluded nor required: it is disfavoured only if X<~50 and f3>~0.3, and the 4-3 core fraction is LARGER than the 3-2 fraction if the core is thick (f4>f3), which makes the bound tighter than in round 1, not looser. (iii) Optically thin LTE: W(H13CN 4-3)<1.0-1.2 K km/s => N(H13CN)<0.8-1.2e12 cm-2 (Tex 20-100 K), N(HCN)<2.3-3.7e13 (X=30), 3.8-6.2e13 (X=50), 7.7-12e13 (X=100) cm-2, beam-averaged over 4.3x2.8" (local columns higher by 1/filling). [Q42 note: the analytic bounds above assume equal Tex for HCN and H13CN. With non-LTE RADEX (own H13CN LAMDA file) the radiative trapping of the thick HCN lines raises its 4-3 excitation relative to the thin H13CN, so the predicted alpha=I(H13CN 4-3)/I(HCN 4-3) stays 0.016-0.035 for every Tk branch and X=32-63 even at tau(HCN 4-3)=11-19 (Q42, out/q42/branch_predictions.txt): the alpha<0.12 limit (and any 4-3 value of precision +-0.04) does NOT constrain the opacity or the Tk branch; use these tau limits only as equal-Tex statements]
results.uncertainty: tau limits follow alpha<0.105-0.12 (+-30%); f3 0.15-0.50 (band, not a single value); L_tot +-15%; core type L_c 0.57-1.0

results.quantity: What the N-core HCN/HCO+ 3-2 ratio R~1 means in RADEX: abundance (optically thin) vs opacity (both thick) interpretation, with predicted H13CN and J-ladder consequences
results.value: RADEX LVG (dv=150 km/s, Tkin 30/60/120 K, n 1e5/1e6/1e7, N(HCN) 1e13-3e17, A=N(HCN)/N(HCO+)=1,3,10; 269 cells): in the thin regime (tau(3-2)<1) R_K(3-2) ~ 0.25 A at n=1e6, 60 K, so the core needs A ~ 4 (thin) and the outer N/S gas R_K=0.4 needs A ~ 1.6: an HCN/HCO+ abundance enhancement of ~2.5 in the core. In the thick regime (tau(HCN 3-2) > 10, N(HCN)/dv >~ 5e16-3e17 cm-2 per 150 km/s; R_K ~ 0.9-1.07 for any A) R_K -> 1 by saturation. Discriminants: (1) HCN/H13CN(4-3): thin cells 30-100 (=X, median 43 at R_K~0.4), thick cells 1.3-10; the data give > 8 beam-averaged, which only bounds the core flux fraction (f<~0.3-0.5 for tau~10, see tau entry); no H13CN at a resolution that isolates the core exists in the data (H13CN 3-2 at 259.0 GHz and H13CO+ are not covered). (2) J-ladder R43/R32: thin 0.57 (0.53-0.79), mid 0.91, thick 1.00 at R_K(3-2)~1; for the outer gas R_K~0.4-0.7: thin 0.63, mid 0.73, thick 0.79 vs observed 0.75-0.78 (blended 6.5-10" zones, 10-35% flux-scale systematics): not discriminating. (3) The thick reading requires local N(HCN) >~ 5e16 cm-2 per 150 km/s: for X(HCN)=1e-8 (assumed) N(H2) >~ 5e24 cm-2, ~1e5 Msun/pc2, versus beam-averaged CO surface densities <= 5.5e3 Msun/pc2 at 55 pc (Brunetti+2021), i.e. filling <~ 0.05 (consistent with the filling >= 0.03 above). Verdict (revised in Q4r2): vib pumping excluded as the cause (<5%); abundance and opacity are NOT separable with these data; the broader-HCN-core hint is withdrawn (null test); the T_b ratio is satisfied by both branches (see the T_b entry). The A~4 quoted here is for n=1e6, 60 K; the finer grid in the T_b entry gives A=1-5.6 (median 1.8) for the thin branch.
results.uncertainty: RADEX 1-zone LVG grid, no beam-filling or abundance prior; spacing of the grid (half dex in N, 3 T, 3 n) => the A and N thresholds are +-0.3 dex

results.target: N core r<0.25" (Xb4b HCN 3-2 spw27, HCO+ 3-2 spw25, pbcor), annuli to 1", 190 apertures r<0.15" within 1.2"
results.value: Common circular 0.30" beam (both cubes convolved channel-wise; native beams differ 2% in minor axis): FWHM HCN 149.9, HCO+ 138.2 km/s, ratio 1.085+-0.015 (400 noise realisations on the observed spectrum) +-0.013 (pixel bootstrap); native beams 1.091+-0.018; centroid HCN-HCO+ -3.2+-0.8 (noise) km/s; non-parametric half-max width ratio 1.21+-0.07 (noisy, 1-2 channels). Outer annuli 0.25-0.5" and 0.5-1": 1.038+-0.010 / 1.038+-0.009; S core 1.00. NULL DISTRIBUTION from 190 beam-spaced r<0.15" apertures with peak S/N>=8 in both lines: width ratio median 1.036, 16-84% 0.980-1.087, 17% of apertures >= 1.084; centroid difference median +0.2, 16-84% -1.0..+1.5 km/s, but the 13 apertures within 0.3" of the N peak scatter by -5..+7.5 km/s and 1.00-1.14 in width. => the core value is ~1 sigma above the field median, and the real (profile-shape + spatial) scatter, ~5%, is 3x the noise error: the core broadening and the 4 km/s offset are NOT significant. A uniform +3.6% (HCN broader) over the region is the only robust difference (profile shape/different spatial weighting). SPATIAL-WEIGHTS MODEL (HCN cube := HCO+ cube x smoothed per-pixel R(x), i.e. identical local profiles, only different spatial weights; HCO+ gradient 119 km/s/arcsec = 36 km/s across the beam): predicts width ratio 1.003 and flat R(v) (0.95-0.96), centroid shift -0.1 km/s; because HCN is the more compact line, weights+gradient make HCN slightly NARROWER, not broader, so the reviewer-suggested explanation does not reproduce the observed ratio either; the observed R(v) (1.19, 1.04, 0.95, 1.25 in 100 km/s bins) carries the same information as the width ratio. Opacity expectation: Gaussian-profile broadening FWHM/FWHM_thin = 1.02 (tau 0.1), 1.18 (1), 1.49 (3), 1.96 (10), 2.33 (30); a differential 8% needs both lines thick with tau_HCN~2 tau_HCO+ (e.g. 30 vs 15), which the allowed RADEX cells give 0.7-1.56 (median 1.03 for thick, 1.0-1.14 thin): not discriminating. The core lines are also NARROWER (HCO+ 138, HCN 150 km/s) than the 0.25-1" annuli (153-164 km/s), the opposite of saturation broadening (tau=10 would broaden x2) unless the intrinsic dispersion is ~70 km/s.
results.uncertainty: width ratio +-0.015 stat, +-0.05 empirical (position scatter); centroid +-0.8 stat, +-5 km/s inner-aperture scatter

results.quantity: Brightness-temperature (T_b) discriminator for opacity: what the T_b(HCN 3-2)/T_b(HCO+ 3-2) ratio at 0.25" allows for the thin and thick branches at the N core and at S, with filling factor, Tex, N(HCN) and abundance ratio
results.target: N core (T_b 1.461 / 1.556 K, ratio 0.94) and S core (0.792 / 1.869 K, ratio 0.42), Xb4b 0.245x0.237" native beam, r<0.25"
results.value: RADEX grid (Tkin 20-150 K, n 1e4-1e8, N 1e13-1e19 per 150 km/s for each line independently => A=N(HCN)/N(HCO+)=0.2-30; 6925 cells), shared beam filling eta=T_b/T_R with eta<=1; cells accepted if T_R(HCN)/T_R(HCO+) is within +-15% of the observed ratio. Single-Tex slab: T_b ratio = (1-e^-tau_H)/(1-e^-tau_O) -> 1.00 for tau_O>=5 whatever tau_H (1.05 for tau_O=3, 1.14-1.15 for tau_O=2), so T_b ratio ~0.94-1 only needs the HCO+ line (and HCN) to be saturated OR the two thin columns to be tuned. N CORE: 29% of the grid is allowed (both-thick 89%, thin 3%, intermediate 3%, HCN-thick/HCO+-not 4%, HCO+-thick/HCN-thin 1%; fractions are grid weights, not probabilities). Both-thick (tau>=3): log N(HCN) per 150 km/s = 15.75-19.0 (median 17.75), filling eta 0.01-0.75 (median 0.07), Tex(HCO+) 7-150 K (median 30), A 0.3-18 unconstrained, Tex(HCN)/Tex(HCO+)=0.93-1.0. Both-thin (tau<1): log N 14.25-16.5 (median 15.0), eta 0.02-0.99 (median 0.33), Tex(HCO+) 13-440 K (median 45), A = 1.0-5.6 (median 1.8, close to the LTE value 1.6 expected from the A_ul ratio 1.7), Tex(HCN)/Tex(HCO+) 0.35-0.96 (subthermal HCN). So the thin branch does not need a coincidence: it needs A~1-6 (tuned within a factor 2.5 of the outer-gas A, see below); the thick branch needs no abundance change but N(HCN)>~6e15 cm-2 per 150 km/s and eta<=0.1-0.2 typically. S CORE: only 4.4% of the grid is allowed (T_b ratio 0.42 is a stronger constraint): in EVERY branch Tex(HCN)/Tex(HCO+) = 0.52-0.63 (median) or HCN thin with A<1: both-thick 47% of cells (log N 15.75-18, eta 0.01-0.81, TexH/TexO 0.53, A 0.3-3.2, 37% with A<1), both-thin 27% (log N(HCN) 14-16, A 0.32-3.2, 69% with A<1), HCO+-thick/HCN-thin-or-mid 4% (A<1 in 100%), HCN-thick/HCO+-not 6%. => at S HCN is either sub-thermally excited (Tex ~half of HCO+, 17 K median) or has an abundance/column below HCO+ (A<1) or both; A<1 holds in 69% of the thin and 37% of the thick allowed cells, and the T_b ratio alone does not decide which line is thicker at S (HCN-thick/HCO+-not and HCO+-thick/HCN-thin cells are both allowed); with the flat R(v), equal widths and T_cont<<T_b there, absorption is excluded. Thin-branch median A: N 1.8 (1.0-5.6) vs S 0.56 (0.32-3.2): an HCN/HCO+ column ratio higher by ~3 at the N core if both are thin (the same 'abundance enhancement' as in the line-ratio reading). Summary: T_b(HCN)~T_b(HCO+) at N is the signature of saturation OR a tuned A~2-6; it does not separate them without H13CN/H13CO+ at the core beam, but it does show that S (ratio 0.42, equal widths) cannot be explained by equal-Tex saturated lines.
results.uncertainty: T_b +-10% (flux scale) common to both lines, +-5% on the ratio; RADEX grid steps: 0.25 dex in N, 6 Tkin, 7 n; fractions are grid-weighted

results.quantity: Injection-recovery test of the H13CN 4-3 limit at the N nucleus (alpha=I(H13CN)/I(HCN)=0, 0.03, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3), coverage of the line by the band and by the fit window, and sensitivity in tau
results.target: N nucleus, Xb47 beam aperture (4.26x2.77"), spw20, same pipeline as s41
results.value: Coverage: H13CN line centre at 342.137 GHz; the band edge 342.396 GHz is at v=-224 km/s on the BLUE (high-frequency) side, so only 2.8% of an HCN-like profile (FWHM ~300 km/s) is beyond the band edge (the 'red half' is fully covered). The fit windows exclude the CO 3-2 core: 341.80-342.20 GHz covers v=-54..+293 km/s = 75% of the template flux (Fisher information sum(t^2/sigma^2): 33% from v<0, 67% from v>0); 341.85-342.12 GHz (v=+15..+249) 42% (all information from v>0); 341.80-342.28 GHz (v=-124..+293) 96% (CO-core contamination; only exp-quad/cubic fit with chi2_red<1.3). Fit of the v>0 half alone (341.80-342.14 GHz) gives alpha_3sigma<0.12 for all four wing families (best 0.04, 1-2 sigma), i.e. the limit is not set by the covered-but-contaminated blue part. Injection into the real spectrum: recovered exactly (bias <=0.01 main window; 0.02 mean, up to 0.07, at alpha=0.03 in the narrow window). Injection into simulated spectra (wing truth = alpha=0 fit of the real spectrum in 3 families + template + noise segments drawn from the line-free 340.7-341.6 GHz spectrum; 144 realisations per level and window recovered with 4 families): main window recovered-minus-injected = +0.013+-0.020 (0), +0.013+-0.031 (0.03), -0.003+-0.022 (0.1), +0.007+-0.027 (0.2), +0.009+-0.023 (0.3) (positive bias <=0.013 from the alpha>=0 boundary, <=0.011 for the matching wing family); false-limit rate (3-sigma UL < alpha_inj) 0/144 at every level (<2% at 95% CL, conservative); fraction with >=3-sigma detections 0, 26%, 85%, 95%, 100% at alpha_inj=0, 0.03, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3; median 3-sigma UL on pure wing+noise 0.06 (p84 0.10, max 0.12), 0.10, 0.16, 0.28, 0.38 for injected 0.03-0.3. The narrow window is poorer (bias up to +0.04+-0.05, detections 8-72%, UL on pure noise 0.12). The real-spectrum limits (0.075-0.12) are at the upper end of the null distribution (the real spectrum contains a 1-3 sigma excess, best alpha 0.04, 0.02-0.06) and the narrow-window best fit alpha=0.085-0.095 (a1 0.035-0.095) is MARGINAL (HCN/H13CN ~10-30), consistent with a faint H13CN or with a wing residual. SENSITIVITY: optically thin H13CN has alpha=1/X=0.010-0.033 (X=100-30), below the typical 3-sigma limit 0.06: the data cannot test thin 12C/13C=30-100; they are sensitive only to alpha>~0.06-0.1, i.e. tau(HCN 4-3) >~ 1.5-3 (X=30), 3-5.5 (X=50), 6-11 (X=100) (alpha=0.075-0.105 needs tau>=2.0-3.2, 3.8-5.5, 7.8-11.1 for X=30, 50, 100), or 12C/13C<~10-17.
results.uncertainty: alpha grid step 0.02 (limits are on this grid); noise per channel 2.2 mJy/beam (aperture, pbcor, 3.4 km/s channel); limits +-0.02

results.target: Xb55 (84x84 px, 100"), Xb4f (96x96, 67"), Xb47 (96x96, 51"); PB-uncorrected map = pbcor map x fitted Gaussian PB; circles about the N-S midpoint, r<=25" common to all three, larger circles for Xb55/Xb4f
results.value: Bowl = minimum annular mean of the pbcor 10" map beyond the zero crossing, relative to the peak (radius): HCO+ Xb55 -0.035 (21"), Xb4f -0.033 (16"), Xb47 -0.018 (12", followed by a positive ring +0.04 at 18-22"); HCN -0.038 (20"), -0.062 (14"), -0.059 (12"); continuum -0.036 (22"), -0.056 (16"), -0.032 (14"). Integral of the PB-uncorrected map to r<25" relative to its maximum cumulative value: HCO+ 0.86/0.93/1.00, HCN 0.81/0.84/1.00, continuum 0.89/0.84/1.00 (Xb55/Xb4f/Xb47); to the full Xb4f/Xb55 field 0.98/0.85 (HCO+), 0.95/0.80 (HCN). The map integral is NOT ~0: a cleaned image integrates to the clean-component flux (the zero-spacing identity holds for the dirty image and the residual only), so the bowl integral is not a missing-flux estimator and no absolute Xb4f loss follows from it. The bowl radius scales with wavelength (21:16:12" = 1.31:1:0.75 for lambda ratios 1.5:1:0.75, HCO+; HCN 1.43:1:0.86; continuum 1.38:1:0.88), i.e. the three sets are the same kind of array, but the bowl DEPTH is not ordered with wavelength (Band 5 is not shallower, Band 7 not deeper): no empirical support for R55>R4f>R47 from the bowls.
results.uncertainty: +-0.003-0.01 of peak (noise realisations); radii +-1.5" (annulus width); the Xb47 field (+-25") ends before its bowl closes and its outer ring is within the PB-corrected noise edge

results.quantity: Is an N vs S vs Bridge difference in the ladder excitation testable at the common 10" beam? Beam overlap and forward dilution of a nuclear contrast
results.target: N, S, Bridge apertures of the 10" ladder
results.value: NOT TESTABLE at 10" (this replaces "no significant difference"). N-S separation 5.1" (N-Bridge 2.4", S-Bridge 2.7"; 0.51 of the 10" beam FWHM): the other nucleus enters each 10" aperture with weight 0.48 (Bridge sees N 0.85, S 0.81), so the three apertures are largely the same gas. The 1.7" cores (Xb4d 3-2: HCN 63.6/20.3, HCO+ 85.1/53.7 K km/s at N/S) carry only 38%/14% (HCN, at N/at S) and 24%/16% (HCO+) of the 10" 3-2 flux; 56-72% is smooth gas shared by the apertures. Forward model (two cores + shared smooth component with the S-core ladder): an intrinsic N/S core ratio-of-ratios rho gives a 10" N/S of 1.08 (rho=1.5), 1.14 (2), 1.24 (3), 1.38 (5) for HCN and 1.06, 1.11, 1.20, 1.34 for HCO+; (with a smooth component at the geometric-mean ladder: 1.05, 1.09, 1.15, 1.22 and 1.04, 1.08, 1.12, 1.19). The measured 10" N/S ratio-of-ratios (same cubes, stat <2%) are 0.94/0.96 (T21/T32 HCN/HCO+) and 1.057/1.043 (T43/T32), i.e. all within 8%: this corresponds to rho<~1.5-2.1; a 2-sigma (32%) difference at 10" would need an intrinsic core contrast >=4 (HCN, S-like envelope) to >=13 (geometric-mean envelope). In RADEX terms, a factor 3 in Tk or 10 in n between the cores changes the 10" N/S by <=4% for a hot reference (Tk 180 K, n 1e4.75), by <=13% in T43/T32 (HCN 1.20, HCO+ 1.13 for Tk_S=Tk_N/3 at 50 K) for a cool reference: far below the 32%. At 6.5" (Xb47/Xb4f; weight 0.18) T43/T32 N/S = 1.155+-0.021 (HCN), 1.104+-0.009 (HCO+), larger than at 10" (1.057, 1.043) as dilution predicts, sign consistent with N being warmer/denser than S, but only an indication (same-cube ratio, stat 1-2%, recovery/pointing systematics ~5%). A deblend of the core ladders from the three 10" ratios is ill-conditioned (core N/S T21/T32 0.42 [0.09,0.70] HCN, 0.55 [0.17,1.01] HCO+; T43/T32 0.58 and 0.56 with errors >1) and is a consistency screen only. The posteriors of N, S, Bridge (P(Tk_N>Tk_S)=0.5 etc.) are the same because the data are the same; the ln B(separate/shared)=-6 to -7 of earlier rounds is an Occam penalty on near-identical data, not evidence of equal conditions, and contradicts neither the 1" N/S differences of team-b p0005 and team-a p0004/p0009 (HCN/HCO+ 3-2 N/S 1.5-2.0 at 1.7") nor the possibility of an intrinsic Tk or n contrast up to ~factor 3.

results.quantity: Disk (E1) vs centre excitation contrast tested on calibration-independent ratio-of-ratios and on the RADEX posteriors with common calibration
results.target: E1 vs N (centre); E2, W unconstrained
results.value: [Q38r2 DOWNGRADED] The E1-vs-centre Tk contrast below applies ONLY to the 10" blended ladder and is NOT confirmed with uv-complete matched 2.2" data. RADEX (s243, 1-0 X961 12m + 3-2 Q34 12m+7m, HCN and HCO+, K km/s at 2.2", 5% per line, shared 10%/15% band scales, Tk<=300 K): N Tk 40 K [14,158]; E1 Tk 178 K [79,251], P(Tk_E1<Tk_N)=0.17 (W: 0.11); P(n_E1<n_N)=0.51; log A = log N(HCN)/N(HCO+): N 0.70 [0.50,0.70], E1 0.30 [0.20,0.40], P(A_E1<A_N)=1.00. Bayes factors vs free (N vs E1): same-Tk&n (abundance/column free) +1.00, same-A (excitation only) -2.10, same-A&N -1.31, same-Tk +0.01, same-n +0.94, all-equal -14.2. So at matched resolution E1 differs from N in HCN/HCO+ abundance/opacity (R10 0.49 vs 0.84 is already present at J=1-0) and not by lower Tk; the 10" posterior P(Tk_E1<Tk_centre)=0.91-0.99 is withdrawn as evidence of cooler disk gas (only 4 data per position at 2.2", Tk weakly constrained: the statement is "no lower Tk at E1", not "E1 is warm"). Matched 2.2" r31=T(3-2)/T(1-0) clump/N: E1 HCN 0.80+-0.07, HCO+ 0.81+-0.03 (a 20% lower r31, not the factor 2 of 10" T43/T32); E2 0.34/0.40 and W 0.55/0.46 depend on the 12m-only 3-2 recovery (E2 HCO+ 1.9 K km/s 12m vs 4.7 comb) and are lower limits on r31 recovery. The 10" analysis follows (superseded in interpretation): Ratio-of-ratios E1/N (K km/s, 10") with errors that include stat, the E1 primary-beam term (max(0.3(1-PB), 0.5|1-A/B|); A/B differs by 34% at Xb47 HCN, 19% HCO+) and the Q12 recovery difference (band scales and the per-line terms are the same cubes at both positions and cancel): HCN T21/T32 1.46 (recovery-corrected 1.62), sigma_ln 0.074 -> 6.5 sigma; HCN T43/T32 0.48 (0.45), sigma 0.206 (stat 0.092, PB 0.18) -> 3.9 sigma; HCO+ T21/T32 1.18 (1.31), sigma 0.057 -> 4.8 sigma; HCO+ T43/T32 0.76 (0.71), sigma 0.111 (PB 0.10) -> 3.1 sigma. If the calibration did NOT cancel (independent bands per position, 7% per line) the same ratios would be 1.9, 2.5, 1.1, 1.3 sigma: the contrast rests on the calibration being common to both positions. E1 detection (stat, 10" |v|<350 km/s): HCN 2-1/3-2/4-3 93/50/11 sigma, HCO+ 161/146/62 sigma; the HCN 4-3 flux is a 11-sigma stat detection but carries the 34% PB/A-B systematic; W HCN 4-3 (2.7 sigma) is not used. Which survives: the HCN ratios (T21/T32 up 46%, T43/T32 down by a factor 2) survive any 10-15% band calibration; the HCO+ differences (18%, 24%) are 3-5 sigma only with the calibration common and recovery/PB as modelled. Posterior contrast with the same band-scale draws applied to E1 and N (analytic per-position terms, 256 Sobol draws): P(Tk_E1<Tk_centre)=0.94 for HCN+HCO+ (Tk_E1 32 K [20,50] vs 141 K [56,223]), 0.91 HCN alone, 0.64 HCO+ alone; flat-Tk-to-500 prior 0.99/0.99/0.69; band 15/10/15%: 0.92/0.89/0.63; with the 7% per-line term also common 1.00/0.95/0.76; no calibration error 0.98/0.96/0.66. P(n_E1>n_centre)=0.64/0.54/0.40: no density contrast. Interpretation: the contrast is carried by HCN (T43/T32 and T21/T32), not by HCO+ (P<0.8). Weak HCN 4-3 at E1 can be lower excitation (Tk<~55 K) or lower HCN/HCO+ abundance/opacity at 4-3, or a PB/recovery artefact at Xb47 (PB term 17%, A/B 0.66): these are not separated by the 10" data; the Q12 de-contamination also shows the disk T21/T32 excess against the nuclear complex vanishes for E1 (E1 Xb4d/Xb4f recovery 1.0). E2 and W remain unconstrained (below).

results.quantity: J=1-0 test of the single-zone ladder branches (thin vs thick HCN, equal filling) against Harada+2018 1.7" HCN/HCO+ 1-0 intensities, and reconciliation with team-a p0009
results.target: N and S (10" ladder posteriors, 1.7" compact component)
results.value: ASSUMPTION-LABELLED inputs: HCN/HCO+ 1-0 at 1.7" from Harada+2018 Table 13 (N 197.2/205.3, S 56.7/87.9 K km/s; R10 0.961 N, 0.645 S; independent Michiyama+2018 0.94+-0.13, 0.60+-0.08) as parsed by team-a; our Xb4d 3-2 at 1.7" (HCN/HCO+ 0.748 N, 0.378 S). The 1-0 beam (1.7") is not the 10" beam, so 1-0 enters (a) as a prediction check on the 10" posteriors, (b) as a filling-independent ratio datum (sigma 10% or 25%) and (c) in a separate compact-component fit. (a) The 10" posteriors predict HCN/HCO+ 1-0 = 0.75 [0.65,1.00] (N) and 0.71 [0.62,1.00] (S): both observed R10 lie inside; N sits at the saturation limit 1.0 of thick equal-Tex lines. (b) Adding R10 as a datum: at S the thin-HCN branch (tau_HCN32<1) falls from 0.26 to 0.04 (sigma 10%) / 0.06 (25%) and the thick branch rises 0.55 -> 0.87 / 0.81 (tau_HCN32 median 20 [6,82]); at N R10=0.96 is in the upper tail (ln Z ratio -2.45 for 10%, -1.03 for 25%), thin 0.22 -> 0.19 / 0.07, thick 0.60 -> 0.52 / 0.78, Tk 100 K [35,223]; so the 1-0 test disfavours the thin-HCN branch at S and is not decisive at N. (c) Compact 1.7" component (HCN, HCO+ 1-0 and 3-2; 4 data, 1-0 and 3-2 scales free to 10%): N thick (P(tau_HCN32>=5)=0.99, tau median 139 [18,713]) with A>3 (0.98; log A 0.8), Tk 22 [11,112] (P(Tk>50)=0.32 vs prior 0.42: Tk unconstrained); S thick (0.96), log A 0.3 [-0.1,0.4], Tk 28 [18,100]. A_N/A_S ~ 3: an HCN column or excitation difference at S, as in team-a p0009 (HCN column ~2x lower at S), whereas n and Tk differences are not required. Forcing the compact component and the 10" ladder to share one zone: N chi2 = 9.2 (10") + 14.0 (1.7") for 10 data (poor; two components needed), S 1.0 + 2.0 (acceptable; Tk 178 [79,223], log n 3.5, tau 51). Reconciliation: our 10" A~2.5 with equal eta is a beam-averaged value; it is not evidence of an HCN-rich thin envelope. With the 1-0 data the surviving branches are thick HCN (tau>~5) at S and thick at the N core; the thin-HCN branch (A 1-5.6 of p0007) survives only at the N-core level (0.07-0.19) and is not supported at S. A free HCN/HCO+ filling ratio q (0.1-10) relaxes this (thin mass 0.37 at N, 0.39 at S), so q and A are degenerate.
results.uncertainty: branch masses: S thin 0.04-0.06 (from 0.26), thick 0.81-0.87; N thin 0.07-0.19 (from 0.22), thick 0.52-0.78; compact A_N/A_S ~3; 1-0 inputs have 4-23% line differences between literature and our integrals

results.value: (a) MAPS (out/q11r2/s72a_maps.png): the blue E=HCN-0.534*HCO+ map has one compact maximum within 4" of S: +0.268 Jy/beam km/s = 5.7 sigma (pixel rms 0.047) at (E+0.15", N-1.80") from S (HCN blue peak 8.7 sigma at (0.0,-1.95), HCO+ 5.1 sigma at (-0.15,-1.95)); half-maximum area 1.1 arcsec2 (beam 0.87): a one-beam lobe, not a smooth skirt; 0/7302 non-bright field pixels (r<12") reach this value. The red mirror E map has no counterpart at Soutflow (-0.7 sigma); its largest feature within 4" of S is at (E+0.15", N+3.3") on the N-S bridge (E +0.167, 3.7 sigma; HCN 6.1, HCO+ 3.5 sigma) - a red-side HCN-rich feature, see the asymmetry entry. (b) RING at 1.85" from S (azimuth 0,45,...315 deg, E_blue sigma): -1.5, -0.4, +1.5, +1.8, +6.5, -0.0, -0.5, -0.3: only az=180 (the Soutflow direction, +0.274+-0.042) is significant; the other seven are within 1.8 sigma (mean of the other seven +0.004, their rms 0.047 vs stat 0.042). Ring at 1.85" from N: E_blue sigma -1.2,-0.2,+2.2,-0.7,-0.7,+0.2,-0.0,-0.7 (none significant); red mirror ring at N has +3.8 sigma at az180 (the bridge side, E +0.183+-0.048). Xb4b ring at S (sigma 0.075): the largest value is also az180 (HCN +0.215, HCO+ +0.204, E +0.106; others -0.125..+0.087). An azimuthally symmetric bowl/sidelobe/zero-spacing artefact of the nearby S core is therefore excluded; a sidelobe of the 0.9" beam would also appear mirrored in the red window, which is empty. (c) CLEAN MASK (out/q11r2/s72a_mask.png): the Xb4d HCN mask is non-zero only in -129..+149 km/s, HCO+ in -946..+170 but with 0 masked pixels in -405..-205 for both lines: the skirt lies entirely outside the clean mask at Soutflow and at every ring position, so mask truncation cannot create it, but the emission is UNCLEANED (residual-image flux, not deconvolved; the window flux in the Soutflow aperture is 0.379 Jy km/s (HCN) / 0.219 (HCO+) outside mask, 0 inside). Residual-image flux has dirty-beam units, so its flux scale carries an efficiency factor (JvM epsilon) that Q2r2 bounded at 0.73-0.95 (synthetic uv; adopted +25%/-10%): this is a systematic on E and on the Xb4d/Xb4b comparison (Xb4b has no mask cubes in the archive set). (d) BOWL/RMS: annulus 1.5-4" from S (N, Bridge excluded) mean level in -405..-205 is +0.00..+0.02 mJy/beam (HCN) and +0.02 (HCO+) vs channel scatter of the annulus mean 0.06-0.07 mJy/beam: no negative bowl; off-source (r>8") per-channel rms is 1.34x/1.19x the line-free value in the HCN spw at -405..-305/-305..-205 km/s but 0.95x in HCO+ (E1/W clumps and other weak lines in the HCN band may contribute; the 200-aperture noise used for E already includes this). CONCLUSION: no artefact signature found (azimuth, red mirror, bowl, mask); a compact lobe, uncleaned, 1.8" S of the S nucleus along the outflow axis (axis PA 198 deg from the Q0 Sblue blob; lobe PA 186 deg).

results.quantity: Is the Xb4d vs Xb4b difference of the Soutflow blue-wing HCN/HCO+ ratio due to missing extended HCN flux? Outer-window fluxes in both arrays and the consequence for p0005 R_wing>R_core
results.target: Soutflow, Bridge, S, N; Xb4b/Xb4d at 1.05"
results.value: Outer blue window -405..-205 at Soutflow (Jy km/s): HCN Xb4d 0.368+-0.039, Xb4b 0.214+-0.065 (diff -0.154+-0.076, -2.0 sigma, ratio 0.58); HCO+ Xb4d 0.199+-0.032, Xb4b 0.214+-0.070 (+0.015+-0.077, ratio 1.08). R_outer 1.9+-0.4 (Xb4d) vs 1.0+-0.4 (Xb4b): differ by 1.5 sigma; E 0.262+-0.042 vs 0.078+-0.079 (difference 0.18+-0.09, 2.0 sigma). Xb4b detects the HCN (3.5 sigma) and HCO+ (3.1 sigma) outer-window flux at Soutflow; its ring at 1.85" from S peaks at the same azimuth (180 deg). So 'absent in Xb4b' is not what the data say: Xb4b is statistically consistent both with E=0 (1.0 sigma) and with the Xb4d value (2 sigma low), because its noise is 1.6-2x higher. The HCN flux deficit in Xb4b (0.58+-0.2 of Xb4d) and none in HCO+ is a 2-sigma hint of a spatially extended (>~2") or uncleaned HCN component, same sign as the Bridge red half (HCN 0.59, HCO+ 1.07); S: HCN 0.88, HCO+ 1.00 (blue half -400..-100). Core-window ratios agree between arrays within 1-2%. Possible origins that remain open: (i) an extended HCN-bright wing component filtered by Xb4b, (ii) uncleaned residual flux in Xb4d whose flux scale differs (Xb4d clean mask absent at these velocities, see artefact entry), (iii) lobe-specific blend. REVISION of p0005 (tiered): MEASURED - Xb4d outer-window HCN excess over k*HCO+ at the lobe 1.8" S of S, 6.2 sigma, R_outer 1.9+-0.4 (core 0.54); REPRODUCED in one array - Xb4b gives the same sign and azimuth but only 1.0 sigma in E and R_outer 1.0+-0.4; INTERPRETATION UNTESTED - extended HCN skirt vs imaging effect vs lobe-specific blend. Team-a's Xb4d 1.24 vs Xb4b 1.00 is the same pattern (their window includes the HCO+ core wing).

results.quantity: Is the HCN excess over k*HCO+ at HCN-frame 2375-2575 km/s (-405..-205 km/s about VSYS) at Soutflow a blend? Companion-line test for HDO, CH3CHO, c-C3H, l-C3H in all four Xb4d spws, shape test, LTE column
results.value: Reproduced: E=+0.262+-0.042 Jy km/s (6.2 sigma, 200-aperture noise; 71% of the HCN window flux 0.368; team-a 0.164 Jy/beam km/s, 57%); N -0.014, Bridge -0.037, S +0.056 (+-0.047-0.055): a blend that scales with dense-gas emission or sits in every spectrum is excluded; only a species confined to the lobe could do this. CANDIDATES in the window (Q0 line list; HCN frame, v_loc=0): HDO 2(2,0)-3(1,3) 266.1611 (Eu 157 K, -307 km/s), CH3CHO 12(6,6)-13(5,8) E 266.2133 (153 K, -365), l-C3H v4=1 266.1655/.1692/.1805 (244 K, -316..-345), c-C3H 4(3,1)-4(1,4) 266.1755/.2039 (32 K, logA -7.3, very weak). COMPANION TEST (LTE, optically thin, g A exp(-Eu/T), normalised so that the species' window lines carry all of E; matched filter of the Gaussian-line template (FWHM 100 or 195 km/s, v_loc 0 or -29) on the Soutflow aperture spectra of spw25/27/29/31, high-pass baseline, noise from 200 random apertures): 95% upper limit on the fraction of E the species can carry (f_max): CH3CHO 0.1-0.4% (60 K), 0.4-0.9% (100 K), 2-4% (200 K), 4-9% (500 K) (the ground-state 13(2,11)-12(2,10) A/E lines at 254.83/254.85 GHz and 13(3,10)-12(3,9) at 251.36/251.49 GHz would be 16-20 Jy km/s if CH3CHO carried E; measured +0.02+-0.09 and +0.00+-0.05); c-C3H <0.1% at all T (the 5(1,4)-4(1,3) group at 252.5-253.1 GHz would be 3000 Jy km/s); l-C3H <=0.1-0.4% (60-200 K), <=1% (500 K) (251.43 GHz triplet predicted 140 Jy km/s). These three carriers are therefore excluded. HDO CANNOT be tested this way: no other HDO line with >=2% of the predicted flux lies in the four spws at T<=500 K (the next, 5(2,3)-4(3,2) 255.050 GHz, Eu 437 K, falls at 252.69 GHz, 90 MHz above spw29). SHAPE: the excess is a bump of FWHM 230+-32 km/s centred at -277+-13 km/s (chi2 120 vs 227 null), not a pinned broad skirt; single-line templates of FWHM 195 km/s fit equally well (chi2 HDO 121, l-C3H 127, c-C3H 138, CH3CHO 140 vs Gaussian 113; FWHM 100 km/s lines are worse by 40+), so the shape does not discriminate; HDO (-307, or -336 in the -29 km/s frame) is 2.3-4.5 sigma from the fitted centre. LTE COLUMN a HDO blend would need (filling 1, thin): N(HDO)=3.4e14 (100 K), 4.6e14 (60 K), 4.4e14 (200 K) cm-2, 2.2e15 (30 K) - 250-620x the thin HCO+ column in the same window (lower bound; filling<1 raises both): not excluded without an assumed abundance. CONSEQUENCES of the two leading interpretations: (a) all of the window flux is wing gas: HCN/HCO+ = 1.9+-0.4 (3.6x the local core 0.53: an abundance and/or excitation enhancement, as in the Sblue RADEX discussion of the Q1 entry; degenerate with 3-2 alone); (b) E is HDO: the wing then has R = k = 0.53, equal to the core, no enhancement, and N(HDO)>=3e14 in a 2" aperture. HCO+ shows a real wing in the same lobe and velocity range (0.199+-0.032, 6 sigma) so a wing component exists in either case; HCN alone extends to -450 km/s (HCO+ undetected beyond -300). Verdict (p0006 iii): not a blend of CH3CHO, c-C3H or l-C3H (>=91-99.9% excluded); HDO untested and not excluded; Xb4d-only significance per the Xb4d/Xb4b entry.

results.quantity: DIRECT CHECK of team-a p0005-r03/p0010 (i): beam-mixing test of the N wing ratio: Xb4b HCN/HCO+ 3-2 at N with the same data at native 0.25", 0.30" and 1.05"
results.target: N (HCN peak), apertures r<0.25" and r<0.5"
results.value: Wing (both sides stacked, 100-260 km/s about the local centroid) over core (|v_loc|<60), R_wing/R_core: native 0.25" r<0.25": 1.00+-0.14 (R_wing 0.97+-0.13, R_core 0.97+-0.03; HCN 12 sigma, HCO+ 9 sigma); 0.30": 1.05+-0.14 (R_wing 1.01, core 0.97); convolved to 1.05" r<0.5": 1.21+-0.18 (R_wing 0.98, core 0.81); 1.05" r<0.25": 1.41+-0.21 (R_wing 1.14, core 0.81). So no wing rise at 0.25-0.30" (team-a: 1.05+-0.13 vs 0.98), and a 20-40% apparent rise after smoothing to the Xb4d beam (about 1.5-2 sigma each; same data so the errors are correlated). Velocity slope of the ratio per 100 km/s in 40 km/s bins (+-140): -0.044+-0.041 (native), -0.010+-0.036 (0.30"), +0.022+-0.036 (1.05", r<0.5") , +0.055+-0.040 (r<0.25"): the sign change is reproduced but each slope is consistent with zero in our empirical noise (team-a: -0.003+-0.013 -> +0.072+-0.008, smaller errors from null windows). Radial dependence at native 0.25" (annuli 0-0.25/0.25-0.5/0.5-1/1-2"): core R 0.97/0.83/0.66/0.41, wing R (both sides) 0.97+-0.14/1.02+-0.13/0.65+-0.08/0.58: the wing ratio tracks the local core ratio at each radius (wing/core 1.0, 1.2, 1.0, 1.4), i.e. there is no intrinsic velocity dependence of HCN/HCO+ at N at 0.25" resolution; the apparent rise at 1" is the mixing of a wing that is concentrated inside r<0.5" (high-ratio gas) with a core spread to larger radii (ratio 0.4-0.7). Conclusion (a direct check of p0005-r03, same Xb4b data at three beams): team-a p0005-r03/p0010 (i) CONFIRMED qualitatively (beam/radial mixing, no intrinsic wing rise at N); quantitative slope significance not reproduced at their level.

results.quantity: Is the S dense-gas blue lobe separable from the disk (rotation / warp null test) and does its geometry match the CO outflow? (HCN, HCO+ 3-2)
results.target: lobe 1.88" (365 pc) S of S; S and N nuclei and red feature for comparison
results.value: YES for the S blue lobe, NO for the nuclear wings. (1) Narrow-component velocity field at the lobe (Xb4b 0.25" per-pixel narrow-peak velocity, pixels >5 sigma): v0=+14 (HCO+) / -11 (HCN) km/s, range -41..+63 / -68..+49 km/s, gradient |grad v|=33 (HCO+) and 40 (HCN) km/s/arcsec (components dv/dN=+27/+38, dv/dE-ish -19/-12), i.e. rotational smearing sigma ~15-18 km/s over the 1.05" beam. To place gas at |v_los|=180 km/s by smearing a >=340 km/s/arcsec gradient is needed (8-12x larger). (2) Beam-smeared rotation null model (every 0.25" pixel carries only a narrow Gaussian of sigma 25/40/60 km/s at its own measured velocity, smoothed exactly like the data): predicted wing flux (-405..-150) at the lobe = 0.000/0.003/0.008 (HCO+) and 0.000/0.002/0.005 (HCN) Jy km/s vs observed 0.31 (HCO+) and 0.30 (HCN) in the same Xb4b cube: rotation cannot produce the lobe wing. At the S nucleus the same null gives 0.02/0.14/0.40 (HCO+, sigma_n 25/40/60) and 0.01/0.05/0.13 (HCN) vs observed 0.18/0.10: the nuclear wings ARE reproducible by beam-smeared nuclear rotation + broad intrinsic lines (at N: 0.00/0.08/0.39 HCO+ vs 0.19), so only the lobe is separable. (3) E-W cut through the lobe (r=0.5" apertures, Xb4d@1.05"): where the wing is detected (flux >0.05 Jy km/s, -1.0"<=dE<=+0.5") the narrow-peak velocity is within -50..+47 km/s (no systematic E-W gradient; outside the lobe the narrow peak is noise dominated) and the wing centroid (-420..-100) is -190..-250 km/s at every such position: no rotating-disk pattern. (4) Geometry vs literature: our lobe is at PA 183+-2 (HCN), 190 (HCO+) deg, r=365 pc projected; Michiyama+2018 South-OF-Blue is 0.54" W, 2.23" S of their S nucleus = PA 194 deg, 445 pc (2" beam), HCN/HCO+ 1-0 detected in [-360,-180]; Sakamoto+2014 (ApJ 797, 90): S nuclear disk edge-on PA ~90 deg, outflow along the rotation axis (PA ~0/180), blue cone S, curving W with distance, opening ~20 deg, CO high-velocity emission peaking 1.8" (310 pc) from the nucleus on both sides, outflow axis inclination i=80 deg (70-85) FROM THE LINE OF SIGHT (flow near the plane of the sky; velocity factor 1/cos i = 2.9-11, 5.8 at 80 deg), Pereira-Santaella+2024 (A&A 681, A117) i~80 deg plane-of-sky, GOALS-JWST (arXiv:2403.14751) 20 deg from the sky plane (~70 deg from the LOS). Our lobe PA and distance agree with the CO outflow axis within the errors. The task note that the S outflow is "close to the line of sight" is not supported by these papers: it is close to the plane of the sky. Caveat: team-a p0006 (q3b_kin) gets the same answer (E-W gradient 35 km/s/arcsec -> expected sigma 62 vs observed 100-150 km/s); a tidal/warped extension of the disk with a velocity structure not seen in the narrow gas is not excluded by the data, but would need -180..-400 km/s with no counterpart in the narrow component.
results.uncertainty: gradient +-10 km/s/arcsec; null predictions are the central values for the three sigma_n

results.quantity: Common kinematic decomposition of the S lobe in HCN and HCO+ 3-2 (narrow disk-like + broad Gaussian), component fluxes and the window sensitivity
results.target: S lobe r=1.0" aperture, Xb4d@1.05" (also r=1.5")
results.value: Shared-kinematics model (same velocity and width of both components for both lines, amplitudes free; 8 parameters): chi2=755/635 (red. 1.19): narrow v=+34 km/s sigma 28, broad centroid -118+-8 km/s sigma 110+-7; broad flux HCN 0.834+-0.056, HCO+ 1.157+-0.076 Jy km/s; ratio HCN/HCO+ (Tb) of the broad component 0.73 (narrow 0.42). Separate kinematics per line (12 parameters): chi2=646/631: HCN broad centroid -178+-8 sigma 142 (flux 0.993+-0.059), HCO+ broad -89+-8 sigma 90 (flux 1.099+-0.080); Tb ratio 0.91. The shared-kinematics model is REJECTED (delta chi2=109 for 4 parameters; HCN broad is ~90 km/s bluer and 1.6x wider than HCO+), so the HCN and HCO+ broad components are not the same gas profile. The line ratio therefore depends on the window: fixed -405..-150 km/s window (data) HCN/HCO+ (Tb) = 1.46 (Xb4d standard), 1.54 (tapered), 0.83 (Xb4b); whole broad component 0.6-0.9. Window fractions: only 52% (HCN, own fit) / 25% (HCO+, own fit) / 38% (shared) of the broad flux lies in -405..-150 km/s and 41%/75%/61% in |v|<150, so a window-only mass is a floor by a factor 2-4. HDO scenario (the Q11 outer-blue HCN excess 0.25+-0.05 Jy km/s is HDO 2(2,0)-3(1,3) at 266.161 GHz, at -365 km/s, FWHM 100 or 195 km/s, fitted as an extra Gaussian on HCN only, shared broad kinematics): HDO flux 0.16+-0.03 (FWHM 100) / 0.31+-0.03 (195) Jy km/s, HCN broad flux falls to 0.76 / 0.70 (from 0.83), HCN/HCO+ broad ratio 0.66 / 0.63; chi2 improves by 50 / 84 over the shared model without HDO but stays worse than the separate-kinematics model (chi2 706 / 672 vs 646 with 3 / 3 more parameters): HDO vs genuinely broader/bluer HCN is NOT decided by these data (delta chi2=26-60 for 3 parameters, correlated noise), consistent with Q11.
results.uncertainty: errors from 60 noise-injection refits

results.quantity: Non-LTE (RADEX LVG) dense-gas mass of the S blue lobe, HCO+- and HCN-based, with abundance and excitation uncertainty
results.target: S lobe broad component (all velocities), r=1.0" aperture (Omega=pi arcsec^2), Xb4d
results.value: [MODEL-FAILURE FLAG (Q2r2 review): the single-zone LVG fit is HCO+-driven and fails the HCN 3-2/1-0 ratio (0.07 vs 0.38+-0.12) and needs N(HCN)/N(HCO+)~10; it is not a validated description. Quote the dense mass as the scaled quantity M(HCO+) = 7.8e6 x (1e-8/X(HCO+)) Msun (68% 5.2e6-1.3e7 at X=1e-8; 2.6e7 at 3e-9, 7.8e7 at 1e-9), i.e. an abundance (x10) times excitation (x3-5) estimate, 'low' confidence; HCN-based ~10x higher. The 'central' 1.4e7 used downstream is a geometric mean chosen with the CO cap and is not independent of it.] Importance-sampled posterior of a single-zone LVG model (RADEX, LAMDA hcn.dat/hco+.dat, Tbg 2.73 K) with free log n(H2) (1e4-1e7), Tk (10-50 K), N(HCN)/dv, N(HCO+)/dv (N(H2)<3e23 cm-2 cap = Sakamoto nuclear peak), filling factor eta (0.02-1), fitted to the 3-2 brightness of both broad components (flux +-25%) and the 3-2/1-0 ratios (HCN 0.38+-0.12, HCO+ 0.19+-0.06), with 4-3/3-2 and 2-1 upper limits. Result (own-kinematics fluxes HCN 0.99, HCO+ 1.10 Jy km/s): log n=4.9 (68%: 4.6-5.3), Tk=28 K (15-43; Tk is unconstrained by the data: 10-15 K and 40-100 K give the same mass within 10%), filling factor of the aperture 0.50 (0.23-0.82), N(HCN)/N(HCO+)=10 (7-13). The HCN 3-2/1-0 ratio is not reproduced (model 0.07 vs 0.38+-0.12, 2.6 sigma, chi2min=6 for 4 data) while HCO+ 0.19-0.21 is: the HCO+ 1-0 prefers n~1e5, the HCN 1-0/3-2 prefers high density or extra HCN excitation (IR pumping by the AGN 14 um continuum is not in this model) or a two-phase gas as in Michiyama+2018. MASS: HCO+-based M = 7.8e+06 (68%: 5.2e+06-1.3e+07) Msun for X(HCO+)=1e-8, 2.6e+07 for 3e-9, 7.8e+07 for 1e-9; HCN-based (own kinematics) 7.3e+07 for X(HCN)=1e-8 and 7.3e+08 for 1e-9, i.e. HCN-based is ~10x the HCO+-based mass because the fit needs N(HCN)~10 N(HCO+) (HCN is under-excited per molecule at n~1e5); HDO scenario (HCN broad flux reduced to 0.70) lowers the HCN-based mass by 26% only (5.4e+07 at X=1e-8). Dependence on assumptions (HCO+ X=1e-8 mass): wide prior n 1e3-1e8, Tk 10-300 K: 9.8e+06; Tk 10-15 K 7.7e+06; Tk 40-100 K 8.5e+06; N(H2) cap 1e24 / 1e25: 8.8e+06 / 1.3e+07; without the 1-0 constraint the fit moves to n=10^6.3 and M(HCO+, X=1e-8)=1.6e+06, M(HCN, X=1e-8)=7.1e+06 (this equals the old thin-LTE 1-2e6 route). Dominant uncertainty: the abundance X (a factor 10 in the prior, 0.29 dex of the 0.45 dex posterior spread of M_HCN), then the density (1e5 vs 1e6: factor ~5) and the column cap/filling factor degeneracy (thick clumps can hide >10x more mass: uncapped N(H2) gives 1.3e+08). The alpha route (alpha_HCN=10 x L'(1-0)) gives 4.6e6-7.9e6 Msun for the Michiyama inner/map HCN(1-0) luminosity (the old 1.5-1.9e7 used L'(3-2)/0.35 over a wider window and aperture; team-a p0006 1.4-4.6e6 used the 1-0 route with the inner aperture): the three are consistent within the window/aperture differences, but alpha_HCN=10 (virialised cloud ensembles) is not meant for unbound outflowing gas and gives dense > total molecular gas (see the dense-fraction entry).
results.uncertainty: factor ~10 (X) x ~3-5 (excitation); HCO+-based 0.8e7 - 7.8e7 for X 1e-8 - 1e-9, CO-limited to <~2.6e7

results.quantity: Red high-velocity feature (+180..320 km/s) between S and N: trials calibration, extension of the N wing or separate peak, sidelobe leakage, N wing limits
results.target: peak at 3.45" N of S (1.8" S of N), r=1.0" apertures, Xb4d@1.05"
results.value: (i) Trials: the red-window aperture flux at the peak is HCN 0.246 Jy km/s = 9.7 field-sigma (sigma 0.025) and HCO+ 0.196 = 6.1 sigma (sigma 0.032); within 8" of the N-S midpoint (~62 independent r=1" apertures, 1" around N and S excluded) it is the global maximum in both lines (grid points >= the feature: 2 of ~1000 for HCN and 11 for HCO+, all at the same place); in line-free windows (+380..+520, +540..+680, -800..-660) of the same region the largest aperture flux is <=0.09 (HCN) and <=0.08 Jy km/s (HCO+), local rms 0.025 / 0.019, so the feature is 9.7 / 10.3 local sigma (Gaussian a-posteriori p<1e-20 x 62 trials): real, not a noise or empty-channel residual fluctuation. (ii) Spatial/velocity structure: along the N-S axis the +180..320 flux (r=1") is 0.02 at S, 0.09 at +1.5", 0.14 at +2", 0.23 at +3, peaks at +3.5" (0.24 HCN, 0.20 HCO+), is 0.15 at +5" and 0.10 at +5.5" (N at +5.2": 0.12 HCN, 0.12 HCO+), i.e. a single ridge from ~+1.5" to +6.5" (FWHM ~4") with its maximum 1.7" S of N, not centred on N: it is more than an extension of the N broad component (N aperture red broad component 0.23+-0.06 HCN at +199 km/s, s75d), and also not on S (a shoulder at +1.85", the mirror of the blue lobe, holds 0.12-0.14 = 25% of the blue-lobe flux). Its position coincides with Michiyama+2018 OF-Red (0.22" W, 3.56" N of their S nucleus; HCN/HCO+(1-0) 0.08+-0.02 each, [240,360]) whose CO they also call intermixed S+N outflow. (iii) Leakage: the +180..320 flux on a ring of r=1.8" around N (12 azimuths, 30 deg steps) is 0.25 at azimuth 180 (toward S), 0.12/0.13 at 150/210 and <=0.05 elsewhere (HCN; HCO+ 0.20, 0.13/0.10), i.e. a one-sided clump 60-90 deg wide, not the ring/lobed pattern expected from the sidelobes of N (and the beam is elongated E-W, where nothing is seen); the line-free window on the same ring is <=0.03; the blue window -405..-150 along the same N-S line is <=0.04 (|blue| at +1..+8" is -0.07..+0.03), so neither N nor the Bridge leak into the S-window channels. (iv) N wing limits for 150-350 km/s (r=1" at N, core -150..150 = 10.4 HCN / 14.3 HCO+ Jy km/s): blue 150-350: +0.025 (HCN) and -0.001 (HCO+) Jy km/s, 3 sigma <0.076 / <0.096 = <0.73% / <0.67% of the core; red 150-350: +0.197 / +0.190 Jy km/s (7.9 / 5.9 sigma, 1.9% / 1.3% of the core), i.e. N has a one-sided RED wing, not a bipolar one, and this wing is the flank of the S-N ridge. Conclusion: a real, spatially distinct red-shifted dense-gas clump/ridge between the nuclei; whether it is the S counter-lobe (it would be 1.8x farther from S than the blue lobe), the N-nucleus outflow (N is near pole-on: the red flank would be at the back of the disk) or Bridge gas is NOT decided; the PV velocities (+230..+280) are those of the red CO wing near N in Sakamoto+2014 and OF-Red in Michiyama+2018.

results.quantity: Q16: can the S-nucleus core T43/T32 be measured from the 6" data? Origin of the 0.06-0.09 offset of the p0012 core ladders (re-implemented deblend, factorial test, injection-recovery, forward-model ratio field)
results.target: S and N nucleus core T43/T32 (HCN, HCO+) at the Xb4f beam from Xb4d 3-2 templates; team-a p0012 values HCN N 0.395 S 0.268; HCO+ N 0.482 S 0.442
results.value: (1) A p0012-like NNLS template deblend (N, S, Bridge [, Outer] templates from Xb4d 3-2, same template for 3-2 and 4-3, Xb4f beam; s77, s80) reproduces the p0012 values only in part and unstably: HCN N 0.32-0.42, S 0.23-0.30 (median over core radius 1-2", fit radius 10/14", no Outer; baseline none/plane; formal vs empirical errors), HCO+ N 0.39-0.53, S 0.35-0.48, Bridge 0.29-0.58; with an Outer component the cores jump (HCN S 0.28-0.58, HCO+ S 0.54-0.87) because the Outer J=3 amplitude collapses to ~0 (degenerate). The fits are statistically unacceptable with formal errors (chi2/dof 20-300): the moment-0 maps have negative bowls of -0.5 to -1.2 Jy/beam km/s and an empirical off-source rms 0.6 (HCN)/1.0 (HCO+) vs formal 0.25, and clipping the noisy Xb4d template at zero adds a +0.5-2 Jy/beam km/s positive bias after convolution to 5.7x3.5". (2) Injection-recovery (s79; truth = observed J3 map, J4 = known ratio field times the Xb4d template plus an extended term, correlated noise 0.3, 20 realisations): when the model assumptions hold the deblend is nearly unbiased: input S 0.36 -> 0.346 [0.305,0.370]; 0.268 -> 0.283; 0.45 -> 0.407; extended gas poor in J4 (halo 0.20): 0.36 -> 0.299 (bias -0.06, worst case); N recovered within 0.045 (low). So NNLS positivity/window by themselves do not produce a -0.09 offset; the real J4 map departs from a J3-shaped template (ratio gradients, different Xb47/Xb4f filtering of extended gas). (3) Forward-model ratio field (s78; J3 reproduced exactly, J4 = conv(template x rho(x)) + rho_h R, rho = rho_h + core excesses of width s, errors with the empirical floor, chi2~dof): rho_S = 0.19-0.72 (HCN) depending on s=1-3" and on the template (HCN or HCO+ morphology), rho_h = 0.0-0.2: the S core ladder is NOT measurable at this resolution (model-dependent over a factor 2-3), consistent with Q3/p0011. (4) Bounds (s85): only 0.31-0.45 (r<1-1.5") to 0.65 (r<2.5") of the S 3-2 flux in the Xb4f beam is compact-core (Xb4d template) and 55-70% is non-core; if all non-core gas has T43/T32 <= the N value (0.45 HCN, 0.57 HCO+) the S core is >= 0.27 (HCN, rc 1.5") / 0.41 (HCO+), i.e. p0012 S 0.268 is at the edge of the allowed range for HCN. p0012 own components predict an S aperture ratio of 0.27-0.33 (HCN) and 0.35-0.46 (HCO+) versus the observed 0.357+-0.011 and 0.486+-0.005: shortfall 0.03-0.09 (HCN), 0.03-0.13 (HCO+); the p0012 S core value requires the non-core gas around S (50-60% of its flux) to have T43/T32 >= 0.43 (N-like), higher than p0012 own Bridge (0.363) and Outer (0.28). Subtracting Bridge-like gas (ladder 0.362) at 10-30% share changes the S core by <0.01 (HCN 0.357 -> 0.355) because the Bridge ladder equals the S ladder; subtracting N-like gas (0.450) at 30% (unphysical share: N response 0.003) gives 0.317 (HCN), 0.452 (HCO+). Net: S core T43/T32 (HCN) = 0.36 (+0.09,-0.09), not measured; the p0012 value 0.268 is not excluded but is not supported either; origin of the offset: not a single choice (baseline bowl, template clipping and Outer degeneracy each move S by 0.03-0.3).
results.uncertainty: S core T43/T32 (HCN) 0.27-0.45 allowed; injection scatter +-0.03, bias -0.01..-0.06 under ideal assumptions; model-dependent range 0.19-0.72 in the ratio-field fit

results.target: N, S, Bridge; 4 ladders each (HCN, HCO+ 3-2/2-1 in the Xb55 beam and 4-3/3-2 in the Xb4f beam), p0012 RADEX classes A+B+F2 pooled, flat T 10-150 K and log n priors, Tbg 2.73 K
results.value: Marginal Tk (16/50/84%): N 40/65/100 K, S 25/40/65 K, Bridge 30/50/80 K (log n 4.4-5.25 for all three, prior-dominated; n(H,O mean) median 4.75). P(Tk>=80 K): N 0.40, S 0.10, Bridge 0.23. Pairwise (regions independent): Tk_N/Tk_S median 1.60 [0.80,2.67], P(Tk_N>Tk_S)=0.67, P(ratio>1.4)=0.53; n_N/n_S median 1.0 [0.32,3.2], P(n_N>n_S)=0.45, P(either Tk ratio>1.4 or n ratio>2)=0.75; Tk_N/Tk_Bridge 1.25 [0.62,2.3] (P>1 0.55); Tk_S/Tk_Bridge 0.80 [0.46,1.6] (P>1 0.30; n ratio 1.33 [0.3,4.2]). With Q12 recovery corrections: Tk N 40/80/100, S 30/50/80, Bridge 30/65/100 K; Tk_N/Tk_S median 1.33 [0.65,2.7], P(Tk_N>Tk_S)=0.62. So the measured N-S ladder contrast (HCN 4-3/3-2 1.26, 2-3 sigma) cannot be turned into a significant Tk or n difference with these four ladders: it allows Tk_N/Tk_S ~1-2.7 or n_N/n_S ~1-3 along the usual Tk-n degeneracy, with equal probability for n higher and Tk higher (P(Tk ratio>1 and n ratio<1)=0.39). S and Bridge are statistically identical (S/Bridge ladder ratios 0.99+-0.11 HCN, 0.98+-0.07 HCO+); N is the only region with a (modestly) different ladder: N distinct from S and Bridge at 2-3 sigma in the ratio, but not in (Tk, n).
results.uncertainty: posteriors on an 11-point T and coarse n grid; regions treated as independent (shared calibration/recovery systematics ignored; the recovery variant brackets them)

results.quantity: Q16: forward-model deblend of the N and S core ladders from circular 6.5"/10" apertures; Tkin>=Tdust and CO checks
results.target: N, S, Bridge, E1, E2 positions; Xb4d 3-2 core morphology smoothed to 6.5" and 10"
results.value: NOT constraining. A 3-component (N core, S core, rest; and 4-comp with Bridge) linear solution of the observed same-beam T43/T32 gives HCN r_S=0.00 [0.00,0.00] and r_N=0.19-0.22, HCO+ r_S 0.82-0.97 with chi2/dof 3-38 (3% template floor): the N, S, Bridge apertures differ by only 6-14%, the solution is degenerate and hits the non-negativity boundary; r_S is not measured this way (consistent with Q3: circular 10" apertures cannot separate N and S). Implied ladder of the non-core gas if the p0012 core values hold: HCN 0.37-0.43 at 6.5" but 0.27-0.30 at 10" (rc=1-1.5"), i.e. not a constant rest ladder, again pointing to biased core values. Tkin>=Tdust: dust Tb at 0.24" is 0.19 K (N), 0.62 K (S) RJ at 265 GHz (p0012 q2_dust_field, 3.0/3.7 K beam-averaged Tbg,eff) and gives no dust temperature; a mid-IR-heated nucleus with n~1e5 cm-3 is expected to have Tk~Td>~30-40 K (literature, not measured here), at odds with 20-30 K but not with the >=25 K lower edge found above. CO Tb: no CO cube in the data, check not possible. Pereira-Santaella+2024 (2024A&A...681A.117P) find >40 K in the central 100 pc of the S outflow (CO v=1-0 P2/R0, a different phase and region): supports Tk(S)>~40 K, not 20-30 K.
results.uncertainty: solutions hit boundary; MC 16-84% over core radius 1-2.5", position +-0.3", floor 3-5%

results.quantity: Q5r2: CS 7-6 vs HCN 4-3 and HCO+ 4-3 in a common 4.31x2.79" beam, on-source baseline-offset correction, N+S(+Bridge) beam-deconvolved ratios, and reconciliation with team-a p0009
results.target: N, S, Bridge, Sblue, E1, E2, W (Xb47)
results.value: (1) BASELINE OFFSET. The off-source (5-13") median of the matched CS amplitude is -0.128/-0.134/-0.124/-0.112 (N/S/Bridge/Sblue) and -0.054/-0.051/-0.050 (E1/E2/W) Jy/beam km/s, i.e. -0.5..-1.0 sigma_field: a negative baseline bowl around the bright nuclear complex (the spw covers only +-800 km/s, so the baseline is pinned by 500-800 km/s sidebands that contain CS/HCN wings and the bowl). Correcting the on-source W for it (W-median; the correction is applied as the central value and the uncorrected value is the other end of the bracket) gives CS 7-6 W (Jy/beam km/s, sigma_used = max(formal, field MAD)): N 1.87 -> 1.99 (13.9 -> 14.8 sigma); S 0.71 -> 0.84 (5.5 -> 6.5 sigma); Bridge 1.00 -> 1.13 (8.1 -> 9.2 sigma); Sblue 0.25 -> 0.36 (2.5 -> 3.6 sigma); E1 0.08 -> 0.14 (0.8 -> 1.3 sigma); E2 0.15 -> 0.20 (1.5 -> 2.0 sigma); W 0.02 -> 0.07 (0.3 -> 1.2 sigma). So S and Bridge CS are firmer (6.5 and 9.2 sigma; they stay 'detected'), Sblue rises from 2.5 to 3.6 sigma ('tentative'), E1/E2/W remain <2 sigma. The offset is a systematic of +-0.13 Jy/beam km/s (7% of N, 15-18% of S): it raises R_K(CS/HCN) at S by ~18% (0.136 -> ~0.16, the HCN offset being <=4% of N, ~10% of S from the pixel-moment field medians -0.65/-0.17 Jy/beam km/s). SO 6_5-5_4(J_N 5_6-4_5; 251.826 GHz) Xb4f: field medians N/S/Bridge -0.036/-0.034/-0.034 (-0.5 sigma); S: SO-only 4.2 -> 4.6 sigma, with the CH3OH ladder free 2.9 -> 3.3 sigma (R_K 0.015/0.012); Bridge 3.2 -> 3.7 sigma; N 1.0 -> 1.4: SO stays 'tentative' (<5 sigma) and non-specific to S; Xb4d medians are <=0.002 (no correction), SO 8-7 medians -0.014 (0.2 sigma). (2) COMMON BEAM. Xb47 HCN 4-3 (4.14x2.70") and HCO+ 4-3 (4.13x2.70") smoothed per channel to the CS beam 4.31x2.79" (radio_beam kernel, flux x beam-area ratio), window 2780+-300 km/s, linear baseline from 500-1100 km/s sidebands, single-pixel moment (noise 0.37/1.0/0.9 Jy/beam km/s for CS/HCN/HCO+, off-source MAD; this single-pixel box estimator is noisier than the aperture matched filter: S CS is 2.2 sigma raw (2.7 offset-corrected, field exceedance 1.5%) here vs 5.5-6.5 sigma in the matched-filter aperture and 8 sigma in the N+S fit below). Peak-pixel R_K(CS 7-6/HCN 4-3), offset-corrected: N 0.168+-0.027, S 0.157+-0.063, Bridge 0.198+-0.066; CS/HCO+ 4-3 N 0.094+-0.014, S 0.051+-0.019, Bridge 0.081+-0.024. At a circular 6.5" beam (team-a's Q1 aperture): CS/HCO+ N 0.071, S 0.064, Bridge 0.069 (+-0.015); CS/HCN 0.157/0.176/0.172. (3) TWO/THREE-COMPONENT DECONVOLUTION: beam-shaped point sources at N, S (and Bridge) + constant fitted to the common-beam moment maps in a 16" box (errors x sqrt(8) for pixel correlation). CS 7-6 amplitudes (Jy/beam km/s): N+S 2.66+-0.19 / 1.54+-0.19; N+S+Bridge 2.37/1.33/0.95. Deblended R_K(CS/HCN 4-3): N 0.165+-0.014, S 0.182+-0.028 (N/S = 0.91+-0.16; with Bridge 0.91+-0.17, Bridge 0.225+-0.056); R_K(CS/HCO+ 4-3): N 0.088+-0.008, S 0.063+-0.009 (N/S = 1.4+-0.23; with Bridge 1.47+-0.24). RESOLUTION OF THE TEAM-A DISAGREEMENT (forum p0009: CS/HCO+ N 0.051+-0.014, S 0.056+-0.019, N~S): it is a definition/aperture difference, not a data conflict. Team-a's 0.051/0.056 are CS 7-6/HCO+ **3-2** from 1" templates deblended into the 4.3x2.8" map (their Q4c) and, for 4-3, a 6.5" aperture (their Q1: 0.052/0.055) that sums N and S; at 6.5" we reproduce them (0.07/0.06 offset-corrected, 0.063/0.054 raw). In the native 4.3x2.8" beam team-a's own line table (CS/HCO+ 4-3 0.08 N, 0.045 S, p0001) agrees with our aperture values (0.087, 0.043). The aperture (peak) ratios N/S=2.0 overstate the contrast because the S aperture is contaminated by neighbouring emission and the N/S point separation is only 1.2 beams; the beam-deconvolved N/S is 1.4-1.5+-0.24 (CS/HCO+ 4-3) and 0.91+-0.16 (CS/HCN 4-3). Final statement: CS 7-6/HCN 4-3 is the same at N, S and Bridge within ~20-25% (N/S 0.9-1.2, +-0.2); CS/HCO+ 4-3 is higher at N by 1.4+-0.25 (1.7 sigma), i.e. not a significant difference. NULL TEST: a reflection of the apertures through the field centre is not a null here (the pointing centre is the N-S midpoint, reflection maps N<->S); instead the fraction of off-source field pixels with a CS moment >= the on-source value is 0.00 (N), 0.015 (S), 0.003 (Bridge), 0.10 (Sblue), 0.15 (W) at 4.3x2.8" and 0 (N, S, Bridge), 0.003 (Sblue), 0.35 (W) at 6.5". A line-free-window on-source null is impossible: the spw spans only +-800 km/s around the line.

results.quantity: Q5r2: Comparison with the only published chemistry of this target, Harada+2018 (Table 13): CH3OH, SO, SiO, CS, HCN, HCO+ at the common 1.7" resolution and in matched beams
results.target: N, S, Bridge/C, Sblue/OS, W/SW; Xb4d smoothed to 1.7" (and 4.31x2.79")
results.value: Harada+2018 (ApJ 855, 49, arXiv:1801.05941) Table 13 was re-parsed from the arXiv PDF text (lit/harada2018_1801.05941.txt -> lit/harada_table13_parsed.csv; 324 rows, 8 positions N, S, C, TNE, TSE, TSW, OS, SW) and the N and S rows agree exactly with team-a's /snapshots/team-a-s04/out/q4c/harada_table13_rows.csv. Harada's data are Band 3 and Band 6 (219-273 GHz) 12-m cubes convolved to 1.7", integrated over +-150 km/s of 2775 km/s (K km/s), errors from the cube rms (flux scale not in their errors; 10% each added below). NO Band 7 data: CS 7-6 and SO 8_8-7_7 are not in Harada (they have CS 2-1, 5-4, SO 2_1-1_2 99.3 and SO 219.949 = J_N 6_5-5_4, Eu 35 K, only at N), SiO 2-1 only, CH3OH 2k-1k 96.7, 5k-4k 241.8, 261.806 and, at TNE/TSW only, 254.015 (<2 sigma elsewhere). (a) CALIBRATION CHECK at identical resolution (Xb4d cubes smoothed per channel to 1.7" circular, peak pixel at our N and S, +-150 km/s about 2775, linear baseline; K): HCO+ 3-2 N 86.6 vs 91.56+-0.62 (ratio 0.95), S 54.2 vs 43.69 (1.24); HCN 3-2 N 64.7 vs 71.38 (0.91), S 20.2 vs 17.72 (1.14); peak T_b HCO+ N 534 vs 531 mK, S 359 vs 372 mK; HCN/HCO+ 3-2 N 0.747 vs 0.780, S 0.373 vs 0.406. N agrees within 5-9% (inside the 10% flux scales), the S integrals are 14-24% higher than Harada's (peaks agree within 4%): their S position/the line-centre offset (our S is at 2763 km/s, their window is centred on 2775) accounts for it. The ratio comparison below is therefore good to ~15-20%. (b) CH3OH 2_0-1_-1 E 254.015 / HCO+ 3-2 (K ratio, 1.7" common beam; ours = max(formal, empirical) errors): N 0.0055+-0.0056 (3 sigma <0.022), S 0.0112+-0.0057, Bridge 0.0408+-0.0035 (11.6 sigma), Sblue 0.0684+-0.0292, W 0.0705+-0.0143. Harada: <2 sigma peaks at N, S, C (centre, nearest to our Bridge); 3 sigma limits from their I errors (~0.7 K km/s) N <0.023, S <0.048, C <0.047, and TNE 0.0195+-0.0305, TSW 0.0562+-0.0682. Agreement: our Bridge 0.041+-0.004 is just below their C limit 0.047; no tension. Their 254 GHz data cannot test the Bridge/W enhancement; ours does (Bridge 11.6 sigma, W 4.9 sigma). (c) Harada's own CH3OH enhancement vs ours (ratio to HCO+ at matched J): 5k-4k 241.8/HCO+ 3-2: N 0.0638+-0.0062, S 0.0996+-0.0131, C 0.1334+-0.0125, OS (outflow south) 0.4570+-0.0600, SW 0.2235+-0.0169, TSW 0.2465+-0.0675; 2k-1k 96.7/HCO+ 1-0 N 0.015+-0.003, S 0.071+-0.008, OS 0.129+-0.015 (S/N 4.7, OS/N 8.6); SiO 2-1/HCO+ 1-0 N 0.031, S 0.031, OS 0.059, C 0.038 (SiO enhanced only at OS/C by 1.9x; N=S). So Harada: CH3OH/HCO+ is enhanced by 1.6x (S, 241.8), 4.7x (S, 96.7) and 7-9x (OS) over N, SiO by ~2x at OS. Ours (254.015, Eu 20 K): N<0.022 (3 sigma) and S 0.011+-0.006 vs Bridge 0.041+-0.004 (Bridge/S 3.7+-2.0), Sblue 0.068+-0.029 (2.3 sigma) and W 0.071+-0.014: CH3OH/HCO+ is also higher off the nuclei (Bridge, Sblue, W) than at N/S by a factor 2-7, the same sense as Harada's C/OS/TSW/SW enhancement; Sblue (3" S-SW of S along the HCN/HCO+ blue-wing blob) is probably the same outflow as Harada's OS (their coordinates are not tabulated; 'outflow south' of S per their Fig. 1 and Sakamoto+2014), but with 2.3 sigma this is suggestive only. At the S nucleus itself we do NOT see the 2-5x CH3OH enhancement of Harada's S/N (ours S/N = 2.0+-2.2 in 254/HCO+ at 1.7"), consistent with it within errors (their S/N from different lines/Eu). (d) CH3OH/CS in a matched 4.31x2.79" beam (Xb4d smoothed to the Xb47 CS beam; CS 7-6 offset-corrected aperture W): CH3OH 254.015/CS 7-6 (K): N 0.16+-0.07, S 0.60+-0.20, Bridge 0.56+-0.10, Sblue 0.46+-0.31; CH3OH/HCO+ 3-2 (4.3x2.8"): N 0.0078+-0.0033 (2.4 sigma), S 0.0168+-0.0051, Bridge 0.0228+-0.0033, Sblue 0.028+-0.017 (3 sigma limits <0.018, <0.032, <0.033, <0.08). Harada CH3OH(241.8)/CS(5-4): N 0.38+-0.04, S 0.94+-0.17, C 1.1+-0.2: the same rise N -> S/Bridge (ours N 0.16, S 0.60, Bridge 0.56; S/N 3.7+-1.8 vs Harada 2.5+-0.5). Caveat: the 254 line (Eu 20 K) and 241.8 (Eu 35-120 K) and CS J are different excitation, so only the sense of the gradient is comparable. (e) SO: Harada N SO 219.949 (J_N 6_5-5_4)/HCO+ 3-2 = 0.026+-0.008 (3.3 sigma; S, C, OS not detected), SO 2_1-1_2 99.3/HCO+ 1-0 N 0.024+-0.004, S 0.069+-0.009, OS 0.032. Our lines are different (251.826 = J_N 5_6-4_5, Eu 50.7 K; 344.311 = 8_8-7_7, Eu 87.5 K); LTE-optically-thin extrapolation of Harada's N 2.42+-0.74 K km/s (A, g_u, E_u from LAMDA so@lique.dat) predicts 251.826: 0.47 (Tex 10 K), 1.03 (20 K), 1.52 K km/s (40 K) [x1.7" beam] vs our N 0.39+-0.28 K km/s (3 sigma <1.2): consistent at Tex<~25 K (1.5 sigma at 20 K; the limit R<0.014 is below the extrapolated value 0.017 only for Tex>~40 K); and SO 8_8-7_7: 0.36 (20 K), 0.87 (30 K), 1.35 K km/s (40 K) at 1.7", i.e. 0.2-1.0 x that in our 4.3x2.8" beam depending on source size, vs our N 3 sigma limit 0.22 K km/s (Xb47): the limit excludes Tex(SO)>~30 K only if SO fills the 4.3" beam; for compact SO or Tex<=20 K there is no tension. Which of our limits are below Harada's detections: none in the direct sense (Harada's detections are of other transitions); SO 8-7/HCO+ 4-3 <0.011 (3 sigma, N) is below Harada's 219.949/HCO+ 3-2 0.026 but that comparison is not like-for-like (Eu 87 vs 35 K).

results.target: N, S, Bridge (Xb47)
results.value: The robust result is the line ratio: R_K(CS 7-6/HCN 4-3) = 0.16+-0.02 (N), 0.14-0.18 (S), 0.14-0.22 (Bridge), equal within 20-25% (deblended N/S 0.9+-0.2; offset-corrected aperture 0.16-0.17 N, 0.16 S). A column-density ratio is NOT a measured quantity: RADEX (LVG, dv=150 km/s, common Tk, n, width and filling) with N(HCN) set so that tau(HCN 4-3) = 0.3, 1, 3, 10 and the ladder-allowed (Tk>=56 K, log n 4-5) gas gives N(CS)/N(HCN) = 0.25-0.43 (N 0.30-0.43, S 0.25-0.37, Bridge 0.26-0.37), changing by only +-15% between tau 0.3 and 10 because the CS 7-6 column is solved at the same (Tk, n, N/dv) as the HCN reference and both lines saturate together; with the full grid (Tk 28-112 K, log n 4-6) the range is 0.17-0.67, driven by n and Tk (0.2 at n=3e5, 0.6 at n=1e4, Tk=28 K), i.e. the same factor-3 uncertainty as the (Tk, n) degeneracy of the J-ladder (Q3: log n=4.5 [3.6,5.0], Tk>56 K). The H13CN 4-3 limit (HCN/H13CN>8.3 at N, >4 at S; Q4) does not tighten this: for 12C/13C = 40-90 it requires tau(HCN 4-3)>=2-6 to sit at the limit, so N(HCN) is only bounded from below by a thick-line argument and N(CS)/N(HCN) is bounded above by ~0.7 in every scenario with a common filling factor. Statement to quote: 'CS 7-6/HCN 4-3 is the same, within ~20-25%, at N, S and Bridge; the implied N(CS)/N(HCN) ~ 0.2-0.7 (one zone, common excitation) is not independently constrained'. SO: 3 sigma N(SO)/N(HCO+) limits from the earlier grid (SO 8-7: <0.4-1 at Tk 80-160 K, n 1e5-1e6; looser at Tk<56 K) are not informative about a shock enhancement.
results.uncertainty: factor ~3 (set by (Tk, n)); +-15% from the HCN opacity; the beam filling of CS and HCN assumed equal; grid 0.25 dex
