results.quantity: Q5r2: Net answer to Q5 - is there a shock/chemistry signature (SO, CS 7-6, SiO, CH3OH) in the nuclei or the outflow, and what are CS 7-6/HCN 4-3 and SO/HCO+?
results.target: N, S nuclei; Bridge; Sblue (S outflow candidate); W clump
results.value: NO shock signature in the nuclei at the sensitivity available; the only shock-tracer detection is cold, off-nuclear CH3OH. (i) CS 7-6/HCN 4-3 (K): 0.16 (N), 0.14-0.18 (S), 0.14-0.22 (Bridge), uniform within ~20-25%; CS 7-6/HCO+ 4-3 0.09 (N), 0.06 (S, deblended) - no CS excess at the S (AGN host) nucleus or at the Bridge. (ii) SO: 8_8-7_7 not detected, SO/HCO+ 4-3 <0.011 (N), <0.014 (S), <0.013 (Bridge) (3 sigma; <0.019/0.024/0.022 at 5 sigma) at 4.3x2.8"; SO 6_5-5_4 (251.826) / HCO+ 3-2 (K): N <0.014-0.016 (1.7", 3 sigma), S 0.012-0.017+-0.006 (2-3 sigma at 1.7"; 4.6/3.3 sigma SO-only/with CH3OH ladder at 6" after the offset correction), Bridge 0.013+-0.006, Sblue <0.09, W <0.05: tentative, not S-specific, not >5 sigma anywhere; SO2, 34SO, SiS, NS undetected. These are consistent with Harada's N SO 219.949/HCO+ = 0.026 for Tex<~25 K. (iii) SiO (6-5, 8-7) is not in the data; Harada's SiO 2-1/HCO+ 1-0 is 0.03 at N and S and enhanced (0.06) only at OS/C. (iv) CH3OH (254.015, 11.6 sigma at 1.7" at the Bridge; 4.9 sigma at W): CH3OH/HCO+ 3-2 = 0.041+-0.004 (Bridge), 0.071+-0.014 (W), 0.068+-0.029 (Sblue, 2.3 sigma), 0.011+-0.006 (S), <0.022 (N, 3 sigma): enhanced by 2-7x off the nuclei - the same sense as Harada's CH3OH/HCO+ enhancement at OS (0.46 vs N 0.064 in 241.8/HCO+ 3-2; 8.6x in 96.7/HCO+ 1-0) and at the tidal arms, so CH3OH is the one chemistry tracer that differs between regions; with the low rotational temperature of the Xb55 J=1-3 E blend (Trot<~11 K, Q12; N 0.93, S 1.33 Jy/beam km/s in 9.4x6.3") the methanol is cold and extended (weak-shock/non-thermal desorption, not a hot nuclear shock), and CH3OH 254/CS 7-6 rises from 0.16 (N) to 0.5-0.6 (S, Bridge) in a matched 4.3x2.8" beam like Harada's CH3OH/CS (0.38 N, 0.94 S). A compact (<0.5") SO-rich or CH3OH-rich core is not excluded (Xb4b SO/HCO+ <0.03-0.07). Resolution: the data separate N, S, Bridge and Sblue at 0.25-1" for HCN/HCO+ 3-2 but only at 4.3x2.8" or worse for CS 7-6 and SO 8-7, so the CS and SO ratios are region-averaged over the nuclei, not nucleus-by-nucleus.
results.uncertainty: as in the component entries; ratios 15-25%, limits 3 sigma from zero with empirical noise, systematic offset +-0.13 Jy/beam km/s in CS

results.quantity: Which origin fits the red wing over the whole nuclear/Bridge region: S counter-lobe, N red-only flow, or Bridge streaming? (likelihood-type comparison, same apertures)
results.target: red wing map +180..320, r=1" apertures on a 1" grid, 291 points, HCN and HCO+
results.value: Null M0 (core-scaled leakage + nuclear wings at N,S): chi2 494 (HCN), 486 (HCO+) for 291 points. Adding ONE localized component: S axis (PA 173-193 from S) -> r=3.10" (602 pc), amplitude 0.236, dchi2 -119, dBIC -96 (HCN); HCO+ r=3.25", dchi2 -68, dBIC -46. A free-position N-flank component (<=2.5" of N) converges to the same place (2.0" S of N, 3.1" N of S): it is not N-centred, so the N-only hypothesis is only viable as an extremely one-sided flow pointing at S (PA 182 from N), which is what is observed for no other N feature: the counter-direction of the M18 North-OF-Blue lobe (PA 111+-20 from N) gains nothing (dBIC +9 HCN, +15 HCO+, i.e. rejected), and the red wing 1.85" N of N / at PA 111 is -0.006/+0.005 (HCN), ~0 (HCO+): no red wing on N's far side. Bridge strip N-S (uniform amplitude): dchi2 -75 / -45 (HCN), dBIC -63 vs -96 for the localized component (HCO+ strip -34 vs -46): the localized clump is preferred in HCN by dBIC ~33 (strong), HCO+ is ambiguous (dBIC 1); a Bridge strip fitted between the nuclei collapses to a width of 0.1-0.2" (i.e. a clump), so the Bridge-streaming alternative is only distinguished by needing +250 km/s against local gas (core peak velocity -1 km/s, range -67..+34, s104b) and a one-sided (red-only) signature. Profile likelihood of a point component along the S-N axis peaks at +3.3" N of S (dchi2 -113 HCN, -63 HCO+), 1.5" at -16/-5, 4.2" at -38/-33, nothing near N (5.1"). NON-DISCRIMINATING observables (identical for the three hypotheses with these data): collinearity of S, ridge and N (PA 183-189 vs 178-185), equal |v| to the lobe (258 vs 249 km/s), and HCN/HCO+ (ridge 1.27 vs lobe 1.57, T_b, 1.05"). DISCRIMINATING in favour of a S-axis localized feature: the position (3.3" N of S, 2.0" from N, not at either nucleus), the absence of red wing at N's far side, the red wing at N core 10 being only 0.09 (a N red-only flow would be strongest at N), and the one-sidedness (no blue at the ridge). Against a pure counter-lobe: radius 1.7x the lobe (3.3" vs 1.9"), narrow profile peak vs the lobe's falling wing, lower r31 (see r31 entry; 2 sigma HCN, 0.9 sigma HCO+: not significant). Literature: Pereira-Santaella+2024 (JWST CO v=1-0) see the S outflow above and below the disk (bipolar collimated outflow from the AGN) but only within r~250 pc (<1.3"), so it supports bipolarity at small radius and says nothing on 640 pc. VERDICT: undecided between a S counter-lobe and an unrelated/asymmetric red feature; the S counter-lobe is the more probable of the three (localized on the S axis, N-flank and N-direction tests fail, Bridge streaming needs +250 km/s one-sided), probability ~55-65%, not established.
results.uncertainty: verdict probabilistic (~55-65% counter-lobe); dBIC from Gaussian noise with sigma=0.027, grid points not strictly independent

results.quantity: Q9: net answer - is the off-nuclear (Bridge/W) CH3OH enhancement real, what is its excitation, and is the Q-branch excess real (check of team-a p0001)
results.target: N, S, Bridge, W, Sblue (Xb55, Xb4f, Xb4d)
results.value: (1) Is the 'Q-branch excess' real? Not reproducible as excess. In the channel-space joint fit of the five Q lines (J=1-5) to the Xb55 spectra at N and S (s18, HCO+ template, 1.3x correlation-inflated rms), optically thin LTE at 8-10 K gives chi2=285 (N) / 303 (S) for ~400 channels (null 555 / 802): the blend + J=4,5 non-detections are consistent with a single cold Tex. The chi2=53/6 dof of p0001 comes from fitting integrated single-line windows: their own table (N, Xb55) has J=5 -0.37+-0.08 Jy/beam km/s (-4.4 sigma), J=7 -0.21+-0.09, J=6 -0.11+-0.08, J=4 -0.07+-0.12, i.e. negative amplitudes that no emission model fits, plus a blend of 2.23 at the high-baseline end of our range; both come from the linear baseline in +-450 km/s windows near the spw ramp. With the blend at its constant-baseline value (0.5-1.1) the 1.6x 'excess' disappears (factor 2 swing). Weak maser or unmodelled blend is not needed. Individual J=1,2,3 amplitudes are degenerate (overlap of 20 and 70 km/s vs 150 km/s width); only their sum is measured (our own s17 per-J chi2 19.8/28.9 for 3 dof has the same degeneracy; do not read it as an excess). (2) Matched-beam contrast: region-integrated CH3OH blend/HCO+ 2-1 (K km/s, Xb55 aperture) = N 0.050 (0.013-0.090), S 0.047 (0.027-0.064), Bridge 0.051 (0.022-0.073), W 0.063 (0.033-0.073): equal within errors at all four positions. At 9" the beam contains N, S and the Bridge, so Xb55 cannot test N-vs-off-nuclear contrast; the 'off-nuclear enhancement' (0.04-0.07 Bridge/W vs N<0.022, S<0.03 at 1-4") is a 1-4" statement from the 254 line in Xb4d/Xb47-matched beams (p0016, report entries above) and rests on a single transition. The 254 line is recovered at the Bridge at the matched beam (Xb4d 0.46 vs Xb4f 0.60, ratio 0.77+-0.3), so the contrast is not a resolved-out artefact, but its size at the nuclei is limited by CH3OH being extended while HCO+ is compact: ratios taken at the HCO+ peaks are diluted. (3) Kinematics: CH3OH 254 centroid minus HCO+ 3-2 in the same pixel: S +16+-5, Bridge +10+-7 (Xb4f), +7+-2 (Xb4d Bridge), Sblue +43+-23 km/s (2 sigma): the CH3OH moves with the HCO+ at the systemic velocity, no outflow-velocity offset; NS 253.968 is excluded (-38..-47 km/s expected). Xb55 blend FWHM 142-153 km/s (three overlapping lines; intrinsic ~110-130 km/s) similar to HCO+. Net: the off-nuclear CH3OH is real as a line (4-6 sigma per channel in Xb55, 9.9 sigma matched filter at the Bridge in Xb4d, two transitions in two bands), cold (Trot ~10 K, 6-18 K at S; Bridge >7 K), extended on >1" scales; the N/S non-detections and Bridge/W enhancement are single-transition and ~3-4 sigma, so medium confidence. p0001's unexplained Q-branch excess and chi2=53/6 are not confirmed: they trace the baseline choice, not excitation.

results.target: Xb55 spw22 (and spw16/18/20 as controls), N, S, Bridge, E1, W, E2, Sblue peak pixels
results.value: The negative ramp at the low-frequency edge of Xb55 spw22 (163.244 GHz; first ~100 channels of 1.953 MHz, ~200 MHz, -3.5 to -5 mJy/beam in the first 10 channels at N, S, Bridge, relaxing roughly linearly to ~0 at channel ~140-170, where the CH3OH blend starts at ch~120) is a CONTINUUM-PROPORTIONAL, EDGE-LOCALISED residual of the pipeline continuum subtraction, not emission and not a property of the sky. Evidence (Xb55 pbcor peak-pixel spectra, noise 2.1 mJy/beam per channel, x1.3 for channel correlation): (a) amplitude over ch 0-30 vs continuum (line-free cont image, 14.3/12.7/14.9/6.9/4.4/-0.4/-0.5 mJy/beam at N/S/Bridge/E1/W/E2/Sblue) fits -0.21+-0.02 x continuum (through origin; chi2 23/6 with E1 an outlier, ~0 at E1); over ch 0-100 -0.157+-0.011 x continuum (chi2 16/6); zero at the continuum-free E2 and Sblue. (b) it exists only at the low-frequency edge: the high-frequency edge of spw22 is 0.0+-0.03 x continuum in the same pixels, and spw16 and spw20 (both edges) are 0+-0.04 x continuum in the same pixels, with the same continuum. (c) Same sign and size at the low edge of spw18 (-0.10 to -0.15 x continuum over the first ~80 channels, stacked N/S/Bridge), so it is spw-specific, not position-specific. (d) The sky-frequency overlap of spw20 (low edge) and spw22 (high edge), 164.54-165.11 GHz, agrees (spw22-spw20 = +0.14+-0.44, +0.13+-0.40, +0.11+-0.51 mJy at N/S/Bridge), so the baseline is not a sky feature; the ramp is not covered by any other spw. Interpretation: an amplitude roll-off of the continuum at the spw edge (bandpass/edge response) that the low-order continuum model of the delivered products does not follow leaves -(15-25)% of the continuum as a negative residual; since it scales with the continuum and is absent at other edges it is a continuum-subtraction residual caused by the edge response, and its amplitude at the CH3OH blend depends on how it is extrapolated across the line (ch 120-190). It is not a CH3OH red wing (negative, and it scales with continuum).
results.uncertainty: ramp/continuum -0.21+-0.02 (ch 0-30), -0.157+-0.011 (ch 0-100); stat per channel 2.1 mJy/beam

results.quantity: Q23: bias of HCN/HCO+ 2-1, 3-2, 4-3 integrals, HCN/HCO+ ratios and ladder ratios from the continuum-proportional spw low-edge ramp
results.target: Xb55, Xb4f, Xb47 (and Xb4d, Xb4b) at N, S, Bridge, W, (E1, E2)
results.value: Round-2 result (velocity convention corrected: radio velocity, the LOW-frequency spw edge is the RED (+v) side, so the ramp is a red-side deficit that runs into the red wing of the +-350 km/s window). The ramp biases the ladder integrals and ratios by less than 1 sigma at N, S, Bridge, but for HCN 4-3 the raw integral is LOW by ~+3..+10% if the ramp persists under the red wing. Evidence the ramp exists in the ladder spws (peak pixel, N+S+Bridge stack, amplitude as fraction of continuum): Xb55 spw18 (HCO+ 2-1) -0.13..-0.15+-0.03; Xb4f spw18 (HCN 3-2) -0.10+-0.03; Xb47 spw16 (HCN 4-3) -0.08+-0.02 (delta-chi2 ~19 vs no ramp); controls consistent with zero: Xb55 spw16 (HCN 2-1) -0.03+-0.02, Xb4f spw16 (HCO+ 3-2) -0.05+-0.02 (marginal), Xb47 spw18 (HCO+ 4-3) -0.01+-0.01; Xb4d/Xb4b no ramp. Direct test (observed blue[-600..-420] minus red[+420..+600] level, mJy/channel, N+S+Bridge, vs the fitted continuum-scaled ramp model, in-sample / leave-one-region-out): Xb55 spw18 +2.15+-0.53 observed vs +1.62 / +1.61 predicted (chi2 2.4/3 vs 18/3 for no ramp); Xb4f spw18 +0.87+-0.39 vs +1.28 / +1.36 (2.6/3 vs 5.7/3); Xb47 spw16 +1.06+-0.66 vs +1.95 / +1.83 (2.3/3 vs 4.1/3); no-ramp controls: Xb55 spw16 +0.41+-0.40 vs 0.03, Xb4f spw16 -0.28+-0.52 vs +0.71, Xb47 spw18 +0.02+-0.53 vs 0; Xb4d/Xb4b HCN 3-2 -0.00+-0.11 / -0.05+-0.06. The red-side deficit is therefore the ramp itself (right sign, right spws, continuum-proportional at N/S/Bridge), not an independent baseline error; the previous reading (blue-side ramp, 'opposite sign', separate 5-12% systematic) was wrong and is withdrawn. Shape: in the measured profiles (s146) the ramp does not die in the first ~10 channels in the ladder spws: Xb47 spw16 is a plateau of ~-0.07+-0.02 x cont out to the window start (ch 48; a MHz-scaled Xb55 empirical shape that ends by ch~45 predicts 0), Xb4f spw18 -0.10 x cont to ch ~60 (window starts ch 74), Xb55 spw18 -0.09+-0.05 at the window start (ch 76). I therefore take the ramp to extend into the red wing (triangle c0=200-400 ch) as the realistic case and the short empirical/exponential/c0<=100 shapes as the optimistic bound. Integral change when the fitted ramp is removed (E0 = s30 estimator; optimistic [short ramp] .. realistic [tri200-400]): HCN 4-3 N -1.9..+2.6..+6.6%, S -3.2..+2.8..+9.7%, Bridge -1.1..+3.9..+8.7% (stat 1.8, 3.9, 3.1%; +-7% calibration; the raw HCN 4-3 integral is too LOW, not too high: the ramp under the red wing outweighs its depression of the red baseline channels); HCN 3-2 -0.3..+1.3..+2.8% (N), +1.8..+3.3 (S), +1.1..+2.9 (Bridge); HCO+ 2-1 <=+1.4%; HCN 2-1, HCO+ 3-2, HCO+ 4-3: <=+0.5% (no ramp / outside window). Ratio shifts, optimistic .. tri400: HCN/HCO+ 2-1 0..-1.3% ; 3-2 0..+2.5% ; 4-3 N -1.9..+6.3%, S -3.2..+10.2%, Bridge -1.1..+8.4% (largest 0.95 sigma at S, the ratio error is ~10% = stat + 7% calibration per line); HCN T43/T32 N -1.6..+3.7%, S -2.9..+6.2%, Bridge -0.7..+5.7% (<=0.6 sigma); HCN T21/T32 0..-3.2%; HCO+ ladder ratios <=0.5%. The N/S contrast in HCN T43/T32 (p0022) changes by <=2.5% (ramp scales with continuum at both). No ladder result moves beyond 1 sigma; the HCN 4-3-based ratios should be quoted as raw +4+-4% (N), +6+-5% (S), +6+-4% (Bridge) up, i.e. HCN/HCO+ 4-3 and T43/T32 are biased low in the old tables. Ramp-immune cross-check (baseline from the blue side only, v<-450, same +-350 window; the ramp under the red wing is NOT removed by any baseline choice, only the template can address it): E1 vs s30 shifts HCN/HCO+ and ladder ratios by <=0.2 sigma everywhere except HCO+ 4-3 at S (+6.8%, a baseline structure on the blue side, not the ramp: control spw without ramp), which moves HCO+ T43/T32 at S by +6.3% (0.6 sigma) and HCN/HCO+ 4-3 at S by -5.6% (0.5 sigma). A blue-side linear baseline over -900<v<-450 is unstable (HCO+ 4-3 S 28.4 vs 20.3 Jy/beam km/s; slope noise from the long lever arm) and a +-250 km/s window changes integrals by line wings (<=3%), neither is a ramp test; the baseline-choice spread (E0/E1/E3) is <=2% for all ladder lines except HCO+ 4-3 S. W (HCN 4-3 non-detection 0.05+-0.30 Jy/beam km/s) and E1/E2 are not quoted in percent: absolute ramp shift for W <=0.03-0.1 Jy/beam km/s (<0.3 sigma); E1/E2 have too little continuum for a ramp (E1 7 mJy at Xb55: <=1 mJy ramp, <=1.5% of HCO+ 2-1). Ramp extent under the line wing (v=+250..+350 km/s, the same channels as the red ridge of p0017/p0018) is not measurable and is the dominant uncertainty; not tested on matched-beam cubes (ramp ~ fraction of beam-convolved continuum, so fractions carry over).
results.uncertainty: HCN 4-3 integral +3..+10% low (range = ramp extent under the red wing, 1-2 x the stat error, +-7% calibration); HCN 3-2 <=+3%; HCO+ 2-1 <=1.4%; ratio shifts <=0.95 sigma (HCN/HCO+ 4-3 at S), <=0.6 sigma for ladder ratios

Beam dilution (revised, see Q6r2 T_b vs scale): a Gaussian source of the measured half-max size within the 0.24" beam is diluted by only 1.2-1.35 (core filling ~0.7-0.8), but the measured T_b falls 3-8x between 49 and 250 pc (slope -0.7..-1.2), so the 1.2-1.35 describes the ~100 pc core only; the pedestal and sub-beam clumpiness is what the T_b(scale) relation measures, and T_b is still rising at the finest scale. Filling implied by the sub-thermal excitation (RADEX LVG, H2, Tbg 2.73 K, s153): the largest possible T_R is the thermalised thick value J(Tk)-J(Tbg) = 24, 54, 114 K (Tk 30, 60, 120 K), so the beam filling must be >= 0.12 / 0.05 / 0.02 (HCO+ 3-2 at S; N 0.11/0.05/0.02) and >= 0.10/0.05/0.02 (HCN N), 0.05/0.02/0.01 (HCN S). With the sub-thermal gas of the 10" fits (n ~1e5, N(HCO+) 1e15 cm-2 per 100 km/s, Tk 60 K: T_R(3-2) = 5.0 K, tau 2.4) the filling would be 0.56 (S) and with N=1e16: T_R 22 K, filling 0.13; at n=1e4 T_R falls to 0.6 K (filling>1: excluded for N<1e15). For the CO 2-1 peak T_b of 37 K at 55 pc (Brunetti+2021) HCO+ 3-2 reaches 0.075 of it in the beam (ratio of RJ temperatures; Planck-equivalent 7.4 K vs ~42 K for CO 2-1 = 0.18). Consequence: (a) the beam-averaged HCO+/HCN 3-2 brightness at 50 pc is 2-3 K RJ, 5-7 K Planck, far below any plausible Tk (30-150 K) so the emission is either sub-thermally excited (n<~1e5, consistent with the 10" ladder fits) or fills <~10% of the beam, and filling and excitation cannot be separated with one line pair (the T_b(scale) trend gives the scale dependence of filling but not the excitation); (b) the HCO+ 3-2 peak T_b of N and S agree within 3% (2.75 vs 2.81 K) while HCN differs by a factor 2 (2.46 vs 1.18 K): the N/S contrast is in HCN/HCO+, not in the HCO+ brightness; ladder comparisons across beams (Q3) should adopt a beam filling of >~0.1-0.5 rather than 1.
results.uncertainty: T_b +-0.07-0.13 K statistical per channel-boxcar peak (3%-10%), +5% flux scale (HCN-vs-HCO+ same OUS), peak-pixel T_b is biased high by ~0.3 sigma_3ch (~0.05 K) by the max over channels; filling lower limits are factor-of-2 sensitive to the Tk choice and the RADEX LVG geometry; the filling values at fixed (n,N) are a table, not a fit

results.quantity: Q6r2: peak T_b of HCO+ and HCN 3-2 versus beam size, 55-250 pc (dilution relation and test of a smooth medium)
results.target: N, S, Bridge, E1, E2; HCO+ 3-2 and HCN 3-2
results.value: Peak T_b(RJ) [K] at native 0.24" (49 pc) / 55 pc / 120 pc / 250 pc [Xb4d-beam 0.93x0.74"; Xb4d native], statistical error 0.01-0.09 K: HCO+ N: 2.75 / 2.32 / 1.14 / 0.69 (Xb4d-beam 0.91, Xb4d native 1.04); slope -0.82; HCO+ S: 2.81 / 2.49 / 1.20 / 0.49 (Xb4d-beam 0.85, Xb4d native 0.91); slope -1.04; HCO+ Bridge: 1.87 / 1.75 / 1.13 / 0.56 (Xb4d-beam 0.89, Xb4d native 0.94); slope -0.71; HCO+ E1: 2.02 / 1.92 / 1.44 / 0.52 (Xb4d-beam 1.02, Xb4d native 1.03); slope -0.81; HCO+ E2: 2.04 / 1.67 / 0.64 / 0.27 (Xb4d-beam 0.47, Xb4d native 0.50); slope -1.20; HCN N: 2.65 / 2.10 / 1.04 / 0.50 (Xb4d-beam 0.83, Xb4d native 0.87); slope -1.00; HCN S: 1.18 / 1.04 / 0.54 / 0.19 (Xb4d-beam 0.35, Xb4d native 0.29); slope -1.10; HCN Bridge: 1.13 / 1.01 / 0.60 / 0.28 (Xb4d-beam 0.46, Xb4d native 0.48); slope -0.84; HCN E1: 0.75 / 0.68 / 0.40 / 0.13 (Xb4d-beam 0.28, Xb4d native 0.30); slope -1.04; HCN E2: 0.74 / 0.63 / 0.30 / 0.12 (Xb4d-beam 0.21, Xb4d native 0.22); slope -1.07. Result: in every region and both lines the peak T_b falls by a factor 3.3-7.6 (HCO+: N 4.0, S 5.7, Bridge 3.3, E1 3.9, E2 7.6; HCN: N 5.3, S 6.2, Bridge 4.0, E1 5.8, E2 6.2) from 49 to 250 pc, i.e. T_b ~ theta^-0.7..-1.2 (an unresolved point source would give -2, a smooth medium 0). The 3.4x drop at S from 0.25" to 1" found by the reviewer is reproduced (0.85 K at the Xb4d beam from 2.8 K). Validation: Xb4b smoothed to the Xb4d beam agrees with the independently imaged native Xb4d to 0-15% (ratio Xb4d/smoothed 1.00-1.15 for 9 of 10 cases, i.e. a modest <=15% loss of extended flux in Xb4b; 0.81 for the faint HCN S). Interpretation: the dense gas at 50 pc is NOT a smooth medium of constant brightness (cf. Brunetti+2021: no trend of surface density, T_b and sigma between 55 and 120 pc in CO 2-1, i.e. smooth gas down to 55 pc): between 55 and 120 pc our T_b already drops by 1.5-2.6x (HCO+ N 2.3->1.1, S 2.5->1.2, E2 1.7->0.64 K) and the 3-2 dense-gas tracers are concentrated in cores of ~0.35-0.55" (70-110 pc) on a fainter (0.3-0.9 K RJ) 1.5-2" pedestal. Beam-core model T_b(theta)=Tc d^2/(d^2+theta^2)+Tp w^2/(w^2+theta^2) (w=1.8" pedestal fixed, 5 beams incl. Xb4d-beam, errors max(stat,3%)): well-constrained only for S HCO+ (d=0.35", Tc 3.5 K, Tp 0.37 K, chi2 0.2/2 dof: filling of the core in the 0.24" beam 0.68, i.e. the beam-averaged 2.8 K RJ is only 20% below the core-resolved brightness) and the HCN Bridge/E1/E2/S fits (d 0.34-0.55", Tc 0.9-1.4 K, filling in the 0.24" beam 0.65-0.8); N is degenerate (HCO+ d 0.11", Tc 11 K; HCN d 0.26", Tc 3.7 K, chi2 10): the core+Gaussian-pedestal form does not describe N (plateau in the radial profile), so for N only the lower limit Tc>=2.8 K (HCO+) / 2.65 K (HCN) and the empirical slope -0.8..-1.0 are quoted. Consequence for beam filling: (i) the sentence "dilution is only 1.2-1.35" holds only for the core within the 0.24" beam, i.e. the filling of the ~100 pc core is ~0.7-0.8; (ii) the T_b at 250 pc is only 0.13-0.3 of that at 49 pc, i.e. the beam-averaged brightness of the dense gas at 250 pc corresponds to a filling of 0.13-0.3 relative to the 50 pc cores; (iii) the 0.24->0.28" step already lowers T_b by 5-20% and no flattening is seen at the finest scale, so filling at <50 pc cannot be assessed from these data, the 5-7 K Planck-equivalent T_b is a lower limit on T_ex for any f<1 and f<1 at 50 pc remains allowed down to the RADEX lower limits of the earlier entry (0.02-0.1).
results.uncertainty: statistical per point 0.01-0.09 K (<=10%); calibration 5%; peak-position choice +-8% (HCN N); missing extended flux in Xb4b lowers the 120/250 pc points by <=15% (Xb4d/smoothed ratio) so the true slope is shallower by ~0.1; Tc/d of the core model: S HCO+ +-30%, N unconstrained

results.target: N and S nuclei, Xb4f native beam 5.72x3.54" (J=3,4); continuum at the B5 beam 8.95x5.98"; HCN and HCO+
results.value: HEADLINE (conditional, not a confirmation): the true HCN N/S T43/T32 is NOT established either way. Observed (Xb4f beam 5.72x3.54", s82) 1.262+-0.074 (HCO+ 1.164+-0.064); team-a p0022 raw ratio reproduced (1.257 Xb55 beam); their MCMC was NOT re-run. Q23 ramp: N/S x0.98+-0.025. Observed = true x D, D=(R47/R4f)_N/(R47/R4f)_S. D needed to reach unity: 1.24 (HCN), 1.14 (HCO+); independently bounded D from our Q12 relative-recovery priors is only <=1.034 (HCN), so unity is reached only with assumption-dependent scenarios. INTERVAL OF SCENARIOS, HCN N/S true (median [68%]): none (ramp only) 1.24 [1.16,1.32]; A, Q12 priors one-sided 1.22 [1.14,1.30] (2.5-3 sigma above 1); B, continuum anchor measured IN THE LINE BEAM (Xb47 and Xb4f continuum convolved to 5.72x3.54; aperture-matched; s101): continuum (47/4f)_N/(47/4f)_S = 1.15 (peak), 1.21 (point), 1.23 (r<1.5"), 1.17 (r<2.5") (mean 1.19, aperture sd 0.04; the 8.95x5.98" beam of the previous round gave 1.14/1.21/1.01/0.99 because that beam blends N and S 5.1" apart), anchor error taken 0.10 (>= aperture spread, registration, alpha) -> true N/S 1.00-1.07 depending on aperture, aperture mean 1.04 [0.92,1.17] (dalpha sd 0.3: 1.0-1.07 with 68% +-0.16); C, team-a physical uv model (not re-run) 0.97 [0.87,1.09]. Range of central values 0.97-1.24; scenarios A and B pooled WITHOUT C: wA=0.25/0.5/0.75 -> 1.10 [0.92,1.25] / 1.16 [0.97,1.27] (P>1 0.80) / 1.19 [1.06,1.29] (P>1 0.90): the pool is a weight judgement, not a likelihood combination, and the "<1 sigma, consistent with unity" statement of the previous round is withdrawn. BRIDGE CONTROL (HCN, same continuum anchor, s101): observed S/Bridge 0.99+-0.11, N/Bridge 1.25+-0.13. The anchor that removes N/S would make N/Bridge true 1.21 [1.05,1.39] and S/Bridge 1.14 [0.98,1.32] (P>1 0.8-0.9): i.e. it does not make the nuclei equal to the (extended) Bridge, it just moves the excess from N-over-S to both nuclei over the Bridge. If recovery depended simply on source extension, S and Bridge (both extended) would be filtered alike and the observed S~Bridge, N>both pattern would stand; if the continuum 47/4f ratio traces recovery, S/Bridge should be ~1.14 (1.4 sigma over the observed 0.99). The data cannot choose: the pattern is N-specific (N compact, steeper/different continuum alpha, or a real excitation difference) or an N,S,Bridge-dependent recovery. Xb4d (0.94x0.74") J3 smoothed to the Xb4f beam vs Xb4f J3 (s102): S(4f)/S(4d smoothed) HCN N 1.16, S 1.36, Bridge 1.17 (HCO+ 1.17, 1.30, 1.20): Xb4d loses 3-2 flux, S more than N or Bridge, so S is the more extended / more filtering-prone source (supports the sign of the one-sided prior) but this bounds Xb4d, not the Xb4f 3-2 or Xb47 4-3 recovery, so it does not bound D. Tbg / IR pumping: T43/T32 ratio of ratios is a data ratio, independent of Tbg; Tbg enters only the Tk conversion. Existing fits (s73/s74): Tbg 5 K S ladders Tk 20-80 K (dchi2(80)=3.1), N 65-150 K; Tbg 10 K S 20-30 K only, N 30-100 K, i.e. higher Tbg widens, not closes, an N-S Tk gap in that 8-datum fit; Tbg>5 K is not supported (beam-averaged dust Tbg,eff 3.0-3.7 K, Q16); pumping weakly constrained. N/S Tk ratio from the four ladders 1.3-1.6 [0.7-2.7], P(Tk_N>Tk_S)=0.6-0.67: not significant (team-a extended-gas T_N/T_S 1.2 [0.96,1.43]). WHAT WOULD DECIDE IT: visibility-level (matched uv-range) imaging of J=3 and J=4 on the common baseline range (>=~15-30 m, where Xb47 and Xb4f overlap) for N and S; or a measurement of Xb47/Xb4f recovery from a model of the extended emission using the visibilities, rather than image-plane priors.

results.quantity: Q27: effect of a free / prior-bounded beam-filling factor (shared across lines) and of p0026's T_b(scale) on the 10" HCN/HCO+ 2-1,3-2,4-3 RADEX single-zone fits (n, Tk, tau, eta)
results.target: N, S, Bridge apertures (10" circular beam, Xb55/Xb4f/Xb47 smoothed); p0012/p0009 comparison; the 6.5" beam cannot hold J=2-1 (Xb55 beam 8.6x6.0")
results.value: RESULT (round 2, s108 with tau labels corrected; N, S, Bridge in 10" circular apertures, flat log Tk 10-300 prior): the Tk lower limit of Q3r4/p0011 (Tk>~50 K) survives a free, prior-bounded or separate beam-filling factor; what filling changes is the opacity, not the temperature sign. (1) Shared eta prior (s104, unchanged numbers): eta=1 fixed log n 4.88 [4.62,5.12], Tk 199 [141,251] K (chi2 1.3 vs profile minimum 0.1, not excluded); flat ln eta [1e-3,1]: Tk 141 [56,223], eta 0.020 [0.010,0.13] (N; S, Bridge within 0.1 dex); [0.05,1]: Tk 199 [141,251], eta 0.19. ln Z 2.2 / 4.7 / 4.9 / 4.2 (Bayes factors 8-15, prior dependent, with flat-n prior 3-5): sub-thermal excitation (eta~1, thin, tau~0.1) and dilution (eta~0.02, tau(HCN 3-2) ~6 [0.2,57]) remain degenerate. (2) Floor from p0026 T_b(scale) (T_R,model(3-2, HCN and HCO+) >= f T_b), sensitivity to line width w (100-250 km/s) and f (0.7-1.0): 250-pc floor (0.50/0.69 K N): Tk 126 [50,199] at w=150,f=0.85, 112-126 over the whole w,f grid, P(Tk>50)=0.84-0.86 (N; S 141 [63,223], 0.90-0.92; Bridge 126 [50,199], 0.85-0.87), eta 0.015-0.017 N: insensitive. 49-pc floor (2.65/2.75 K N): the result depends on w,f: N Tk 100 [45,178] (w=100,f=0.7) -> 71 [32,141] (150, 0.85, s104) -> 35 [25,63] (250, 1.0), P(Tk>50)=0.81 -> 0.68 -> 0.29, eta 0.013 -> 0.010 -> 0.007, tau(HCN 3-2) 18 -> 38 -> 119; S Tk 126 [56,223] -> 112 [50,199] -> 63 [35,126], P(Tk>50)=0.89 -> 0.86 -> 0.67; Bridge 126 -> 100 -> 71, P 0.85 -> 0.83 -> 0.73. Direction: the 0.24" peaks are beam-limited (HCO+ sources are 0.5" deconvolved) so their T_b is a LOWER bound on the intrinsic brightness; the floor therefore gives an UPPER limit on eta (<=0.01-0.02 N, S 0.011-0.019, Bridge 0.012-0.018 at 49 pc; 0.015-0.023 at 250 pc) and tau is a lower limit. (3) Separate eta_HCN, eta_HCO+ (flat ln [1e-3,1] each, also |ln q|<=ln10): N Tk 158 [71,251] (5% lower 20 K), P(Tk>50)=0.89, log n 4.75 [4.00,5.12], tau(3-2) 0.8 [0.1,14]; S 158 [79,223], 0.91; Bridge 158 [71,251], 0.89; ln Z lower by 1.2 than shared eta (-12.6 vs -11.4): no evidence for differential filling, the extra freedom only moves Tk up and lets the thin branch back in. With H13CN(4-3) (p0007 limit, tau(H13CN)<0.128 -> tau(HCN 4-3)<X x 0.128, X=HCN/H13CN 30/50/100; the label error of s104, which applied it to 3-2, is corrected): shared eta Tk 158 [89,223] / 158 [79,223] / 158 [79,223] (N), separate 178 [100,251] / 178 [89,251] / 178 [89,251], P(Tk>50)=0.92-0.95 N, S 0.93-0.96, Bridge 0.92-0.95; 5% lower limit 28-45 K (shared), 28-35 K (separate): Tk>50 K survives (P>=0.88 in every variant except the 49-pc floor with w>=200 km/s). (4) 20-30 K gas (p0012 S 1", p0009) in the 10" beam: posterior mass at Tk<=30 K 0.05 N (0.03 S, 0.05 Bridge) shared eta, 0.07 (0.06, 0.07) separate eta, 0.02-0.03 at eta=1 (prior mass 0.42): Bayes factor cold/warm 0.04-0.11 (about 1:10-25 against). Profile chi2 (best eta in [1e-3,1]) at Tk=25 K = 3.4 N, 3.5 S, 3.1 Bridge vs 0.1 at the optimum (dchi2 ~3, <2 sigma): a 25 K gas fits only as dilute (eta 0.010) and thick (tau(HCN 3-2) 10-12, n 10^5.25); for eta>=0.05 chi2(25 K)=41/37/36 and for eta>=0.3 50/49/49 (excluded; Tk<=30 min 4.3-5.0). So the 10" ladder neither confirms nor excludes a cool thick core: it excludes a cool gas that fills the 10" beam, and allows a cool core with eta~0.01 (emitting area 4e4 pc2, equivalent diameter ~235 pc, i.e. a few 0.24" core sizes at 40 Mpc, so geometrically plausible). With the 49-pc floor and w=250 the Tk<=30 mass rises to 0.29 (N): the p0012 S value and our 10" result are then compatible. They are not independent measurements (different apertures, different deblending), so the tension is Delta ln Z ~ 2-3, not a rejection. (5) Columns and masses (D=40 Mpc, mu=2.8, N(H2)=eta N(HCO+)/X, 10" beam area 4.3e6 pc2, X(HCO+)=1e-9/3e-9/1e-8): thin eta=1: Sigma 283 [224,448]/94/28 Msun/pc2 (M(10") 1.2e9/4e8/1.2e8 Msun at N; S, Bridge 1.5e9/5e8/1.5e8); baseline thick branch eta~0.02: Sigma 895 [307,6696]/298/89 (M 3.8e9 [1.3e9,2.9e10]/1.3e9/3.8e8; P(Sigma>3e3)=0.28/0.12/0.02); 49-pc floor: 3575 [655,16160]/1192/357 (M 1.5e10/5e9/1.5e9; P(Sigma>3e3)=0.53/0.30/0.05); S, Bridge similar within 0.3 dex. Independent bound: the 10"-smoothed Xb47 346.5 GHz continuum (T_b 0.006-0.007 K at N, S, Bridge) read as all dust gives Sigma <= 75/40/18 (N; Td=30/50/100 K; S 59/31/14, Bridge 77/41/19) Msun/pc2, M(10") <= 3e8/2e8/8e7 Msun (kappa_gas factor ~3, ~30% flux lost by Xb47 filtering, free-free would lower it): all branches with X(HCO+)<=3e-9 are above it by 1.2-10x; only the eta=1 thin branch (or X(HCO+)>=1e-8: Sigma 28-360) is compatible, and the 49-pc-floor branch exceeds the 3e3 Msun/pc2 nuclear peak CO Sigma (Sakamoto+2014; averaged over 10" it must be <<3e3) for X<=3e-9 in 30-53% of draws. This column/mass test therefore disfavours the thick eta~0.01 branch unless X(HCO+)>~1e-8, but cannot decide because X is unmeasured and dust kappa/Td are uncertain by >=3x; it also pushes toward high X(HCO+) in every branch. (6) Excitation vs dilution: remains degenerate; the ladder (T21/T32 ~2.6, T43/T32 ~0.34) is equally fitted by thin sub-thermal gas at n~10^4.9, Tk~150-200 K, eta~1 and by dilute thick gas (eta~0.01-0.03, tau 6-60) at Tk 50-220; corr(ln eta, log Tk)=+0.4-0.6. eta at 10" is the area filling of gas at the brightness of the compact peaks, not the 50-pc filling and not a clump area fraction. (7) Corrections: in s62/s64/s66/s104 'tau(HCN 3-2)' was F.tauH[:,1] = tau(2-1) (grid J index 0 = 1-0); tau(3-2) is larger by 1.2-3 (N baseline tau(3-2) 5.9 [0.2,57], tau(4-3) 1.0 [..]) and the s104 H13CN-limit variant (tau(3-2)<6.4) is replaced by the tau(4-3) version above (Tk 158 [79,223] instead of 178 [112,251] for shared eta): conclusions on Tk unchanged, tau values quoted earlier are tau(2-1).

results.target: S blue lobe (-320..-180 km/s, 1.85" S of S nucleus), aperture r=max(beam,0.6")
results.value: 1-0 HCN/HCO+ 0.61+-0.25 (1.5", X145), 0.59+-0.11 (2.2", X961) vs 3-2 1.39+-0.16 (1.5"), 1.24+-0.16 (2.2"): the high 3-2 lobe ratio does NOT persist in 1-0 (difference 2.6 sigma at 1.5", 3.3 sigma at 2.2", statistical only). 1.5" lobe: HCN 1-0 2.3+-0.8, HCO+ 1-0 3.8+-0.8 K km/s; 3-2 HCN 1.1, HCO+ 0.8 -> r31(HCN) 0.50+-0.18, r31(HCO+) 0.22+-0.05 (S nucleus 0.22 / 0.34): HCN 3-2 is relatively strong in the lobe, i.e. HCO+ 3-2 is weak (r31(HCO+) is the lowest of any region) and HCN r31 is the highest, but only at 2.8 sigma. The 1-0 lobe ratio equals the S-nucleus value (0.57-0.58): at 1.5-2.2" the lobe window (-320..-180) is contaminated by the blue wing of the S nucleus 1.85" away, so the 1-0 ratio cannot be distinguished from S-nucleus leakage, while the 3-2 ratio (1.2-1.4) differs from the S nucleus 3-2 (0.38) by 5 sigma even at 2.2". Weak lines: SiO, HC3N, HNC, H13CO+, H13CN, HN13C all undetected (3 sigma limits 0.6-0.8 K km/s; HNC/HCN<0.5, SiO/HCO+<0.36, uninformative). Literature: Michiyama+2018 (ApJ 868, 95; full text retrieved via lit.py) report HCO+(1-0)/CO(1-0)=0.20+-0.04 in the S outflow vs 0.08+-0.01 in the S nucleus (dense-gas fraction higher in the outflow) and R32/10(CO)=1.3+-0.2 vs 0.7; I could not retrieve a numerical HCN/HCO+ 1-0 value for the S outflow from the extracted text, so the claim of a high 1-0 HCN/HCO+ in the S outflow is not verified here. Our 1-0 ratio (0.6+-0.1-0.25) is not high; Harada+2018 give only per-nucleus values (N 0.96, S 0.645 at 1.7").

results.quantity: Q29: does adding J=1-0 (and H13CO+) to the 3-2 ladder change the N/S excitation vs abundance conclusion? RADEX Bayes factors with sensitivity
results.target: N vs S, N vs Bridge, S vs Bridge at 2.2" (X961 1-0 + Xb4d 3-2) and N vs S at 1.5" (X145 + Xb4d)
results.value: Model-free first: r31 is >= at N than S as measured (HCN 1.27, HCO+ 1.13 at 2.2") but the difference is within the 3-2 recovery bound (see r31 entry); HCN/HCO+ N/S contrast 1-0 1.47 vs 3-2 1.65 (D=1.07-1.16, 1.7 sigma incl. systematics). RADEX (LVG, one zone, common filling eta<=1, Tk<=300 K, flat priors in log n, log N, log A=N(HCN)/N(HCO+); band scales 10%/15% and 5% per-line noise): 3-2 only: all hypotheses indistinguishable (|ln BF vs free|<=0.9, except "all same" -8 to -13). Adding 1-0 (no H13CO+): N vs S ln BF vs free: same Tk,n 1.3 (2.2")/0.6 (1.5"), same A 0.0/-1.2, same A and N(HCO+) 1.0/-1.0, same everything but filling -14/-21: nothing preferred (|ln BF|<=1.3, signs flip with the assumed noise). Adding the H13CO+ ratio term (N: tau(HCO+ 1-0)=1.5 instead of 9): same Tk,n (abundance/column differ) +3.3 (sl=0.05) / +2.6 (sl=0.10); same A (excitation differs) -0.7 / +0.3; same A and N(HCO+) (excitation only) +1.0 / +2.3; common density only +2.1/+1.8; all-same -13 / +2.2. Hence ln BF(same Tk,n vs same A) = +3.9 (tight noise) to +2.3 (loose); vs excitation-only +2.3 to +0.3; unchanged if the 3-2 fluxes are multiplied by the recovery bound (f=0.5, 1: +3.1..3.2 / -0.6; excitation-only +0.2..0.6 at sl=0.05, +2.3 at sl=0.10). Across band-scale/noise settings the ordering "common excitation + different columns/abundance" > "different excitation" is kept, with factors 1.3-45 depending on the noise; it is a moderate, prior-dependent preference, not decisive. N vs Bridge: same Tk,n +3.2, same A +1.5, excitation-only +4.2 (no preference between abundance-only and excitation-only). S vs Bridge: same Tk,n +3.6, same A +1.1. Constrained physical quantities (N / S / Bridge, 2.2", with H13CO+): Tk 112 [40,251] / 199 [112,251] / 178 [71,281] K (individually poorly constrained, prior-dependent, P(Tk>50)=0.79/0.97/0.93), log n 4.4/4.25/4.25 (+-0.25), tau(HCO+ 1-0) 1.5/1.0/1.2, A=N(HCN)/N(HCO+) 4.0 [3.2,5.0] / 2.0 [2.0,2.5] / 3.2 [2.5,4.0]. The HCN/HCO+ column (abundance) ratio is ~2x higher at N than S, consistent with the isotopologue ratio (N 1.7, S<1.3). Predicted r31 under the two hypotheses are given in Q28 (two-phase grid).
results.unit: ln Bayes factor vs independent fits; K; cm-3; dimensionless
results.uncertainty: ln BF sensitivity: +-1.5 with ratio noise (per-line 3-10%), band-scale sigma (5-30%), prior; Tk 32-251 K 68% range

The HCN/HCO+ column ratio N/S (x2, 0.3 dex) stays, as does the lower N Tk, but both are driven by the 1-0 HCN/HCO+ ratio contrast and by the (1-0 vs 3-2) HCN and HCO+ line opacity, weakly. ln BF N vs S (vs free), 2.2", 1-0+3-2: same Tk,n with free columns (abundance-only) +1.02; same A, free Tk,n (excitation-only) +0.21; excitation+column only (same A and N) +1.31 (old Xb4d-based: +1.30, -0.04, +0.97); 1.5": +0.26, -0.42, -0.10 (old +0.61, -1.20, -1.04). The difference abundance-only minus excitation-only is +0.8 (2.2") and +0.7 (1.5"): at best weak (<1 in lnBF) preference for a common density/temperature with different HCN/HCO+ abundance at N vs S over a common abundance with different excitation, not decisive. A full "same everything" (filling only) is disfavoured ln BF -4.6 (2.2") and -9.8 (1.5"), far less than before (-14, -21), because the Xb4d recovery bias at S is gone. If the data are read as within 2 sigma (D=1.00+-0.04, r31 N/S=1.0), nothing in the data requires different excitation; N/S differences are in the HCN/HCO+ ratio at both J, which is an abundance (or opacity/column) signal.

results.quantity: Q35: is the N-vs-S CS excitation contrast the cause of the J-dependent sign (HCN-rich vs HCO+-poor)? CS ladder 2-1/5-4/7-6 and thin-tracer excitation at N, S, Bridge
results.target: N, S, C/Bridge; Harada 1.7" and Xb47 4.3"
results.value: CS 5-4/2-1 (K km/s, 1.7") N 0.315, S 0.202, C 0.180 -> N/S = 1.57 [1.28,1.94]; for comparison HCN 3-2/1-0 N/S 1.16 [1.00,1.34], HCO+ 3-2/1-0 N/S 0.90 [0.78,1.03] (r31 of HCN and HCO+ equal at N and S, Q34), and the thin tracers C18O 2-1/1-0 N/S 1.48 [1.25,1.74], 13CO 2-1/1-0 1.34 [1.16,1.54]. So the excitation enhancement at N is shared by CS and by the CO isotopologues (lower-density gas) and is absent in HCN and HCO+ 3-2/1-0: it is a property of the gas, not a CS peculiarity. Joint RADEX fit (common Tk, n, eta for HCN, HCO+, CS; Harada six lines + CS7-6/HCN4-3 and HCN4-3/HCO+4-3 at 4.3"): N Tk 199 [178,223] K, log n 4.50 [4.38,4.62]; S Tk 100 [63,158] K, log n 4.62 [4.38,4.88]; Bridge(C) Tk 178 [141,223], log n 4.25 [4.12,4.50]. The HCN+HCO+-only fit gives N Tk 22 [11,141], S 50 [20,112] (degenerate). CS Tex(2-1/5-4/7-6) N 11/9/17 K, S 13/8/14 K, Bridge 7/9/17 K: all strongly sub-thermal (n_crit(5-4)~1e6), Tex contrast N/S <~1.1 at 5-4 and ~1.2 at 7-6, i.e. the CS contrast is a Tk (and tau) contrast, not a Tex contrast. Test: predicted CS 5-4/2-1 from the HCN+HCO+ (Tk,n) with N(CS)/N(HCN)=0.03-1 is 0.10 [0.04,0.23] at N (observed 0.315, 1.2-3x above), 0.10 [0.05,0.22] at S (observed 0.20, consistent), 0.08 [0.05,0.13] at C (0.18). The CS ladder is hotter than HCN/HCO+ only at N (and weakly at C); best-fit chi2 of the one-gas ladder at N is 10.2 for ~0 dof (11.6 for dof 2 with the 4.3" ratios) vs 2.1/3.5 at S: a single-gas model is disfavoured at N, so the CS normalisation at N carries an excitation systematic. Consequence for the sign flip: HCO+/CS N/S 1.09 (1-0/2-1) -> 0.63 (3-2/5-4) -> 0.68 (4-3/7-6) is the CS(low J) vs CS(high J) change, at constant HCN/HCO+ (1.49, 1.92, 1.62). Absolute RADEX N(CS) is not tied to a single excitation (Tex 8-17 K) so the J=2-1 and 5-4/7-6 CS-normalised results are two different corrections of the same N-S contrast; after the joint fit the column-density ratios (next entry) are the J-free answer. RADEX check of the 4-3/3-2 hot-gas C18O 2-1/1-0 prediction (3.7-4.0 at Tk 100-200 K, n=3e4) is far above the observed 1.1-1.6 (C18O comes from lower density gas than HCN/HCO+), so the thin CO ratio is used only for the sign of the N-S contrast.
results.uncertainty: N/S excitation ratios +-0.15-0.3 (rms + 7% flux scale per line); Tk/n posterior 16-84%; Tex per-line +-3 K

results.quantity: Q35: column-density ratios N(HCN)/N(HCO+), N(CS)/N(HCN), N(CS)/N(HCO+) at N, S, Bridge and their N/S contrasts (excitation-corrected): which species departs?
results.target: N, S, Bridge(C); Harada 1.7" lines + 4.3" ratios
results.value: Adopted fit (6 lines at 1.7" + 2 ratios at 4.3"), medians [16-84%]: log N(HCN)/N(HCO+) N 0.6, S 0.4, C 0.4 (+-0.1 grid); N(CS)/N(HCN) ~0.25 [-0.6 dex, +-0.1] at all three; N(CS)/N(HCO+) 1.0 N, 0.63 S, 0.63 C. N/S contrasts: N(HCN)/N(HCO+) = 1.64 [1.31,2.09] (P>1 = 1.00); N(CS)/N(HCN) = 0.96 [0.71,1.28] (P>1=0.45); N(CS)/N(HCO+) = 1.58 [1.19,2.12] (P>1 = 0.94); i.e. N(HCN)/N(CS) = 1.04 [0.78,1.41] and N(HCO+)/N(CS) = 0.63 [0.47,0.84] (P>1 = 0.06). Bridge/S: N(HCN)/N(HCO+) 1.03 [0.83,1.32], N(CS)/N(HCN) 1.07 [0.76,1.54], N(CS)/N(HCO+) 1.11 [0.79,1.62]. Without the 4.3" ratios: N(HCN)/N(HCO+) N/S 1.65 [1.33,2.19], N(HCO+)/N(CS) N/S 0.62 [0.44,0.83]; HCN+HCO+ only: N(HCN)/N(HCO+) N/S 2.40 [1.71,3.25]. ANSWER: with CS as the reference, HCN tracks CS (N/S 1.0) and it is HCO+ whose column is lower at N by ~0.6 (2.5 sigma on the posterior; P(N/S>1)=0.06), i.e. N is HCO+-poor, not HCN-rich, in this normalisation. This conclusion rests on CS being a faithful abundance reference at N; the one-gas model fits the CS ladder less well at N (chi2 10 vs 2 at S), and a different reference (C18O 1-0, CS 2-1) gives HCN-rich (N/S 1.5-1.6) and HCO+ flat (1.0-1.1); see the normaliser entry. Thin limit, no 4-3 detection assumed: H13CN/H13CO+ 1-0 (2.2", Q29) = 0.75 [0.60,0.93] N, 0.23 [0.09,0.42] S (1 sigma, truncated >=0; 3-sigma upper 1.15), 0.94 [0.72,1.22] Bridge; N/S = 3.3 [1.7,9.0], P(N/S>1) = 0.97, 5th percentile 1.19 (S is only a 1-sigma H13CN value: weak evidence, ~2 sigma, not used in the conclusion). With a RADEX conversion N(H13CN)/N(H13CO+) = 2.9 (x/divide 1.25) x intensity ratio (Q29 s188, n=1e4-1e5) and a common 12C/13C of 30-100 (cancels): N(HCN)/N(HCO+) = 2.2 [1.6,3.0] N, 0.65 [0.24,1.3] S, 2.7 [1.9,3.9] Bridge; N/S of the column ratio 3.6 [1.3,11.8] with 0.15 dex independent isotopic-fractionation factors per species (P>1 = 0.90). This agrees with the optically-thick-corrected 12-line ratio N/S 1.6 within errors but cannot discriminate (H13CN at S is undetected). Harada+2018 give no HCN/HCO+ abundances for NGC 3256 (Table 13 is line intensities; HCN/HCO+ 1-0 = 0.96 N, 0.65 S, 0.67 C), so the comparison is with their line ratios only (reproduced). [Q39 UPDATE: on a fine continuous grid the P(>1)=1.00 / 2.5 sigma statements above are over-precise; N(HCN)/N(HCO+) N/S is ~2.1 sigma (profile likelihood) and N(HCO+)/N(CS) N/S 0.63 is only 1.6 sigma; see the Q39 entries.]
results.uncertainty: see value; grid-limited +-0.1-0.14 dex; isotopologue limits 1-sigma

results.target: N/S; 1.7" Harada peak pixels and 4.3" deblend
results.value: 346 GHz continuum N 39.3, S 21.8 mJy/beam (4.3x2.8"); free-free from H40a (Harada 1.7", N 5.68+-0.81, S 5.50+-0.81 K km/s) via the RRL/continuum LTE relation (Te 5e3-1e4, y=0.08): S_ff(346) = 2.1-4.6 (N), 2.0-4.4 (S) mJy/beam point-like, i.e. 5-12% (N) and 9-20% (S) of the continuum. Dust-only N/S = 1.88-2.00 (uncorrected 1.80; 2.33 if the ff flux in the 4.3" beam is 2x the 1.7" peak). HCO+/cont N/S 0.67 (uncorrected) -> 0.64-0.60 (ff-corrected) -> 0.52 (generous); HCN/cont 1.09 -> 1.05-0.98 -> 0.84; CS/cont 0.99 -> 0.95-0.89 -> 0.77: the correction moves everything down together, the HCN/HCO+ contrast (1.62) is unchanged, and the dust-temperature / opacity difference between N and S (S hosts an AGN) is not constrained by these data. MC injection errors replace sqrt(8): HCO+/cont N/S = 0.67 [0.56,0.78] (2.8 sigma below 1 incl. the 5% systematic; was quoted 4 sigma), HCN/cont 1.09 [0.85,1.42], CS/cont 0.95 [0.70,1.45], HCN/CS 1.10 [0.72,1.67], HCO+/CS 0.68 [0.45,0.96] (1.2 sigma), HCN/HCO+ 1.62 [1.23,2.15]; recovered bias <=5% in all scenarios (point sources, 1" resolved, 0.3" shifts, fourth component). Alternative normalisers (Harada 1.7", J-matched where possible), HCN/norm and HCO+/norm N/S: C18O 1-0: 1.48 [1.26,1.73] / 0.99 [0.85,1.16]; CS 2-1: 1.63 [1.41,1.88] / 1.09 [0.94,1.26]; 13CO 1-0: 3.62 / 2.43 (13CO is optically thick and N/S 13CO(1-0)=0.96: not a mass tracer); C18O 2-1 with 3-2: 1.16 [0.99,1.35] / 0.60 [0.52,0.70]; CS 5-4 with 3-2: 1.20 / 0.62. The flip is between 1-0 and 3-2 for every normaliser that is more excited at N (C18O 2-1/1-0 N/S 1.48, CS 5-4/2-1 1.57): HCN/HCO+ is stable (1.49, 1.92, 1.62) but HCN/norm and HCO+/norm both fall by ~1.5 when the reference line is a higher J. A J-independent reference (an optically thin column tracer measured at the same J, or a mass-weighted dust continuum) is not available. Profiles (Xb47 deblend, 100 km/s bins): HCN and HCO+ 4-3 are single-peaked at N and S with the same FWHM (200 km/s in the bin units), peak/total 0.49-0.50 (HCO+) at both nuclei, and HCN/HCO+ (K) is constant with velocity: N 0.55 (-50), 0.55 (+50); S 0.33, 0.32, 0.36 (-50..+150): no dip or velocity-dependent suppression of HCO+ at N, so self-absorption is not seen at 100 km/s / 4.3" resolution (deeper absorption in an unresolved 0.2" core cannot be excluded).

results.quantity: Q40: can the 13C isotopologue data (H13CO+ 1-0/3-2 at N from Harada 1.7") exclude the cold/dense optically thick branch of the N one-gas RADEX posterior? Effect on N(HCN)/N(HCO+) and N/S
results.target: N (1.7" peak pixel, matched 12C/13C beam); S, Bridge as supplements
results.value: RESULT (conditional): Tk<=30 K, n~10^5.4-7, optically thick solutions are DISFAVOURED, not excluded, by the matched-beam H13CO+ pair at N. Marginalised over 12C/13C (X = 22-100, log-normal prior centred 45-60, 0.2 dex or flat) and over Tk, n, N: posterior P(Tk<=30 K) = 0.002-0.006 (band-scale priors 10%/15%), 0.02-0.03 (20%/25%), 0.03-0.05 (40%/40%), vs prior mass 0.32; Bayes factor (Tk>=100 K : Tk<=30 K) ~ 15-1000 (>=15 even with loose scales). Fixed-X numbers from round 1 (dchi2 = 17 at X=40, 5.2 at X=60, -1.3 at X=90 for 10/15% band priors) are NOT a clean 13C result: decomposing dchi2(cold-hot) at X=40 gives band/eta prior 3.1, 12C HCO+ 6.6, CS 4.3, HCN 1.0, 13C pair 2.3 (total 17.2); at X=63 the prior term is 9.3 for both branches and the 13C pair 2.7 vs 1.0. The 13C 3-2/1-0 ratio alone (0.28+-0.06 stat, 0.30 fractional with band scales) does NOT discriminate (dchi2 = 0: some (n, N) reproduces it at every Tk); the discrimination comes from tying N(H13CO+) to N(HCO+) through X. The data themselves select X: lnZ(X) peaks at X~30-50 (X_N = 31-35 median for 10/15% band scales, 40-51 for 20-40%), consistent with Tang+19 (12C/13C 30-67, mean 42 in NGC 253 nuclei, 24-62 NGC 1068); at X>=80 cold and hot are indistinguishable (dchi2 ~0-3). Above conclusion therefore needs X<~60; it also rests on the one-zone model and on 3-2/1-0 relative calibration (band scales). Temperature: only a LOWER limit. Best-fit hot solutions pile up at the 300 K grid cap (log n 4.6-4.8); capping Tk at 150 K costs dchi2 = 5.6 (10/15% priors), 1.0 (20/25%), 0.4 (40/40%); cap 100 K: 8.2/1.5/0.5; cap 50 K: 10.5/2.7/2.0. Posterior P(30<Tk<100 K) = 0.02-0.25; P(Tk<=150) = 0.09-0.47. So Tk >~ 50 K is supported, 100-300 K is not distinguished from 50-100 K for loose band scales. N(HCN)/N(HCO+) (marginal over X, Tk, n): N = 3.5 [3.2,3.8] (10/15% priors) to 3.7-3.85 [3.2,4.7] (loose), S = 2.2 [1.8,2.6], N/S = 1.6-1.8 [1.3,2.4], P(N/S>1) = 0.98-0.99; profile significance remains ~2.1 sigma (not upgraded). Beam test: variant A2 (H13CN 1-0 added with an extra 30% beam-mismatch systematic) gives the same N result (P(Tk<=30)=0.001-0.018). S fits acceptably (chi2 2-8) but prefers higher X (median 65-85) than N (31-51), as expected if 12C/13C increases away from the nucleus (Tang+19) or from beam/aperture mismatch (2.2" vs 1.7" not removed). A matched-taper re-extraction was not done. [Q42 note: Q42 shows (i) adding the H13CN 4-3 ratio changes nothing (P(Tk<=30) 0.0026 vs 0.0021, X_N 33), (ii) the exclusion of the cold branch depends on the 13C data used: with Harada 1.7 arcsec peak-pixel H13CO+ (X_N~33) P(Tk<=30)=0.002 (band priors 10/15%); with 2.2 arcsec common-taper 13C/12C ratios at N (aperture 0.0231, X_N 58 [48,68]) 0.005-0.014, peak-pixel 0.04-0.06, and with the 20/25% band priors 0.2-0.5 (BF hot:cold 1-4): the cold/thick branch is disfavoured only for tight band-scale priors; (iii) the X_S/X_N contrast (85/33=2.6) shrinks to 1.3-1.8 [1.0,2.4] at one 2.2 arcsec taper (P(X_S>X_N)=0.6-0.93). See the Q42 entries]

(6) NNLS injection test (s242; simulated skies = fitted nuclear+clump model + optional unmodelled 25"/40" extended component, ACA-like uv coverage 8.7-45 m, Hogbom clean, PB, native-beam maps refitted with the same design): recovered/true R(J) for E1 and W = 1.00-1.01 (R21), 1.01-1.03 (R32), 0.92-0.93 (R43), R32/R21 recovered 1.00-1.03 for a flat truth (0.70 -> 0.70-0.73 for a true decline 0.5/0.35), nuclear R ladder exact (+-1%); E2 is biased (R32/R21 1.02-1.12; R43 recovered 0.2-0.5 of truth) and is excluded. Caveat: identical morphology in both lines, no noise, assumed uv coverage, so this validates the fit machinery, not the real uv sampling. (7) E2: 12m-only vs comb 3-2 differ by a factor 2.5 (HCO+ 1.9 vs 4.7 K km/s; R32/R10 0.18+-0.23 vs 0.63+-0.11) and the NNLS E2 is biased: E2 is DROPPED from the ladder/double-ratio claims; E1 and W 12m-only and comb agree (R32/R10 0.72 vs 0.74; 0.89 vs 0.89). results.value: RESULT: NO additional constraint. Reason (RADEX, out/q42/branch_predictions.txt): the model alpha is 0.016-0.035 in ALL branches (cold Tk<=30 K, tau(HCN 4-3)=7-19: alpha 0.019-0.033; hot Tk 211-300 K, tau 0.7-14: 0.016-0.033) because non-LTE trapping raises the 4-3 excitation of the thick HCN line, so the equal-Tex relation ratio~tau/X of Q4 does not hold; the limit is 4-7x above any prediction and a measurement would have to reach ~+-0.005 to separate branches (and the branch predictions differ by <40%). The discriminating H13CN datum is 1-0 (model H13CN/HCN 1-0: 0.12-0.13 cold, 0.085-0.09 mid, 0.04-0.06 hot vs 0.0207+-0.0034 observed at 2.2"): see Q42b. HCN 4-3 (spw16) and H13CN 4-3 (spw20) are different spws of one OUS (beams 4.14x2.70 and 4.26x2.77"), not one cube.

results.quantity: Q46 (conclusion): where do N and S sit among LIRG/AGN HCN/HCO+ values, and what it means for the diagnostic
results.value: (1) N (1-0 0.84-0.96; 3-2 0.99 at 55 pc, 0.69 at 250 pc; 4-3 0.52 at 800 pc) is ordinary for starburst-dominated LIRGs at every J: at the median of Nishimura's 3-2 sample (median 1.13) and of GOALS 1-0 (0.9-1.0), at the SB median of Izumi's 4-3 (0.48). A N core ratio of ~1.0 is NOT an AGN-like or CON-like value; ratios 1-2 are common in LIRG nuclei without luminous AGN (e.g. ESO 173-G015 1.13, NGC 5135 1.03, NGC 2369 1.49, ESO 320-G030 2.34 at 50-100 pc). (2) S (0.57-0.65; 0.44 at 55 pc; 0.29 at 800 pc) is the unusual nucleus: at the bottom of the 3-2 sample (all 21 resolved values >= 0.445, and 20/21 >0.5), below the GOALS 1-0 means, and 'starburst-like' on the 4-3 diagram, although it hosts the AGN. (3) The HCN/HCO+ ratio at a single J and at 50-800 pc therefore fails as an AGN diagnostic for NGC 3256 in both directions (N false-positive-looking relative to S; S false-negative), consistent with Harada+2018, Privon+2015, Nishimura+2024 (no correlation with alpha_AGN) and Ueda+2021. The cause of the N/S contrast is not decided by this literature placement: Nishimura find outflow-related ratios to be abundance-driven and shock-heated, and the ratio rises at the centres in 16 of 20 galaxies (median resolved/global 1.14; N core/blend 2.25 is a large but not unique example). (4) Caveats: beams are not matched (our 55-250 pc/800 pc vs 50-420 pc and 0.5-18"); single-nucleus aperture definitions differ; classification of N as SB-dominated and S as AGN host is taken from the literature; NGC 3256 is not in the Nishimura sample.
results.uncertainty: See Q46a-d; comparisons are at ~10-30% ratio level and beams differ by factors of 2-4; only 8 published galaxies have beams <110 pc at 3-2.
