interpretation:
The survey finds that the spectral content of the dataset is dominated by only a handful of lines: HCN and HCO+ 2-1/3-2/4-3 (very high S/N at both nuclei), CS 7-6 (N 15 sigma, S 7.5 sigma, Xb47), a CH3OH J_-1-J_0 E blend in Band 5, and the blue wing of CO 3-2 at the Xb47 spw20 edge. Everything else (SO 5_6-4_5, the 254.015 GHz CH3OH line, HC3N 28-27, HC15N, SO 8_8-7_7, HCN-vib, H13CN) is absent or only marginal, so shock/chemistry diagnostics beyond CS, HCN/HCO+ ratios and CH3OH will be limits (Q4, Q5). The proposal's SO(6_5-5_4) is not in the data. The system is resolved at 0.25-1": N (double-horned, broad, extended continuum), S (compact continuum, line centre ~65 km/s blueward of systemic, narrower), a narrow Bridge component 1.4" S of N, two eastern clumps (E1, E2, redshifted 50-90 km/s), a western clump, and a blue-shifted blob (Sblue) 3" S-SW of S with a broad (120-230 km/s) blue-shifted profile and a blue wing; the S nucleus itself has a 4-9% blue wing. These match the picture of a dense-gas outflow near the S nucleus, but the high-velocity channels are outside the clean mask, so wing fluxes are residual-included image fluxes (flux-scale systematic +25%/-10%, Q2r2; not lower limits). N and S are cleanly separable at Bands 6-7 (beam minor axes 2.7-3.5" << 5.2") and only partially in Band 5. HCN/HCO+ at matched J is already a regional discriminator (N 0.6-1.0, S 0.4-0.5 at J=3-2); this is handed to Q1 together with matched-beam convolution. The delivered mfs/cont images are line-free. ROUND 2: The S blue wing and the elongated (~2", ~0.4 kpc) blue-wing structure south of S are real (8-19 sigma vs empirical noise, reproduced by an independent array, not a sidelobe copy of S/N); this is the main dense-gas outflow candidate in the data (the S blue lobe; the red feature between S and N is a second, unassigned candidate, see Q2r2) and supports regional comparisons for S vs its lobe, with residual-included image fluxes (+25%/-10% flux-scale systematic, not lower limits). N and S have different line-centre velocities (N-S +71 km/s), so a single systemic velocity is not appropriate. Of the weak lines only CH3OH (J=1-3 E blend, cold/sub-thermal, Trot<~11 K) and probably HOC+ 2-1 (HCO+/HOC+~37-50, N+S blend) are secure; SO 5_6-4_5 (blended with CH3OH) and HC3N are unconfirmed at the 2-4 sigma level against baseline scatter; the former '253.9 GHz feature' is CH3OH 2(0)-1(-1)E (254.015 GHz), detected at the Bridge (off-nuclear) with Tex~10 K (8-21 K) from the ratio to the J=1-3 blend. Continuum spectral index alpha(B5-B7)~1.5+-0.2 once beams and aperture are matched. Q1 (HCN/HCO+ at matched J, round 2): HCN/HCO+ is lower at the AGN-hosting S nucleus than at N at every J (3-2 at 0.25": N 0.97-1.03, S 0.43-0.48; at 0.94": 0.86-0.88 vs 0.40; 6.5" blended 0.54 vs 0.39; deblended S/N 0.7+-0.2 at 2-1, 3-2 and 4-3), so there is no HCN/HCO+ enhancement at the S nucleus (agreeing with Harada+2018). The N ratio rises smoothly inward (0.39 at 2-3" to 0.97 at r<0.25"), the S ratio is flat at 0.37-0.43 from 0.25" to 3": a compact HCN-bright core in N, not S. R falls ~25% per J step at 6-10" (within-band; ladder flux slopes carry 25-35% cross-band systematics). Disk: only J=2-1 gives a usable off-nuclear ring (8-12": 0.49+-0.03(+-0.1 sys) vs 0.56 inside 8"); the earlier 0.30 was a negative-bowl artefact; at 3-2 and 4-3 the annuli beyond 8" are unusable. The one enhancement candidate is the blue-wing blob 1.9" S of S: HCN/HCO+ 1.4 (68% 1.1-1.8) at -400..-150 km/s vs 0.55 at the same position's core (R_wing>R_core at >3 sigma, window-robust), rising with blueshift, but the independent Xb4b replication gives 0.86+-0.25 and R_wing>1 is not established (tentative). With 3-2 alone excitation (n>=1e7 or T) and abundance (x2.6) are degenerate; an enhancement would resemble shock chemistry (Nishimura+2024). Q1 (HCN/HCO+ at matched J): the ratio at matched beam is lower at the AGN-hosting S nucleus than at N at every J (3-2 at 0.25": N 1.03, S 0.48; at 6.5": 0.54 vs 0.39; 4-3 at 6.5": 0.43 vs 0.32; deblended S/N ~0.6-0.75 at 2-1, 3-2 and 4-3), and falls ~25% per J step everywhere (midpoint 0.58, 0.45, 0.33 at 10"), so there is no HCN/HCO+ enhancement at the S nucleus, agreeing with Harada+2018. The only enhancement candidate is the blue-wing blob (see above): R_wing>R_core is robust, R_wing>1 is not replicated; team-a's full-window 0.75+-0.06 is a core-dominated window of the same data (injection tests show no peak-pixel bias), and team-a p0004 independently agrees on N/S, the 2-1 disk ratio (0.47-0.50 vs 0.56-0.62) and the wing. The N-nucleus ratio >1 at 0.25" is a compact HCN-bright core. Ladder ratios alone allow A=N(HCN)/N(HCO+) from <1 (n>=3e6) to ~4 (n~1e4-1e5): abundance versus excitation is undecided without H13CN. Q4 (opacity, absorption, HCN-vib): H13CN 4-3 lies on the blue wing of CO 3-2 and is not separable; with an explicit wing model HCN/H13CN(4-3) > 8 (N), > 4 (S) at the 4" beam, i.e. the beam-averaged HCN 4-3 is not extremely thick (tau < ~4-13 for 12C/13C 30-100) but no 12/13 or opacity measurement is possible; the abundance-ratio window 30-100 is not tested. HCN v2=1f is undetected (< 2-5% of HCN v=0 at the N core, < 3-9% at S), so IR pumping cannot produce the N-core HCN excess (the 1e partner blended with HCN contributes < 5%). Continuum absorption is impossible (T_cont 0.18-0.59 K vs T_line 1.5-1.9 K, Tex >> 3 K) and the S nucleus shows flat R(v) and identical HCN/HCO+ widths: no HCO+ self-/continuum absorption, so the S deficit (R=0.43) is real. The compact N core (R 0.98, peak T_b 1.5 K) is either an abundance enhancement (A~4 vs ~1.6 outside, thin) or optically thick saturation (needs N(HCN) >~ 5e16 cm-2 per 150 km/s and filling <~ 0.05); the data cannot separate them (broader HCN core by 4-8%, ~2 sigma, hints at some opacity). Q4 round 2: (1) The N-core 'HCN broader than HCO+' (ratio 1.085+-0.015 stat) is not significant against the spatial scatter of the ratio in the region (median 1.036, 16-84% 0.98-1.09, 190 apertures) and a spatial-weights+velocity-gradient model predicts 1.00 (HCN narrower), so it is withdrawn as an opacity hint; the same applies to the R(v) pattern and the 3 km/s centroid offset. (2) The T_b ratio at 0.25" (N 0.94, S 0.42) is satisfied by both the saturated branch (tau>=3 in both lines, eta 0.01-0.75, N(HCN)>~6e15 cm-2 per 150 km/s) and the thin branch (A=N(HCN)/N(HCO+)~1-6, median 1.8 vs 0.56 at S); it does not separate opacity from abundance at N, but it excludes equal-Tex saturated lines at S, where HCN must have Tex~half that of HCO+ and/or a column below HCO+ (A<1). (3) The H13CN limit is validated by injection-recovery (conservative, bias<=0.013) but the data are only sensitive to alpha>~0.06-0.1 (tau>~2-11 for 12C/13C=30-100); the thick-core bound is a band: tau_core<~4-8 (f3=0.36), 3-6 (f3=0.5), 7-14 (f3=0.2) for 12C/13C=30-50, allowing tau>=10 in 52-79% of the scenarios; the core is not shown to be thick or thin. Q3 (round 4): the 10" HCN and HCO+ 2-1/3-2/4-3 ladders at the centre are fitted by sub-thermal, warm gas: Tk > ~56 K (84%; >~28 K at 95%; no upper bound, the median depends on the Tk ceiling of the prior), n < ~1e5 (97.5%; lower end set by the prior), HCN column 2-3x HCO+ at equal filling (degenerate with the HCN/HCO+ filling ratio), thick HCN (tau_HCN32 > 1 at 78%), eta ~ 0.02. These are one-zone beam averages with a 10%/band flux scale shared by all positions; the earlier tight joint result (Tk=152 K, n 4.62 [3.62,4.88]) overstated the constraint (independent calibration per position). N vs S vs Bridge is NOT testable at 10": the apertures overlap (N-S 5.1", weight 0.48), 56-72% of the 3-2 flux is shared smooth gas, and an intrinsic core contrast of 2 is diluted to 8-14% (a 2-sigma detection would need >=4), so identical 10" ladders are guaranteed and say nothing about the nuclei; they remain consistent with the 1" N/S differences. At 6.5" T43/T32 N/S is 1.10-1.16 (indicative). The only 10" contrast with power is E1 vs centre: HCN T21/T32 1.46x and T43/T32 0.48x (3.9-6.5 sigma with common calibration; HCO+ 1.18x, 0.76x at 3-5 sigma), P(Tk_E1<Tk_centre)=0.94 (HCN alone 0.91, HCO+ alone 0.64), E1 Tk<~56 K; E2 and W are unconstrained. J=1-0 intensities at 1.7" (Harada+2018, assumption-labelled) disfavour thin HCN at S (0.26->0.04) and leave N undecided; the compact components are thick with A_N/A_S~3, consistent with team-a p0009 (HCN column or excitation difference at S; n and Tk differences not required). Abundance is not measured: N(H2) is known to +-1 dex per X(HCO+), which itself spans 1 dex. A cold (10-35 K), thick or dense-thin branch is not excluded by the ladder (chi2 differences <=4) and needs a physical argument (Tk >= Tdust, CO Tb). | Q12 (round 2): the three low-resolution sets (Xb55, Xb4f, Xb47) are ACA data. Their relative filtering is NOT measured: bowl depths (3-6% of peak) are not ordered with wavelength, the cleaned-map integral is not zero (so the bowl is not a missing-flux estimator), and a forward model with cleaning does not give R55>=R4f>=R47. The loss-only extrapolation (R55/R4f 1.05-1.18 at the centre, R47/R4f 0.89-0.97) is a prior-conditional systematic budget item of <=10% at the centre, below the 10% per-band calibration; the claim that T(2-1)/T(3-2)>1 and T(4-3)/T(3-2)<<1 at the nuclei is thus a statement about calibration, not about recovery. After removing nuclear contamination, the clump E1 is compact and fully recovered by the 12-m array (Xb4d/Xb4f 1.0) while W is extended (0.3); the disk T21/T32 excess at E1 vanishes against the nuclear complex (0.96), the HCN 4-3/3-2 disk deficit (E1, W) and the HCO+ 4-3/3-2 deficit at W survive. Same-J HCN/HCO+ ratios at N,S,Bridge are robust to recovery at <=10%. Q11 (cross-team wing check, tiered): at N the HCN/HCO+ 3-2 ratio has no intrinsic velocity dependence at 0.25" (wing/core 1.0+-0.14) and the 20-40% rise at ~1" is beam/radial mixing (direct check of team-a p0005-r03/p0010 (i): confirmed); S stays at 0.4-0.6 in the wings (p0010 ii confirmed); MEASURED: Xb4d outer-blue-window HCN excess over k*HCO+ at a one-beam lobe 1.8" S of S (6.2 sigma; R_outer 1.9+-0.4 vs core 0.54; red side empty); REPRODUCED IN ONE ARRAY (Xb4b: same sign, 1.0 sigma, 2 sigma lower HCN); INTERPRETATION UNTESTED between extended HCN-rich wing, imaging effect (no azimuthal/mask/bowl signature found) and HDO blend (CH3CHO, c-C3H, l-C3H excluded); Bridge blue half not detected; N wing <~3% of the core.

Q2 (outflow separation, round 2): the S blue lobe (365 pc S of S, PA 183-194 deg, v_los -100..-400 km/s) is separable from the nuclei and cannot be beam-smeared disk rotation (velocity gradient at the lobe 30-40 km/s/arcsec vs >=340 needed; null model predicts <0.01 vs 0.30 Jy km/s observed), and it lies where the CO outflow of Sakamoto+2014 and the HCN/HCO+(1-0) South-OF-Blue of Michiyama+2018 are; the nuclear wings at S and N, by contrast, are reproducible by beam-smeared nuclear rotation plus broad lines. HCN and HCO+ broad components have different kinematics (HCN bluer, broader), so the HCN/HCO+ ratio of the lobe is window dependent (1.5 in -405..-150, 0.6-0.9 over the whole broad component, 0.42 in the narrow component; hence the Q1 'wing R=1.4' and the Q11 outer-blue excess are window values, not gas properties) and the HDO alternative for the HCN excess stays open. A non-LTE treatment (HCO+ mass 0.8-2.6e7 Msun for X(HCO+) 1e-8..3e-9, HCN-based 10x larger and requiring N(HCN)~10N(HCO+) or IR pumping) gives a dense mass M = 7.8e6 (1e-8/X(HCO+)) Msun (bracket 0.8-2.6e7 with the CO cap, up to 8e7 uncapped; a factor ~10 abundance x 3-5 excitation estimate, low confidence; the single-zone model fails the HCN 3-2/1-0 ratio, so it is not a validated description, and the often-used central 1.4e7 is only a geometric mean chosen with the CO cap), comparable with the CO outflow mass of the lobe (dense fraction 0.1-1, unconstrained), and Mdot_dense ~15-60 Msun/yr for a flow 70-85 deg from the line of sight with the CO-capped mass (3-2000 over the whole grid; scaling M v tan i/R, 1.5 dex, low confidence), comparable to the CO rate (50 X20, 40-104) and to the SFR. The red feature 1.7" S of N is a real, localised red-shifted clump/ridge at the position of Michiyama's OF-Red; it is not leakage and not a simple extension of the N wing, but its origin (S counter-lobe, N outflow, Bridge) is open. Q16 (p0012 S-nucleus temperature, round 2): the p0012 result that S is cool (20-30 K) with >=80 K excluded (dchi2 9-14) is NOT supported. It rests on the deblended S-core 4-3/3-2 ladders (HCN 0.268), a quantity the 6" data cannot measure: our re-implemented deblends give 0.23-0.58 depending on baseline, template and component choices, a forward-model ratio-field fit gives 0.19-0.72, and injection-recovery shows the method is nearly unbiased only when its assumptions hold. The matched-beam S aperture (0.357) is dominated (55-70%) by non-core gas, and p0012 own components under-predict it by 0.03-0.09 (HCN). Using any ladder vector inside the allowed range, S has Tk 25-80 K and 80/100 K are disfavoured at only dchi2 1.4-6.5 / 4.5-8.2; the hot exclusion and S<50 K are not robust. What survives only as an uncorrected image-plane contrast (downgraded by Q19, see below) is T43/T32 N/S = 1.26+-0.09 (HCN, 2.9 sigma) and 1.16+-0.08 (HCO+, 2.0 sigma) in the matched 5.7x3.5" beam, which is NOT significant after differential Xb47/Xb4f recovery (HCN 1.10 [0.93,1.25], HCO+ 1.06 [0.93,1.18]), N distinct from the Bridge (1.25+-0.13) while S is not distinguishable from the Bridge (0.99+-0.11, 0.98+-0.07). The contrast corresponds to Tk_N/Tk_S >~1 (median 1.3-1.6) or n_N/n_S up to ~3 along the Tk-n degeneracy, neither significant; p0011 and p0012 do not conflict (p0011 used circular 6.5/10" apertures that mix N and S, p0012 deblended). Absolute Tk: N 65-150 K, S and Bridge 25-100 K (one-zone, Tbg 2.7-5 K). Q16 (p0012 S-nucleus temperature, round 2): the p0012 result that S is cool (20-30 K) with >=80 K excluded (dchi2 9-14) is NOT supported. It rests on the deblended S-core 4-3/3-2 ladders (HCN 0.268), a quantity the 6" data cannot measure: our re-implemented deblends give 0.23-0.58 depending on baseline, template and component choices, a forward-model ratio-field fit gives 0.19-0.72, and injection-recovery shows the method is nearly unbiased only when its assumptions hold. The matched-beam S aperture (0.357) is dominated (55-70%) by non-core gas, and p0012 own components under-predict it by 0.03-0.09 (HCN). Using any ladder vector inside the allowed range, S has Tk 25-80 K and 80/100 K are disfavoured at only dchi2 1.4-6.5 / 4.5-8.2; the hot exclusion and S<50 K are not robust. What survives only as an uncorrected image-plane contrast (downgraded by Q19, see below) is T43/T32 N/S = 1.26+-0.09 (HCN, 2.9 sigma) and 1.16+-0.08 (HCO+, 2.0 sigma) in the matched 5.7x3.5" beam, which is NOT significant after differential Xb47/Xb4f recovery (HCN 1.10 [0.93,1.25], HCO+ 1.06 [0.93,1.18]), N distinct from the Bridge (1.25+-0.13) while S is not distinguishable from the Bridge (0.99+-0.11, 0.98+-0.07). The contrast corresponds to Tk_N/Tk_S >~1 (median 1.3-1.6) or n_N/n_S up to ~3 along the Tk-n degeneracy, neither significant; p0011 and p0012 do not conflict (p0011 used circular 6.5/10" apertures that mix N and S, p0012 deblended). Absolute Tk: N 65-150 K, S and Bridge 25-100 K (one-zone, Tbg 2.7-5 K). Q5 (shock/chemistry): no shock-chemistry signature is established in the nuclei; the only shock-tracer detection is cold CH3OH off the nuclei. CS 7-6 (n_crit ~ 5e6) is detected at N (15 sigma), S (6.5 sigma after correcting the -0.13 Jy/beam km/s baseline offset; 5.5 raw) and Bridge (9 sigma) in the 4.3x2.8" beam; CS 7-6/HCN 4-3 (K) is ~0.16 at N, 0.14-0.18 at S and 0.14-0.22 at the Bridge, equal within 20-25% (N/S 0.9-1.2+-0.2 after deblending N and S in a common beam), so there is no CS excess at the AGN-hosting S nucleus; CS/HCO+ 4-3 is 1.4+-0.25 times higher at N than at S (not significant). The team-a CS/HCO+ N~S (0.051/0.056) is the J=3-2/6.5"-aperture version of the same data, not a contradiction. The abundance ratio N(CS)/N(HCN) (0.2-0.7 in RADEX, factor 3 from the (Tk, n) degeneracy, HCN opacity changes it by only 15%) is not independently constrained and is not offered as a result. SO 8_8-7_7 is not detected (SO/HCO+ 4-3 < 0.011 N, < 0.014 S, < 0.013 Bridge, 3 sigma); SO 6_5-5_4 (251.826) is at best a 3-5 sigma, CH3OH-blended feature at S/Bridge, not S-specific; SO2, 34SO, SiS, NS undetected; SiO is outside the coverage. Against Harada+2018 (the only published chemistry; Band 3/6, 1.7"): our HCO+/HCN 3-2 reproduce theirs within 5-9% at N and 14-24% at S, our SO limits are consistent with their N SO 219.949/HCO+ = 0.026 for Tex<~25 K, and CH3OH/HCO+ (254.015) is 2-7x higher off the nuclei (Bridge 0.041+-0.004, W 0.071+-0.014, Sblue 0.068+-0.029) than at N (<0.022) and S (0.011+-0.006), the same sense as Harada's CH3OH enhancement at OS (8.6x in 96.7/HCO+ 1-0), TSW, SW and C; SiO, their strongest outflow tracer, is not covered. CH3OH is therefore cold (Trot<~11 K, Q12) and extended - weak shocks or non-thermal desorption - and a hot, nuclear shock chemistry is not seen. A compact (<0.5") SO/CH3OH-rich core is not excluded (Xb4b limits 0.03-0.07). Q19: the N>S ladder contrast (HCN T43/T32 N/S 1.26 raw, 1.24 after ramp) is reproduced by team-a p0022 but its removal by differential Xb47/Xb4f recovery rests on assumptions: true N/S lies between 0.97 and 1.24 depending on the recovery scenario (our priors 1.22; line-beam continuum anchor 1.0-1.07; team-a model 0.97) and is not established either way; no N-S excitation difference is claimed, none is excluded.
caveats: Formal errors are supplemented by an empirical baseline term (template slid over line-free channels) and spatial field scatter for tentative lines; flux-scale (5% B6, 10% B5/B7) and a Gaussian primary-beam term (5-10% for pb<0.9; NOTE Q12: Xb4f, Xb47 and Xb55 are 7-m ACA data with PB FWHM 39/30/58", so the 12-m 1.13 lambda/D FWHM originally assumed is wrong for them; gains in out/q12 pb table) are added only in the sig_cal column and in the text of the budgeted entries; absolute pb accuracy at E1/E2/W was not measured.

Single-Gaussian parameters (centroid, FWHM) are INVALID where chi2r>>1 (N and S at all resolutions: double-horned/two-component profiles, chi2r 2-20): such rows are flagged in the report; use the integrated intensity (template/sum) or the 2G components.

A single systemic velocity is not applicable: N 2792+-19, S 2721+-21 km/s (N-S offset +71+-28), midpoint ~2756; the 2780 km/s of round 1 is the blended low-resolution centre. Weak-line templates/windows are per region.

Wings and the Sblue structure are real in two independent arrays (Xb4d, Xb4b convolved) but lie outside the clean mask. Single flux-scale convention (Q2r2): residual-included image fluxes with a measured imaging spread (+-5-8% Xb4d; Xb4b 0.5 of Xb4d for HCN, 0.8 for HCO+) and a synthetic-uv bias bound epsilon=0.73-0.95, adopted systematic +25%/-10%; they are NOT lower limits and the earlier sidelobe/missing-flux term of <=0.01-0.02 Jy/beam km/s is superseded. The Xb4b HCN test has no power against sidelobes on its own.

SO 5_6-4_5 (blended with the CH3OH A-type ladder, flux an upper limit) and HC3N 28-27 are unconfirmed; the 254 GHz feature is CH3OH 2(0)-1(-1)E (identified by velocity, round 4); single-beam (Xb4f) significance of SO/HC3N drops from 5.0/3.8 sigma to 2.8/2.0 sigma against the spatial scatter, and the non-detection at 1" and 0.25" is non-diagnostic because beam dilution of a smooth source would put the signal below the limits.

Continuum: 0.24" and 0.94" arrays resolve out extended flux (48%/68% of the 5.8" flux at B6), so comparisons of flux or alpha across OUS must use matched beams and are image-plane only; the defensible alpha(B5-B7)=1.5+-0.2 (+-0.5 systematic).

Line IDs from Splatalogue rest frequencies; blends with separation < line width (HCN v2=1, CS/H2CS/29SiO, CH3OH J=1-3, H13CN/CO) are degenerate; H13CN is only bounded (Q4): HCN/H13CN(4-3) > 8 (N), > 4 (S), conditional on the assumed CO-wing family; a 12/13 ratio or opacity measurement is not possible.
Distance 40 Mpc (literature) is assumed for pc conversions; literature outflow geometry (Michiyama+2018, Pereira-Santaella+2024) is quoted from abstracts only.

Literature: Michiyama+2018 (arXiv:1810.04821) abstract verified via arXiv API (outflow from S nucleus; N no detection); distance 40 Mpc (Pereira-Santaella+2024) and Nishimura+2024 were taken from earlier notes and not re-verified; the HOC+ literature ratios (Harada+2018 2018ApJ...855...49H, Usero+2004) could NOT be verified and were removed. CH3OH excitation is model dependent (blend degenerate; 30% window/template systematic).

CH3OH is the only weak molecule with an off-nuclear signature: the 254.015 GHz line is detected at the Bridge in Xb4d (9.9 sigma matched filter, 3.4 sigma fixed-window moment) and absent at the N and S nuclei (Xb4d 3 sigma UL 0.12 Jy/beam km/s); line identification by velocity is relative to HCO+ 3-2 in the same pixel with a 10 km/s systematic floor, one transition only. The 254/J=1-3 ratio gives LTE Tex 8-21 K (S), thin, same filling assumed.

Q1r2: Disk HCN/HCO+ is measurable only at J=2-1 (Xb55) out to ~12" (PB model >=0.5, annulus flux positive); the zero level of every array is not flat (positive far field, negative 17-24" ring), so the 8-12" ratio has a ~+-0.1 systematic; 3-2 and 4-3 disk ratios are unconstrained (degenerate between missing short spacings and low excitation).

Q1r2: The zone-template deblend still has chi2_red 9-99 and a 15-25% S-vs-N model bias in injection; Ext zone is unconstrained; N and S values at 10" are model-dependent and S/N=0.7+-0.2 should not be sharpened. The T_b ladder ratios r21~1.6-2.2 (>1) mix cross-band flux scales (10-35%) with possible missing 3-2 flux and are not thermometers without Q3 modelling.

Q1r2: Sblue wing: R_wing>R_core is robust in Xb4d but the Xb4b-smoothed replication (0.86+-0.25; HCN wing only 53% recovered) does not confirm R>1; window choice (-350..-100) gives 1.0; weak neighbouring lines (HDO, c-C3H, CH3OH) lie in the HCN window and are not excluded.

Q4: H13CN limits depend on the CO 3-2 wing model family (alpha shifts by ~0.05 between families; fits including the CO core fail with chi2_red 2-13); H13CN, H13CO+ and HNC at the N-core beam (<0.5") are not in the data, so the core opacity is not measured. Equal-Tex/equal-filling and 12C/13C=30-100 are assumed.

Q4: The HCN v2=1f limits exclude strong pumping only (LTE Tvib < 270-360 K); the J=3-2 1f line is covered only from -250 to +175 km/s and sits on the HCO+ red wing; the 4-8% HCN core broadening, the R(v) pattern in the N core (chi2 25/4) and the RADEX thresholds (A~4, N(HCN)>~5e16) are tentative/model-dependent.

Q4r2: The width-ratio null test uses the aperture-averaged Gaussian FWHM (chi2_red 4-6, line profiles are not Gaussian) and the empirical scatter over positions, which includes real profile differences; it shows the core ratio is not an outlier, not that opacity is absent. The spatial-weights model uses the observed smoothed R map and assumes identical local profiles.

Q4r2: The T_b analysis is one RADEX zone per line with a shared filling factor; two-phase gas (hot compact thick HCN + diffuse HCO+) or different filling for the two lines is not covered; fractions of allowed cells are grid weights, not posteriors; T_b are observed-frame RJ values with a 10% flux scale. H13CN/H13CO+ at the core beam are not in the data.

Q4r2: H13CN injection simulations use noise from the line-free spectrum (no CO-wing structure in the noise) and a wing truth taken from the real fit; alpha grid step 0.02; limits assume the HCN 4-3 profile as the H13CN template and equal Tex/filling. The thin 12C/13C=30-100 regime is below the sensitivity. The thick-core band assumes the 6.5" L=Tb(4-3)/Tb(3-2) for the beam average and RADEX L_c for the core.

Q3: The 10" ladder fits have 6 data for 5 parameters (1 dof); posteriors are prior- and grid-weighted (flat in log n, Tk, N, A; 0.25 dex grid; 11 Tk values), so quoted intervals are marginals, not confidence regions, and at the grid edge (Tk 112 [56,112]) the upper end is the grid step.

Q3: Band 5/6/7 flux scales (10-35%) and the missing flux of the compact Band 5/7 observations (extended disk emission) directly set the n,Tk results; there is no overlapping line to calibrate the bands against each other (Xb4f vs Xb47/Xb55 was not testable). The disk 4-3 low-S/N and Band 7 short-baseline coverage are the main risks for the disk contrast.

Q3: Single-zone, one filling factor for both molecules and all J, 150 km/s reference width, LVG sphere: different filling of HCN and HCO+, a hot compact component (Q4: N core T_b ratio ~1) and velocity-resolved ratios are not modelled; plane-parallel geometry lowers n by ~0.5 dex. The cold dense (10 K, >1e7) islands in the posterior are low-weight but not excluded. N(H2) needs an abundance assumption (X(HCO+)=1e-9 used for scale only).

Q3: At 10" the N and S apertures are 5" apart and share most of their beam; the 'zone' deblend (s37) has chi2_red 9-99, so zone-level N vs S differences have 30-70% errors. H13CN limits (Q4) are beam-average and only exclude tau(HCN 4-3)>~4-13. Confirmation requires matched-beam H13CN/H13CO+ and J=2-1 at <3" or CO ladders for the kinetic temperature.

Q12: absolute losses of every array are not measurable without total-power/short-spacing data (cleaned-image integrals equal the clean-component flux, not zero); simulated ACA losses at r<8" are 10-30% for plausible skies but depend on assumed uv coverage, sky and clean parameters. MRS ratios (0.30 [0.20,0.45]) are nominal. The loss-only extrapolation to Xb55/Xb47 is conditional on its priors and the forward model does not reproduce its ordering. Clump fluxes depend on the assumed Gaussian clump shape (FWHM 1.5-4"), the halo decomposition and, for E2 and the HCN clumps, are not constrained (blending with the S halo; clumps below 3 sigma). The Xb47 field (+-25") ends before its bowl closes.

Q3r4: single-zone RADEX with one eta per position; the 10" ladders are beam averages of compact cores plus a shared smooth component (cores hold 14-38% of the HCN 3-2 flux), so n, Tk, A are not nuclear values; the grid is converged at 0.1 dex in N and A (0.2 dex changes the lower Tk edge); N-S-Bridge posteriors are identical by construction; the joint centre fit uses a product-of-marginals truncation of the per-position eta; J=1-0 intensities are literature values at 1.7" with different uv coverage; Brunetti+2021 pressures, cloud sigma and CO brightness temperatures are quoted from the review and were not re-checked; E2 and W are prior-dominated.

Q11: the Soutflow HCN excess (outer blue window) is a 6.2-sigma, one-beam, uncleaned (outside the Xb4d clean mask) lobe 1.8" S of S, one-sided (red mirror empty), present at one ring azimuth only; not an azimuthal artefact, not confirmed at the same significance in Xb4b (1.0 sigma, 2.0 sigma lower HCN; Xb4b noise 1.6-2x higher). Residual-image flux scale (JvM epsilon) is a systematic. Its nature (HCN-rich wing gas vs lobe-specific HDO blend) is undecided: CH3CHO/c-C3H/l-C3H carriers are excluded (<=1-9% of E), HDO cannot be tested with companion lines in the band (needs N(HDO)>=3e14 cm-2). The earlier 'blue-half ratio 1.3-1.4' is frame dependent (1.04-1.68). The s70 Gaussian fit (centre pinned at -150, FWHM 430) is withdrawn (descending-axis interpolation bug); corrected fit centre -277+-13, FWHM 230+-32 km/s. N wing limit <~3% of the core, baseline-limited. Red-side HCN feature on the Bridge (3-4 sigma) is a hint only.

Q2r2: the flux scale of the residual-dominated wing is +25%/-10% (cross-imaging spread of Xb4d/tapered/manual cubes and a synthetic-uv epsilon of 0.73-0.95 whose sign/size depends on the unknown uv coverage; Xb4b gives half the HCN flux); 'lower limit' is no longer claimed. The non-LTE dense mass is a single-zone model that does not reproduce the HCN 3-2/1-0 ratio (HCN IR pumping, two phases, or HCN overabundance not modelled), is dominated by the unknown abundance (X 1e-9..1e-8, factor 10), by the density (1e5 vs 1e6) and by a clump-column degeneracy (capped at 3e23 cm-2); the 1-0 fluxes are Michiyama's (different aperture/beam, +-30%). Mdot depends on i (70-85 deg; i from the line of sight, flow near the plane of the sky), v (broad |v| 134 vs wing 283 km/s), R and the formula (x3): 1.5 dex, and is not a steady-state measurement. Gaussian decompositions: HCN and HCO+ require different kinematics and HDO vs HCN-rich gas is not decided. The null test uses pixels >5 sigma at 0.25 arcsec and thus misses faint extended emission, but an analytic bound (>=340 km/s/arcsec) gives the same conclusion; the nuclear wings are not separable from rotation. The red feature's origin (S counter-lobe, N outflow, Bridge) is open. Confirmation needs the 1-0/2-1 lines of the lobe at matched resolution (HCN 2-1 with Xb55 is too coarse), HCN v2=1 / H13CN to test pumping and opacity, and CO at 0.2-0.5" for a window-matched dense fraction. Mass and Mdot must be quoted as brackets: M=7.8e6(1e-8/X) Msun (0.8-2.6e7 CO-capped; model fails HCN 3-2/1-0; 1.4e7 is not an independent point value) and Mdot ~15-60 Msun/yr for i=70-85 (3-2000 whole grid; 30 Msun/yr is a central case of a scaling M v tan i/R). Mass includes |v|<150 km/s gas of uncertain outflow nature.

Q16: aperture ladders are not core ladders (the S aperture contains Bridge-like gas and the outflow lobe, 55-70% non-core flux); the S Tk range 25-100 K spans the p0012 core vector, the aperture and the contaminant-subtracted vectors. p0012 deblend script is not in the snapshot, so its exact recipe was not re-run (our re-implementation reproduces it only in part and unstably). Different spatial filtering of Xb47 and Xb4f (Q12: T43/T32 true/obs 1.03-1.12) is applied only as a variant. Moment-0 maps carry negative bowls and an off-source rms 2.5-4x the formal noise; the T grid is coarse (15-30% above 40 K). One-zone RADEX, Tbg blackbody (Tbg 10 K disfavoured, 5 K tested), no IR pumping (HCN 3-2/1-0 failure from Q3/Q4), CO and Tdust not measured. A resolved J=4 (or 2-1) map at ~1" would settle the S core ladder; the archive has none.

Q5: CS 7-6 is a blend with H2CS 10-9 and 29SiO 8-7 that cannot be separated at these widths (CS 68-100% of the quoted W at N from the data alone; 85-100% with assumed abundances; S/Bridge unconstrained by the data); the CS baseline carries a -0.13 Jy/beam km/s on-source offset systematic (corrected here, +-0.13 kept as systematic; the spw spans only +-800 km/s so no on-source line-free test is possible); the S CS detection is 6.5 sigma in the matched-filter aperture but only 2.7 sigma in a single-pixel box moment; SiO and the 219.949 GHz SO line are not covered; the only SO hint (S, Xb4f) rests on one line, is not >5 sigma after the offset correction (4.6 sigma SO-only, 3.3 with the CH3OH ladder) and is not S-specific; Xb47 apertures mix N and S (5.2" apart, 4.3x2.8" beam) so CS/SO ratios are region averages (deblended N/S ratios are model dependent at the 20% level); Harada+2018 has no Band 7 data and uses different SO/CH3OH transitions (LTE extrapolation, factor 2-5 uncertain), its OS position is not tabulated so Sblue=OS is an identification, not a measurement; N(CS)/N(HCN) is not constrained beyond 0.2-0.7.

Q20: the Band 7 data (4.1x2.7" beam) cannot isolate the ridge from N (1.9") and S (3.3"): the 4-3 ridge signal is extracted by a template fit assuming the 4-3 excess has the spatial shape of the 3-2 excess (an assumption that biases s if the 4-3 emitting region is more extended), with a free core-wing coefficient (negative for HCN 4-3, -0.03, probably continuum/self-absorption at the nuclei, so the nuclear red wing is not modelled physically) and errors of 35-45%; the ~3 sigma significance is formal (effective dof from beam area, shifted-template null). The HCO+ 4-3 ridge excess is above the thermal limit (r43/32 1.3, 1 sigma). CS 7-6, SO, HC3N and H13CN limits are 9-70x above the core line ratios and cannot test the ridge or the origin; H13CN has no mirrored window and sits on the CO 3-2 wing. 1-0 flux scale unverified (Q17) so no r31 argument is used.

Q9: the CH3OH J=1-3 blend integral has a baseline systematic of a factor 2-4 (red wing/spw-edge ramp), not the +-30% quoted earlier; earlier results using blend 0.97/1.38 (N/S) and Trot 8-21 K remain valid within this range but Trot is only 6-18 K at S, >7 K at the Bridge. Region assignment in Xb55 is impossible (one 9" beam).

Q22: the Xb55 spw22 low-edge negative ramp (-0.16 to -0.21 x continuum) is a continuum-proportional edge residual; with it modelled the CH3OH blend baseline systematic is +-14-35% (range factor 1.3-2.2, not 2-4) and Trot at S ~13 (10-20) K; the Q9 factor 2-4 statement applies to naive constant/linear baselines in +-400 km/s windows. Not verifiable without the uv data.

Q23: the low-frequency-edge (RED-side) ramp is real in Xb55 spw18, Xb4f spw18 and Xb47 spw16 and persists as a plateau of ~-0.07..-0.10 x continuum to the window start, so it lowers the HCN 4-3 integral by ~3-10% (HCN 3-2 <=3%, HCO+ 2-1 <=1.4%); HCN/HCO+ 4-3 and HCN T43/T32 in earlier tables are biased low by up to ~10% and ~6% (<1 sigma). The N/S contrast is unchanged. Extent of the ramp under the red wing (+250..+350 km/s) is unconstrained by the data.

Q6: the 0.24" sizes are half-max (compact-core) sizes: both nuclei have a 1.5-2" pedestal, single Gaussians are box-dependent, the Bridge and E1 are blended/elongated, and S/N<10 entries (Sblue, W, HCN E1) are tentative; HCN is more compact than HCO+ at N (0.41 vs 0.52"); the S continuum (0.23", ~45 pc) is only marginally resolved. Line widths at N are non-Gaussian (half-max 111 vs 1G 132 km/s) and unaffected by beam smearing (<=16 km/s); clump widths (23-28 km/s) match the CO GMC sigma of Brunetti+2022 while the nuclei are 2-3x broader. T_b of 2-3 K RJ (5-7 K Planck-equivalent) means the 3-2 emission is sub-thermal or fills <~10% of the beam; filling and excitation cannot be separated without a second transition at 0.25" (none exists in these data). Distance 40 Mpc (Sakamoto+2014 use 35 Mpc: pc values scale by 0.88). No spectral ramp affects Xb4b spw25/27 (Q23).

Q6r2: peak T_b of the dense gas falls 3-8x between 49 and 250 pc (slope -0.7..-1.2), so beam filling at 50 pc cannot be taken from a single Gaussian-dilution factor and the gas is not a smooth medium; N has no well-defined core+pedestal decomposition and its size is imaging dependent (half-max 0.52" regular vs 0.36" manual cube); virial masses depend by a factor ~2 on the R/sigma convention and are upper limits.

Q27: eta is a fit nuisance with flat-ln prior; p0026's floors treat the 0.24" peak T_b (channel peak, observed frame, 150 km/s width assumed) as a lower limit on the intrinsic T_R of ALL gas in the 10" beam (49-pc floor = bounding scenario, because 56-72% of the 10" 3-2 flux is smooth gas) and compare it with RADEX line-centre T_R at dv=150 km/s. Posterior n and the Tk upper edge depend on the prior (flat log n vs flat n). eta=1 is statistically allowed (chi2 1.3 for 6 data, ~4 free params) so dilution vs sub-thermal excitation remains degenerate at 10". The 6.5" matched ladder could not be refit with J=2-1 (Xb55 beam 8.6x6.0"). p0012's 1" S Tkin 20-30 K constraint is not re-tested.
